units.title: Group weighted fine increments by coarse dyadic cells
units.statement: Fix a positive horizon and nested regular dyadic grids at levels m and n with m≤n. Assign each coarse cell a real weight and each fine cell a real value. The fine sum weighted by the enclosing coarse cell equals the weighted sum of consecutive differences of the fine prefix sums at coarse grid points.
assumptions: The grids are regular dyadic grids of the same positive horizon T. The fine grid refines the coarse grid.
Each wⱼ and zᵢ is an arbitrary real number. The prefix includes the cell ending exactly at its cutoff.

steps.title: Locate the enclosing cell
steps.text: Each fine cell lies inside a unique coarse cell. Its fine right endpoint lies at or before coarse node sₖ exactly when its enclosing coarse cell has index smaller than k.
steps.lean:
private theorem fine_right_le_coarse_point_iff
    {T : ℝ≥0} (hT : 0 < T) {m n : ℕ} (hmn : m ≤ n)
    (k : Fin (2 ^ m + 1)) (i : Fin (2 ^ n)) :
    regularGridTimes (dyadicMesh T n) (2 ^ n) i.succ ≤
      regularGridTimes (dyadicMesh T m) (2 ^ m) k ↔
    (coarseCell hmn i).val < k.val := by
  let j := coarseCell hmn i
  let s := regularGridTimes (dyadicMesh T m) (2 ^ m)
  let t := regularGridTimes (dyadicMesh T n) (2 ^ n)
  have hs := regularGridTimes_strictMono (dyadicMesh_pos hT m) (2 ^ m)
  have ht := regularGridTimes_strictMono (dyadicMesh_pos hT n) (2 ^ n)
  change t i.succ ≤ s k ↔ j.val < k.val
  constructor
  · intro h
    by_contra! hkj
    have hkl : k ≤ j.castSucc := hkj
    have hleft := (hs.monotone hkl).trans (coarse_left_endpoint_le_fine_left (T := T) hmn i)
    exact (not_le.mpr (hleft.trans_lt (ht Fin.castSucc_lt_succ))) h
  · intro hjk
    have hkr : j.succ ≤ k := Nat.succ_le_iff.2 hjk
    exact (fine_right_endpoint_le_coarse_right (T := T) hmn i).trans (hs.monotone hkr)

steps.title: Subtract the two inclusive prefixes
steps.text: The difference selects exactly the fine cells enclosed by the jth coarse cell. Interchanging the finite sums gives the displayed identity.
steps.lean:
theorem dyadic_sum_coarse_weight_eq_prefix_differences
    {T : ℝ≥0} (hT : 0 < T) {m n : ℕ} (hmn : m ≤ n)
    (w : Fin (2 ^ m) → ℝ) (z : Fin (2 ^ n) → ℝ) :
    let s := regularGridTimes (dyadicMesh T m) (2 ^ m)
    let t := regularGridTimes (dyadicMesh T n) (2 ^ n)
    let P := fun k => ∑ i : Fin (2 ^ n), if t i.succ ≤ s k then z i else 0
    (∑ i : Fin (2 ^ n), w (coarseCell hmn i) * z i) =
      ∑ j : Fin (2 ^ m), w j * (P j.succ - P j.castSucc) := by
  intro s t P
  have hcell (i : Fin (2 ^ n)) (j : Fin (2 ^ m)) :
      (if t i.succ ≤ s j.succ then z i else 0) -
        (if t i.succ ≤ s j.castSucc then z i else 0) =
      if coarseCell hmn i = j then z i else 0 := by
    change (if regularGridTimes (dyadicMesh T n) (2 ^ n) i.succ ≤
        regularGridTimes (dyadicMesh T m) (2 ^ m) j.succ then z i else 0) -
      (if regularGridTimes (dyadicMesh T n) (2 ^ n) i.succ ≤
        regularGridTimes (dyadicMesh T m) (2 ^ m) j.castSucc then z i else 0) = _
    simp only [fine_right_le_coarse_point_iff hT hmn, Fin.val_succ, Fin.val_castSucc]
    rcases lt_trichotomy (coarseCell hmn i).val j.val with h | h | h
    · have hne : coarseCell hmn i ≠ j := fun he => h.ne (congrArg Fin.val he)
      simp only [if_pos h, if_pos (h.trans (Nat.lt_succ_self _)), if_neg hne, sub_self]
    · have he : coarseCell hmn i = j := Fin.ext h
      simp [he]
    · have hne : coarseCell hmn i ≠ j := fun he => h.ne (congrArg Fin.val he).symm
      simp only [if_neg (not_lt.mpr (Nat.succ_le_iff.2 h)), if_neg (not_lt.mpr h.le),
        if_neg hne, sub_self]
  calc
    _ = ∑ i : Fin (2 ^ n), ∑ j : Fin (2 ^ m),
        w j * (if coarseCell hmn i = j then z i else 0) := by
      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
      intro i _
      rw [Finset.sum_eq_single (coarseCell hmn i)]
      · simp
      · intro j _ hj
        simp [Ne.symm hj]
      · simp
    _ = _ := by
      rw [Finset.sum_comm]
      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
      intro j _
      simp only [P, ← Finset.sum_sub_distrib, Finset.mul_sum, hcell]

units.lean_statement: Both grids are represented by finite indices. For each fine cell i, coarseCell gives the index c(i).
units.lean_proof: Subtract the two prefix indicators cell by cell and exchange the finite sums.
units.boundary: This identity concerns weights constant within each coarse cell. The continuous-weight approximation is a separate result.

units.title: One almost-everywhere subsequence for countably many limits in measure
units.statement: Suppose a countable family of sequences into a pseudo extended metric space each converges in measure. A single strictly increasing subsequence makes every sequence in the family converge to its stated limit almost everywhere on the same event.
units.formula: \exists\,k:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N\ \text{strictly increasing},\qquad \mu\text{-a.e. } \omega,\ \forall i,\quad F_{i,k(n)}(\omega)\to G_i(\omega).
assumptions: The family index type is countable and the sample space carries a measure. The codomain is a pseudo extended metric space.
For each family member, its sequence converges in measure to the specified limit, defined through the measure of each positive extended-distance error event.

steps.title: Choose one index for each tolerance
steps.text: Encode the countable family into natural numbers. For each sequence, the usual geometric error thresholds can be chosen nondecreasing in n. The maximum over codes at most n is then nondecreasing as both the thresholds and the set of codes grow. Adding n makes the selected indices strictly increasing.
steps.lean:
let _ : Encodable I := Encodable.ofCountable I
  let pick (j n : ℕ) := ((Encodable.decode j : Option I).map
    (fun i => ExistsSeqTendstoAe.seqTendstoAeSeq (h i) n)).getD 0
  let bound (n : ℕ) := (Finset.range (n + 1)).sup (fun j => pick j n)
  let k (n : ℕ) := n + bound n
  have hPick (j : ℕ) : Monotone (pick j) := by
    intro m n hmn
    cases hj : (Encodable.decode j : Option I) with
    | none => simp [pick, hj]
    | some i =>
      simpa [pick, hj] using (ExistsSeqTendstoAe.seqTendstoAeSeq_strictMono (h i)).monotone hmn
  have hBound : Monotone bound := by
    intro m n hmn
    apply Finset.sup_le_iff.2
    intro j hj
    exact (hPick j hmn).trans
      (Finset.le_sup (f := fun j => pick j n) (Finset.range_mono (Nat.succ_le_succ hmn) hj))
  have hk : StrictMono k := fun _ _ hmn => Nat.add_lt_add_of_lt_of_le hmn (hBound hmn.le)

steps.title: Intersect the almost-everywhere conclusions
steps.text: For any fixed family member, the error-event measures are summable from the stage at which its code first appears. Borel–Cantelli gives the limit almost everywhere. Intersect over the countable family.
steps.lean:
refine ⟨k, hk, ae_all_iff.2 ?_⟩
  intro i
  let S (n : ℕ) : Set Ω := if Encodable.encode i ≤ n then
    {ω | (2 : ℝ≥0∞)⁻¹ ^ n ≤ edist (F i (k n) ω) (G i ω)} else ∅
  have hMeasure (n : ℕ) : μ (S n) ≤ (2 : ℝ≥0∞)⁻¹ ^ n := by
    by_cases hn : Encodable.encode i ≤ n
    · have hp : pick (Encodable.encode i) n ≤ bound n :=
        Finset.le_sup (f := fun j => pick j n) (Finset.mem_range.2 (Nat.lt_succ_of_le hn))
      have hIndex : ExistsSeqTendstoAe.seqTendstoAeSeq (h i) n ≤ k n :=
        (by simpa [pick] using hp : _ ≤ bound n).trans (Nat.le_add_left _ _)
      simpa [S, hn] using ExistsSeqTendstoAe.seqTendstoAeSeq_spec (h i) n (k n) hIndex
    · simp [S, hn]
  have hFinite : (∑' n, μ (S n)) ≠ ∞ := by
    refine ne_top_of_le_ne_top ?_ (ENNReal.tsum_le_tsum hMeasure)
    simpa only [ENNReal.tsum_geometric, ENNReal.one_sub_inv_two, inv_inv] using ENNReal.ofNat_ne_top
  filter_upwards [ae_eventually_notMem hFinite] with ω hω
  refine EMetric.tendsto_atTop.mpr fun ε hε => eventually_atTop.1 ?_
  have hSmall : ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, (2 : ℝ≥0∞)⁻¹ ^ n < ε :=
    (ENNReal.tendsto_pow_atTop_nhds_zero_of_lt_one (by norm_num)).eventually_lt_const hε
  filter_upwards [hω, hSmall, eventually_ge_atTop (Encodable.encode i)] with n hn hs hi
  have hErr : edist (F i (k n) ω) (G i ω) < (2 : ℝ≥0∞)⁻¹ ^ n := by
    simpa [S, hi] using hn
  exact hErr.trans hs

units.lean_statement: The theorem uses an arbitrary measure and the same samplewise event for all countably many limits.
units.lean_proof: Use a monotone finite maximum of Mathlib's geometric thresholds, apply Borel–Cantelli separately to each member, then take a countable intersection.
units.boundary: The conclusion is along a single subsequence. Uniform convergence over the family and convergence along the full sequence require separate conditions.

units.title: Continuous weights from dyadic prefix limits
units.statement: Suppose signed cell masses along a cofinal sequence of dyadic levels have uniformly bounded total absolute mass. If their prefix sums at each fixed dyadic node converge to the prefix integral of an integrable time density, the left-endpoint sum against any continuous weight converges to the integral of the weighted density.
assumptions: The horizon T is positive and the sequence of fine levels tends to infinity.
The real weight w is continuous on [0,T], and the real density b is integrable against the horizon time measure.
The total absolute cell mass is uniformly bounded along the specified sequence. For every fixed dyadic node, the inclusive fine prefix converges to the integral primitive of b at that node.

steps.title: Freeze the weights on a coarse grid
steps.text: Hold the coarse level m fixed. Once the fine level σ(n) is at least m, use the coarse left-endpoint weight for every fine cell it contains. The block identity and the prefix hypotheses give the limit as a finite sum of weighted primitive differences.
steps.lean:
intro t hPrefix
  obtain ⟨M, hM⟩ := hVar
  let C := max M 1
  have hC : 0 < C := zero_lt_one.trans_le (le_max_right _ _)
  let P (m : ℕ) (k : Fin (2 ^ m + 1)) (n : ℕ) :=
    ∑ i : Fin (2 ^ σ n), if t (σ n) i.succ ≤ t m k then z (σ n) i else 0
  let L (m : ℕ) := ∑ j : Fin (2 ^ m), w (t m j.castSucc) *
    (prefixIntegral b T (t m j.succ) - prefixIntegral b T (t m j.castSucc))
  let V (m n : ℕ) := ∑ j : Fin (2 ^ m), w (t m j.castSucc) *
    (P m j.succ n - P m j.castSucc n)
  let S (n : ℕ) := ∑ i : Fin (2 ^ σ n), w (t (σ n) i.castSucc) * z (σ n) i
  let I := ∫ s, w s * b s ∂(TimeMeasure.upTo T)
  have hV (m : ℕ) : Tendsto (V m) atTop (𝓝 (L m)) := by
    refine tendsto_finsetSum _ fun j _ => ?_
    exact ((hPrefix m j.succ).sub (hPrefix m j.castSucc)).const_mul _

steps.title: Bound the freezing error
steps.text: For these refining fine levels, each fine left endpoint and its coarse left endpoint are in the same coarse cell. Uniform continuity on [0,T] bounds the difference of the two weights. Multiply that bound by the uniform bound on total absolute mass.
steps.lean:
let δ := ε / (3 * C)
  have hδ : 0 < δ := div_pos hε (by positivity)
  obtain ⟨r, hr, hwmod⟩ :=
    (Metric.uniformContinuousOn_iff.1 (isCompact_Icc.uniformContinuousOn_of_continuous hw)) δ hδ
  have hChoice : ∀ᶠ m : ℕ in atTop,
      (dyadicMesh T m : ℝ) < r ∧ dist (L m) I < ε / 3 :=
    (eventually_dyadicMesh_lt T hr).and ((Metric.tendsto_nhds.1 hL) _ (by positivity))
  obtain ⟨m, hmMesh, hmL⟩ := hChoice.exists
  filter_upwards [hσ.eventually (eventually_ge_atTop m),
    (Metric.tendsto_nhds.1 (hV m)) (ε / 3) (by positivity)] with n hn hmV
  have hBlock : V m n = ∑ i : Fin (2 ^ σ n),
      w (t m (coarseCell hn i).castSucc) * z (σ n) i :=
    (dyadic_sum_coarse_weight_eq_prefix_differences hT hn
      (fun j => w (t m j.castSucc)) (z (σ n))).symm
  have hOsc (i : Fin (2 ^ σ n)) :
      |w (t (σ n) i.castSucc) - w (t m (coarseCell hn i).castSucc)| ≤ δ := by
    let j := coarseCell hn i
    let x := t (σ n) i.castSucc
    let y := t m j.castSucc
    have hyx : y ≤ x := coarse_left_endpoint_le_fine_left (T := T) hn i
    have hfine : t (σ n) i.castSucc ≤ t (σ n) i.succ :=
      (regularGridTimes_strictMono (dyadicMesh_pos hT (σ n)) _).monotone (Fin.castSucc_le_succ i)
    have hxy : x ≤ y + dyadicMesh T m := by
      exact (hfine.trans (fine_right_endpoint_le_coarse_right (T := T) hn i)).trans_eq
        (dyadic_activeCell_right j)
    have hd : dist x y ≤ (dyadicMesh T m : ℝ) := by
      rw [NNReal.dist_eq, abs_of_nonneg (sub_nonneg.mpr (by exact_mod_cast hyx))]
      exact sub_le_iff_le_add.mpr (by exact_mod_cast (add_comm y (dyadicMesh T m) ▸ hxy))
    exact (Real.dist_eq .. ▸
      hwmod x ⟨bot_le, ht _ _⟩ y ⟨bot_le, ht _ _⟩ (hd.trans_lt hmMesh)).le
  have hApprox : dist (S n) (V m n) ≤ ε / 3 := by
    rw [Real.dist_eq, hBlock]
    dsimp only [S]
    rw [← Finset.sum_sub_distrib]
    calc
      _ ≤ ∑ i : Fin (2 ^ σ n), |w (t (σ n) i.castSucc) * z (σ n) i -
          w (t m (coarseCell hn i).castSucc) * z (σ n) i| :=
        Finset.abs_sum_le_sum_abs _ _
      _ ≤ ∑ i : Fin (2 ^ σ n), δ * |z (σ n) i| := by
        apply Finset.sum_le_sum
        intro i _
        rw [← sub_mul, abs_mul]
        exact mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right (hOsc i) (abs_nonneg _)
      _ ≤ δ * C := by
        rw [← Finset.mul_sum]
        exact mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left ((hM n).trans (le_max_left _ _)) hδ.le
      _ = ε / 3 := by
        dsimp only [δ]
        rw [← div_div, div_mul_cancel₀ _ hC.ne']

steps.title: Pass to the weighted integral
steps.text: The existing deterministic weighted time-sum theorem gives the limit of Lₘ. Choose m so both the freezing error and the error in Lₘ are small, then take the fine level sufficiently large.
steps.lean:
have hTriangle := (dist_triangle (S n) (V m n) I).trans
    (add_le_add (le_refl _) (dist_triangle (V m n) (L m) I))
  linarith

units.lean_statement: The fine levels are indexed by a map σ tending to infinity. The target prefix is the existing PrefixIntegral under TimeMeasure.upTo T.
units.lean_proof: Fix a coarse level chosen by uniform continuity and the existing time-sum limit. Then use eventual refinement and the finite combination of prefix limits.
units.boundary: The cell masses may be signed. Bounded total absolute mass along the sequence is the condition used to control the uniform weight error.

units.title: Continuous-weight covariation of two completed Itô rows
units.statement: Let X and Y be two real Itô rows driven by the same standard vector Brownian motion relative to the given filtration and measure. For an almost surely continuous real weight with measurable time slices, the left-endpoint weighted products of dyadic increments converge in measure to the time integral of the weight times the inner product of the diffusion coefficients.
assumptions: The horizon T is positive. The sample measure is finite, and the filtration satisfies the usual conditions. The coordinate set is finite with decidable equality.

Each row uses progressive square-integrable coefficients on the product of the sample measure and the horizon time measure. Its drift has almost-everywhere strongly measurable evaluations up to T and almost surely continuous finite-variation paths on [0,T].
At each fixed t≤T the weight W(t) is almost-everywhere strongly measurable. Almost every weight path is continuous on [0,T].

notation.text: Each real row uses the corresponding scalar stochastic integral against every coordinate of the same Brownian motion.

steps.title: Choose a common subsequence of actual limits
steps.text: On any subsequence, apply the countable selection theorem to all mixed prefix limits and the two terminal square-sum limits. This gives a further subsequence on which the limits hold together almost everywhere.
steps.lean:
have hPrefix (m : ℕ) (k : Fin (2 ^ m + 1)) :
      TendstoInMeasure μ (P m k) atTop (fun ω => prefixIntegral (b ω) T (t m k)) := by
    apply TendstoInMeasure.congr_right ?_
      (tendstoInMeasure_dyadic_prefix_mul_increments_of_ito_rows
        hB hT hUsual η ξ A C hAmeas hCmeas hA hC m k)
    filter_upwards [hProduct] with ω hω
    have hRestrict (j : J) : Integrable (fun s => (η j).process s ω * (ξ j).process s ω)
        ((TimeMeasure.upTo T).restrict (Iio (t m k))) := (hω j).integrableOn
    rw [prefixIntegral_eq_setIntegral, min_eq_left (ht m k)]
    change (∑ j : J, ∫ s in Iic (t m k),
      (η j).process s ω * (ξ j).process s ω ∂(TimeMeasure.upTo T)) =
      ∫ s in Iio (t m k), ∑ j : J, (η j).process s ω * (ξ j).process s ω ∂(TimeMeasure.upTo T)
    rw [integral_finsetSum _ (fun j _ => hRestrict j)]
    exact Finset.sum_congr rfl fun _ _ => setIntegral_congr_set (Iio_ae_eq_Iic' (by simp)).symm
  have hQX : TendstoInMeasure μ (Q X) atTop (E η) :=
    tendstoInMeasure_dyadic_prefix_sq_increments_of_ito_row hB hT hUsual η A hAmeas hA 0 (Fin.last _)
  have hQY : TendstoInMeasure μ (Q Y) atTop (E ξ) :=
    tendstoInMeasure_dyadic_prefix_sq_increments_of_ito_row hB hT hUsual ξ C hCmeas hC 0 (Fin.last _)
  have hI (r : J → ProgressiveL2Integrand filtration μ T) (s : ℝ≥0) :
      AEStronglyMeasurable (fun ω => ∑ j : J,
        itoIntegralProcess (r j) hT ((coordinateFamily hB).isBrownian j) hUsual s ω) μ :=
    (Finset.aestronglyMeasurable_sum Finset.univ fun j _ =>
      (((itoIntegralProcess_stronglyAdapted (r j) hT
        ((coordinateFamily hB).isBrownian j) hUsual) s).mono
          (filtration.le s)).aestronglyMeasurable).congr
      (Eventually.of_forall fun ω => by simp only [Finset.sum_apply])
  have hSm (n : ℕ) : AEStronglyMeasurable (S n) μ := by
    have hXm (s : ℝ≥0) (hs : s ≤ T) : AEStronglyMeasurable (X s) μ :=
      (hAmeas s hs).add (hI η s)
    have hYm (s : ℝ≥0) (hs : s ≤ T) : AEStronglyMeasurable (Y s) μ :=
      (hCmeas s hs).add (hI ξ s)
    have hCell (i : Fin (2 ^ n)) :
        AEStronglyMeasurable (fun ω => W (t n i.castSucc) ω * z ω n i) μ :=
      (hWmeas _ (ht n i.castSucc)).mul
        (((hXm _ (ht n i.succ)).sub (hXm _ (ht n i.castSucc))).mul
          ((hYm _ (ht n i.succ)).sub (hYm _ (ht n i.castSucc))))
    exact (Finset.aestronglyMeasurable_sum Finset.univ fun i _ => hCell i).congr
      (Eventually.of_forall fun ω => by simp only [S, Finset.sum_apply])
  let K := (Σ m : ℕ, Fin (2 ^ m + 1)) ⊕ Bool
  let F : K → ℕ → Ω → ℝ :=
    Sum.elim (fun k => P k.1 k.2) (fun side => if side then Q Y else Q X)
  let G : K → Ω → ℝ :=
    Sum.elim (fun k ω => prefixIntegral (b ω) T (t k.1 k.2))
      (fun side => if side then E ξ else E η)
  have hF : ∀ k, TendstoInMeasure μ (F k) atTop (G k) := by
    rintro (k | side)
    · exact hPrefix k.1 k.2
    · cases side
      · exact hQX
      · exact hQY
  change TendstoInMeasure μ S atTop (fun ω => ∫ s, W s ω * b ω s ∂(TimeMeasure.upTo T))
  refine (exists_seq_tendstoInMeasure_atTop_iff hSm).2 ?_
  intro u hu
  have hFamily (k : K) : TendstoInMeasure μ (F k ∘ u) atTop (G k) :=
    (hF k).comp hu.tendsto_atTop
  obtain ⟨v, hv, hPath⟩ := exists_seq_tendsto_ae_of_countable hFamily
  refine ⟨v, hv, ?_⟩
  filter_upwards [hPath, hProduct, hW] with ω hω hp hw
  let σ := u ∘ v
  have hσ : Tendsto σ atTop atTop := (hu.comp hv).tendsto_atTop

steps.title: Control the signed cell masses
steps.text: The absolute product of the two increments is bounded by half their squared sum. The two terminal limits bound this sum along the selected subsequence. The coefficient products have integrable time sections by product L² and Fubini.
steps.lean:
have hEnergy : Tendsto (fun n => (Q X (σ n) ω + Q Y (σ n) ω) / 2) atTop
      (𝓝 ((E η ω + E ξ ω) / 2)) :=
    ((hω (.inr false)).add (hω (.inr true))).div_const 2
  obtain ⟨M, hM⟩ := hEnergy.bddAbove_range
  have hVar (n : ℕ) : ∑ i : Fin (2 ^ σ n), |z ω (σ n) i| ≤ M := by
    calc
      _ ≤ ∑ i : Fin (2 ^ σ n), (Δ X (σ n) i ω ^ 2 + Δ Y (σ n) i ω ^ 2) / 2 := by
        apply Finset.sum_le_sum
        intro i _
        dsimp only [z]
        rw [abs_mul]
        have h := sq_nonneg (|Δ X (σ n) i ω| - |Δ Y (σ n) i ω|)
        nlinarith only [h, sq_abs (Δ X (σ n) i ω), sq_abs (Δ Y (σ n) i ω)]
      _ = (Q X (σ n) ω + Q Y (σ n) ω) / 2 := by
        rw [← Finset.sum_div, Finset.sum_add_distrib]
        simp only [Q, show t 0 (Fin.last (2 ^ (0 : ℕ))) = T from regularDyadic_last_time T 0,
          if_pos (ht _ _)]
      _ ≤ M := hM (mem_range_self n)
  have hb : Integrable (b ω) (TimeMeasure.upTo T) := integrable_finsetSum _ (fun j _ => hp j)

steps.title: Apply the continuous-weight limit pathwise
steps.text: For almost every sample, the continuous weight, the bounded signed masses, and the cumulative limits satisfy the deterministic theorem. Apply the subsequence characterization of convergence in measure.
steps.formula: S_{n_\ell}\to\int W(s)\sum_j\eta_j(s)\xi_j(s)\,ds\quad\text{almost everywhere along the selected subsequence}.
steps.lean:
exact tendsto_dyadic_weighted_sums_of_prefix_limits hT (fun s => W s ω) (b ω) hw hb
    (z ω) σ hσ ⟨M, hVar⟩ (fun m k => hω (.inl ⟨m, k⟩))

units.lean_statement: The theorem uses the actual completed stochastic integrals and the actual horizon time integral, with the weight evaluated at the left grid endpoint.
units.lean_proof: Select one almost-everywhere subsequence for the prefixes and energy sums. Use the energy sums to bound total absolute mass and apply the deterministic theorem.
units.boundary: The limit is for the full horizon and is in measure. The weight assumptions suffice for this quadratic term. The first-order stochastic integral and the full smooth Itô identity have their own contracts.

units.title: Stopping at a dyadic grid point selects the increments ending there or earlier
units.statement: Fix a positive time horizon T, a coarse level m and a fine level n at least m. Choose a coarse grid point τ. For any two real paths X and Y on nonnegative time, the fine-grid sum of products of their stopped increments equals the fine-grid prefix sum of their original increment products through τ.
assumptions: The horizon T is positive. Both grids are regular dyadic partitions of [0,T].
The fine level n is at least the coarse level m. The cutoff may be any coarse grid point, including 0 and T.
The two paths are arbitrary real-valued functions of nonnegative time.

steps.title: Find the coarse cell containing each fine cell
steps.text: A fine cell is contained in the coarse cell with index j given by dyadic refinement. If the cutoff is the kth coarse grid point, that cell lies on one side of the cutoff.
steps.lean:
intro τ t
  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
  intro i _
  let j := coarseCell hmn i
  have hstep : t i.castSucc < t i.succ :=
    regularGridTimes_strictMono (dyadicMesh_pos hT n) _ (Fin.castSucc_lt_succ)

steps.title: Evaluate the stopped increment on either side
steps.text: If j is smaller than k, both endpoints keep their original time. Otherwise both endpoints are mapped to τ, and the increment is zero. The inequality on the right endpoint includes a fine cell that ends exactly at τ.
steps.lean:
by_cases h : j.val < k.val
  · have hj : j.succ ≤ k := Nat.succ_le_iff.2 h
    have hright : t i.succ ≤ τ :=
      (fine_right_endpoint_le_coarse_right (T := T) hmn i).trans
        ((regularGridTimes_strictMono (dyadicMesh_pos hT m) _).monotone hj)
    rw [if_pos hright, min_eq_right hright, min_eq_right (hstep.le.trans hright)]
  · have hj : k ≤ j.castSucc := Nat.le_of_not_gt h
    have hleft : τ ≤ t i.castSucc :=
      ((regularGridTimes_strictMono (dyadicMesh_pos hT m) _).monotone hj).trans
        (coarse_left_endpoint_le_fine_left (T := T) hmn i)
    rw [if_neg (not_le.mpr (hleft.trans_lt hstep)), min_eq_left (hleft.trans hstep.le), min_eq_left hleft]
    simp

units.lean_statement: The right-hand side uses a sum over all fine cell indices with an if on the right endpoint. The two endpoint indices are i.castSucc and i.succ.
units.lean_proof: Dyadic refinement gives the enclosing coarse cell. Its order relative to the cutoff resolves both the condition and the stopped times, pointwise.
units.boundary: The proof gives a pointwise identity on nested deterministic grids. Convergence of the sum requires a separate probabilistic result.

units.title: Quadratic variation of an Itô row up to a fixed dyadic time
units.statement: Let X be the sum of a drift with almost surely continuous finite-variation paths on [0,T] and a finite row of completed scalar Itô integrals. The integrals are driven by the coordinates of a standard vector Brownian motion relative to the given filtration and measure. For a fixed coarse dyadic time τ, the prefix sums of squared fine-grid increments of X converge in measure to the integrated squared row norm up to τ.
assumptions: The underlying measure is finite and the filtration satisfies the usual conditions. The Euclidean-valued standard Brownian motion is relative to that filtration and measure.
Each coordinate integrand is progressive and square-integrable for the product of the horizon time measure and the underlying measure. The coordinate index set is finite with decidable equality.
The horizon T is positive. At each deterministic time t≤T, the drift Aₜ is almost-everywhere strongly measurable. Almost every drift path is continuous and has bounded variation on [0,T].
The cutoff τ is any fixed grid point of a specified coarse dyadic grid on [0,T].

steps.title: Stop the drift by a monotone time change
steps.text: The map that clips time at τ is continuous, nondecreasing and maps the horizon into itself. Its composition with the drift preserves the path conditions and has almost-everywhere measurable evaluations at each time.
steps.lean:
intro τ X
  have hτ : τ ≤ T :=
    ((regularGridTimes_strictMono (dyadicMesh_pos hT m) _).monotone (Fin.le_last k)).trans_eq
      (regularDyadic_last_time T m)
  let S (t : ℝ≥0) := min τ t
  let A₀ (t : ℝ≥0) := A (S t)
  have hA₀ (t : ℝ≥0) (_ht : t ≤ T) : AEStronglyMeasurable (A₀ t) μ :=
    hAmeas _ ((min_le_left τ t).trans hτ)
  have hmaps : MapsTo S (Icc 0 T) (Icc 0 T) := fun t _ =>
    ⟨bot_le, (min_le_left τ t).trans hτ⟩
  have hmono : Monotone S := fun _ _ ht => min_le_min_left τ ht
  have hcont : Continuous S := continuous_const.min continuous_id
  have hA₀path : ∀ᵐ ω ∂μ, ContinuousOn (fun t => A₀ t ω) (Icc 0 T) ∧
      BoundedVariationOn (fun t => A₀ t ω) (Icc 0 T) := by
    filter_upwards [hA] with ω hω
    refine ⟨hω.1.comp hcont.continuousOn hmaps, ?_⟩
    exact ne_top_of_le_ne_top hω.2
      (eVariationOn.comp_le_of_monotoneOn (fun t => A t ω) S (hmono.monotoneOn _) hmaps)

steps.title: Apply stopped quadratic variation
steps.text: The fixed time is a bounded stopping time. With the clipped drift, the existing stopped-row theorem gives convergence of the squared increments of the full stopped process to the restricted energy.
steps.lean:
have h := tendstoInMeasure_dyadic_sq_increments_stopped_ito_add_boundedVariation
    hB hT hUsual η (fun _ => τ) (isChewiStoppingTime_const filtration τ) (fun _ => hτ)
    A₀ hA₀ hA₀path

steps.title: Replace stopped increments by the prefix
steps.text: Every sufficiently fine grid refines the chosen coarse grid. The deterministic cutoff identity with both paths equal to X gives exact equality of the two sums at those levels.
steps.lean:
refine TendstoInMeasure.congr' ?_ EventuallyEq.rfl h
  filter_upwards [eventually_ge_atTop m] with n hn
  exact Eventually.of_forall fun ω => by
    simpa only [pow_two, X, A₀, S] using
      dyadic_sum_mul_stopped_increments_eq_prefix hT hn k (fun t => X t ω) (fun t => X t ω)

units.lean_statement: The stopped-row construction uses the actual completed Itô process for each Brownian coordinate. The time integral is restricted to Iic τ under TimeMeasure.upTo T.
units.lean_proof: Clip the drift, apply the stopped-row limit at the deterministic stopping time and identify the sums on all refinements.
units.boundary: The theorem concerns one fixed dyadic cutoff and convergence in measure for the unweighted scalar sum. Mixed and continuously weighted limits are separate results.

units.title: Covariation of two Itô rows up to a fixed dyadic time
units.statement: Let X and Y be two real Itô rows driven by the same finite-dimensional Brownian motion. Fix a coarse dyadic time τ. The sum of products of the increments of X and Y over fine cells ending at or before τ converges in measure to the time integral of the inner product of their diffusion rows up to τ.
assumptions: The underlying measure is finite. The filtration satisfies the usual conditions, and B is a standard Euclidean Brownian motion relative to that filtration and measure.

The two finite rows of coefficients η and ξ are progressive and square-integrable for the product of the horizon time measure and the underlying measure. The Brownian coordinate index set has decidable equality.
The drift evaluations of X and Y are almost-everywhere strongly measurable at every deterministic time t≤T. Almost every drift path is continuous and has bounded variation on [0,T].
The horizon T is positive. The fixed cutoff τ is any coarse dyadic grid point, including the endpoints.

notation.text: Each row includes its own drift and one completed scalar Itô integral per Brownian coordinate.
At level n the fine grid has 2ⁿ cells. The cutoff belongs to a fixed coarse grid.

steps.title: Form the sum of the two rows
steps.text: The sum of the drifts is continuous with variation at most the sum of the two variations. The integrands add in progressive L². Linearity of the completed Itô integral identifies the summed row Z with X+Y almost everywhere at each fine-grid time.
steps.lean:
intro τ X Y
  let t (n : ℕ) := regularGridTimes (dyadicMesh T n) (2 ^ n)
  let I (r : J → ProgressiveL2Integrand filtration μ T) (j : J) :=
    itoIntegralProcess (r j) hT ((coordinateFamily hB).isBrownian j) hUsual
  let plus (j : J) := ProgressiveL2Algebra.add (η j) (ξ j)
  let D (s : ℝ≥0) (ω : Ω) := A s ω + C s ω
  let Z (s : ℝ≥0) (ω : Ω) := D s ω + ∑ j : J, I plus j s ω
  let Δ (F : ℝ≥0 → Ω → ℝ) (n : ℕ) (i : Fin (2 ^ n)) (ω : Ω) :=
    F (t n i.succ) ω - F (t n i.castSucc) ω
  let Q (F : ℝ≥0 → Ω → ℝ) (n : ℕ) (ω : Ω) :=
    ∑ i : Fin (2 ^ n), if t n i.succ ≤ τ then (Δ F n i ω) ^ 2 else 0
  let E (r : J → ProgressiveL2Integrand filtration μ T) (ω : Ω) :=
    ∑ j : J, ∫ s in Iic τ, (r j).process s ω ^ 2 ∂(TimeMeasure.upTo T)
  have hDmeas (s : ℝ≥0) (hs : s ≤ T) : AEStronglyMeasurable (D s) μ :=
    (hAmeas s hs).add (hCmeas s hs)
  have hD : ∀ᵐ ω ∂μ, ContinuousOn (fun s => D s ω) (Icc 0 T) ∧
      BoundedVariationOn (fun s => D s ω) (Icc 0 T) := by
    filter_upwards [hA, hC] with ω ha hc
    exact ⟨ha.1.add hc.1, boundedVariationOn_add ha.2 hc.2⟩
  have hX : TendstoInMeasure μ (Q X) atTop (E η) :=
    tendstoInMeasure_dyadic_prefix_sq_increments_of_ito_row hB hT hUsual η A hAmeas hA m k
  have hY : TendstoInMeasure μ (Q Y) atTop (E ξ) :=
    tendstoInMeasure_dyadic_prefix_sq_increments_of_ito_row hB hT hUsual ξ C hCmeas hC m k
  have hZ : TendstoInMeasure μ (Q Z) atTop (E plus) :=
    tendstoInMeasure_dyadic_prefix_sq_increments_of_ito_row hB hT hUsual plus D hDmeas hD m k
  have ht (n : ℕ) (i : Fin (2 ^ n + 1)) : t n i ≤ T :=
    ((regularGridTimes_strictMono (dyadicMesh_pos hT n) _).monotone (Fin.le_last i)).trans_eq
      (regularDyadic_last_time T n)
  have hSum (s : ℝ≥0) (hs : s ≤ T) : ∀ᵐ ω ∂μ, Z s ω = X s ω + Y s ω := by
    have hCoordinate : ∀ᵐ ω ∂μ, ∀ j : J, I plus j s ω = I η j s ω + I ξ j s ω := by
      rw [ae_all_iff]
      intro j
      exact itoIntegralProcess_add (η j) (ξ j) hT ((coordinateFamily hB).isBrownian j) hUsual hs
    filter_upwards [hCoordinate] with ω hω
    change A s ω + C s ω + (∑ j : J, I plus j s ω) =
      (A s ω + ∑ j : J, I η j s ω) + (C s ω + ∑ j : J, I ξ j s ω)
    simp only [hω, Finset.sum_add_distrib]
    ring

steps.title: Polarize the three scalar limits
steps.text: Apply the scalar prefix theorem to Z, X and Y. The cell identity below turns the mixed increment sum into half the difference of their square sums. From any subsequence, extract a further one on which all three square sums converge almost everywhere and take the same linear combination there.
steps.lean:
change TendstoInMeasure μ P atTop M
  refine (exists_seq_tendstoInMeasure_atTop_iff hPm).2 ?_
  intro n hn
  obtain ⟨a, ha, hza⟩ := (hZ.comp hn.tendsto_atTop).exists_seq_tendsto_ae
  obtain ⟨b, hb, hxb⟩ := (hX.comp (hn.comp ha).tendsto_atTop).exists_seq_tendsto_ae
  obtain ⟨c, hc, hyc⟩ := (hY.comp ((hn.comp ha).comp hb).tendsto_atTop).exists_seq_tendsto_ae
  refine ⟨a ∘ b ∘ c, ha.comp (hb.comp hc), ?_⟩
  filter_upwards [hza, hxb, hyc, hEnergy, ae_all_iff.2 hPolar] with ω hz hx hy he hq
  have hz' := hz.comp (hb.comp hc).tendsto_atTop
  have hx' := hx.comp hc.tendsto_atTop
  have hLimit := ((hz'.sub hx').sub hy).div_const 2
  simpa only [Function.comp_apply, he, hq] using hLimit

steps.title: Identify the limit on each Brownian coordinate
steps.text: Each of the three squared coefficients is integrable in time on almost every path by product L² and Fubini. Apply the same polarization identity inside the restricted time integrals and sum over the coordinates.
steps.lean:
have hEnergy : ∀ᵐ ω ∂μ, (E plus ω - E η ω - E ξ ω) / 2 = M ω := by
    have hCell (j : J) : ∀ᵐ ω ∂μ,
        ((∫ s in Iic τ, (plus j).process s ω ^ 2 ∂(TimeMeasure.upTo T)) -
          (∫ s in Iic τ, (η j).process s ω ^ 2 ∂(TimeMeasure.upTo T)) -
          (∫ s in Iic τ, (ξ j).process s ω ^ 2 ∂(TimeMeasure.upTo T))) / 2 =
        ∫ s in Iic τ, (η j).process s ω * (ξ j).process s ω ∂(TimeMeasure.upTo T) := by
      filter_upwards [(plus j).memLp.integrable_sq.prod_right_ae,
        (η j).memLp.integrable_sq.prod_right_ae, (ξ j).memLp.integrable_sq.prod_right_ae]
        with ω hp he hx
      let ν := (TimeMeasure.upTo T).restrict (Iic τ)
      have hp' : Integrable (fun s => (plus j).process s ω ^ 2) ν := hp.integrableOn
      have he' : Integrable (fun s => (η j).process s ω ^ 2) ν := he.integrableOn
      have hx' : Integrable (fun s => (ξ j).process s ω ^ 2) ν := hx.integrableOn
      have hsub : Integrable (fun s => (plus j).process s ω ^ 2 - (η j).process s ω ^ 2) ν :=
        hp'.sub he'
      change ((∫ s, (plus j).process s ω ^ 2 ∂ν) -
        (∫ s, (η j).process s ω ^ 2 ∂ν) - (∫ s, (ξ j).process s ω ^ 2 ∂ν)) / 2 = _
      rw [← integral_sub hp' he', ← integral_sub hsub hx', div_eq_mul_inv, mul_comm,
        ← integral_const_mul]
      apply integral_congr_ae
      exact Eventually.of_forall fun s => by
        change (2 : ℝ)⁻¹ * (((η j).process s ω + (ξ j).process s ω) ^ 2 -
          (η j).process s ω ^ 2 - (ξ j).process s ω ^ 2) =
          (η j).process s ω * (ξ j).process s ω
        ring
    filter_upwards [ae_all_iff.2 hCell] with ω hω
    simp only [E, M, ← Finset.sum_sub_distrib, Finset.sum_div, hω]

units.lean_statement: The formula uses actual scalar completed integrals in each coordinate. The limiting integral is restricted to Iic τ under TimeMeasure.upTo T.
units.lean_proof: The proof uses scalar convergence for the two rows and their sum, followed by exact polarization of both the discrete sums and the limiting integrals.
units.boundary: The cutoff is fixed and the limit is in measure. Varying weights and pathwise or uniform-in-time convergence have separate contracts.

units.title: Stability of integrated square energy
units.statement: Integrate the squared value of each coordinate over time and add the coordinate energies. The difference between the two random energies is integrable, and its mean absolute value is controlled by the product-space L² norms of the coordinatewise sums and differences.
assumptions: The measure μ is finite, the horizon T is nonnegative, and J is a finite index set.
For every j, both processes are real, progressive for the given filtration, and square integrable on the product of μ and time measure restricted to the deterministic horizon [0,T].

steps.title: Factor the two squares
steps.text: On almost every sample path both squared inputs are integrable in time. Subtract their integrals and factor the difference inside the time integral.
steps.lean:
have hEq : diff =ᵐ[mu] fun omega => ∫ t, f (omega, t) ∂nu := by
    filter_upwards [hEta.prod_right_ae, hXi.prod_right_ae] with omega he hx
    change (∫ t, eta.process t omega ^ 2 ∂nu) -
      (∫ t, xi.process t omega ^ 2 ∂nu) = _
    change Integrable (fun t => eta.process t omega ^ 2) nu at he
    change Integrable (fun t => xi.process t omega ^ 2) nu at hx
    rw [← integral_sub he hx]
    apply integral_congr_ae
    filter_upwards [] with t
    change eta.process t omega ^ 2 - xi.process t omega ^ 2 =
      (eta.process t omega + xi.process t omega) * (eta.process t omega - xi.process t omega)
    ring

steps.title: Apply Fubini and Cauchy–Schwarz
steps.text: For coordinate j set u=ηⱼ+ξⱼ and v=ηⱼ−ξⱼ. Their product is integrable by Hölder. Move the absolute value inside the time integral, integrate over the product space, and apply Cauchy–Schwarz.
steps.lean:
calc
    _ = ∫ omega, |∫ t, f (omega, t) ∂nu| ∂mu :=
      integral_congr_ae (hEq.mono fun _ h => congrArg abs h)
    _ ≤ ∫ omega, ∫ t, |f (omega, t)| ∂nu ∂mu := by
      apply integral_mono hprod.integral_prod_left.abs hprod.abs.integral_prod_left
      intro omega
      simpa only [Real.norm_eq_abs] using
        norm_integral_le_integral_norm (fun t => f (omega, t)) (μ := nu)
    _ = ∫ z, |f z| ∂(mu.prod nu) := (integral_prod _ hprod.abs).symm
    _ ≤ ‖plus.toLp‖ * ‖minus.toLp‖ := by
      have hbound : (∫ z, |f z| ∂(mu.prod nu)) ≤
          Real.sqrt (∫ z, (u z)^2 ∂(mu.prod nu)) *
            Real.sqrt (∫ z, (v z)^2 ∂(mu.prod nu)) := by
        simpa [f, nu, processTimeMeasure, Real.norm_eq_abs, abs_mul, Real.rpow_two, sq_abs, Real.sqrt_eq_rpow] using hcs
      rwa [hnormPlus, hnormMinus, Real.sqrt_sq (norm_nonneg _), Real.sqrt_sq (norm_nonneg _)] at hbound

steps.title: Add over coordinates
steps.text: Use the triangle inequality on the finite coordinate sum. The coordinatewise integrability estimates justify exchanging the sum and integral.
steps.lean:
have hsum := integrable_finsetSum Finset.univ (fun j _ => hi j)
  refine ⟨hsum.congr (Eventually.of_forall fun omega => (heq omega).symm), ?_⟩
  simp_rw [heq]
  calc
    _ ≤ ∫ omega, ∑ j : J, |diff j omega| ∂mu :=
      integral_mono hsum.abs
        (integrable_finsetSum Finset.univ (fun j _ => (hi j).abs))
        (fun omega => Finset.abs_sum_le_sum_abs _ _)
    _ = ∑ j : J, ∫ omega, |diff j omega| ∂mu :=
      integral_finsetSum _ (fun j _ => (hi j).abs)
    _ ≤ _ := Finset.sum_le_sum (fun j _ => (scalar_pathEnergy_L1_le (eta j) (xi j)).2)

units.title: Read the time energy of a step process
units.statement: For a fixed sample path, the real time integral of an elementary adapted process squared equals the sum of its squared coefficients weighted by the lengths of its cells clipped at T.
assumptions: An elementary adapted real process on a finite strictly increasing grid, with its stored left-endpoint measurable bounded coefficients.
Any nonnegative horizon T and any sample point ω. The clipped interval lengths are nonnegative.

steps.title: Evaluate the nonnegative integral
steps.text: The existing cell formula evaluates the nonnegative Lebesgue integral. The squared coefficients and clipped lengths are finite, so the formula is a finite sum of finite terms. Convert the nonnegative integral to ℝ to obtain the real integral.
steps.lean:
have hm : Measurable (fun t => q.value t omega) := by
    unfold ElementaryAdaptedProcess.value
    exact Finset.measurable_sum _ fun _ _ =>
      Measurable.ite measurableSet_Ioc measurable_const measurable_const
  rw [integral_eq_lintegral_of_nonneg_ae (Eventually.of_forall fun _ => sq_nonneg _)
    (hm.pow_const 2).aestronglyMeasurable, lintegral_value_sq, ENNReal.toReal_sum]
  · apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
    intro i _
    rw [ENNReal.toReal_mul, ENNReal.toReal_ofReal (sq_nonneg _)]
    rfl
  · intro i _
    exact ENNReal.mul_ne_top ENNReal.ofReal_ne_top ENNReal.coe_ne_top

units.title: Quadratic variation of elementary Itô rows
units.statement: At each level of a dyadic grid, take a row of completed Itô integrals of elementary processes on that level's grid. The sum of the squared row increments minus the row's time energy is square integrable at each level and tends to zero in mean absolute value.
assumptions: One Euclidean Brownian motion under the sample measure μ, relative to the given filtration. The coordinates in a finite index set J come from this same motion.
The sample measure is finite. The horizon T is positive and the filtration satisfies the usual conditions.

For each level n and coordinate j, the stored dyadic elementary process has level n. Its bounded left-endpoint measurable coefficients have fourth moments bounded by one common real constant C over all n, cells and coordinates.

steps.title: Use the Brownian cell increments
steps.text: The completed scalar integral on a cell equals the stored coefficient times that coordinate's Brownian increment almost surely. Sum this equality over the coordinates.
steps.lean:
have hInc (level : ℕ) (i : Fin (2 ^ level)) (j : J) :
      ∀ᵐ omega ∂mu,
        itoIntegralProcess (eta level j) hT (hcoord j) hUsual (times level i.succ) omega -
          itoIntegralProcess (eta level j) hT (hcoord j) hUsual (times level i.castSucc) omega =
          coeff level i j omega *
            (B (times level i.succ) omega j - B (times level i.castSucc) omega j) := by
    have h := itoIntegralProcess_elementary_grid_increment_ae
      (q level j) hT (hcoord j) hUsual (cell (q level j) (hlevel level j) i)
    dsimp only at h
    rw [(grid_endpoints (q level j) (hlevel level j) i).1,
      (grid_endpoints (q level j) (hlevel level j) i).2] at h
    exact h

steps.title: Match the compensator
steps.text: The real energy of each elementary input is exactly the squared coefficient sum weighted by the cell lengths. Thus the actual centered error agrees almost surely with the Brownian grid error.
steps.lean:
have hEnergy (level : ℕ) (omega : Omega) :
      (∑ j : J, ∫ t, (eta level j).process t omega ^ 2 ∂(TimeMeasure.upTo T)) =
        ∑ i : Fin (2 ^ level), (∑ j : J, (coeff level i j omega)^2) *
          ((times level i.succ - times level i.castSucc : ℝ≥0) : ℝ) := by
    change (∑ j : J, ∫ t, ((q level j).process.value t omega)^2 ∂(TimeMeasure.upTo T)) = _
    simp_rw [elementary_grid_compensator (q level _) (hlevel level _)]
    rw [Finset.sum_comm]
    exact Finset.sum_congr rfl (fun i _ => (Finset.sum_mul ..).symm)
  have hEq (level : ℕ) : error level =ᵐ[mu] discrete level := by
    filter_upwards [ae_all_iff.2 fun i => ae_all_iff.2 (hInc level i)] with omega hpoint
    change (∑ i : Fin (2 ^ level), (row level (times level i.succ) omega -
      row level (times level i.castSucc) omega)^2) -
      (∑ j : J, ∫ t, (eta level j).process t omega ^ 2 ∂(TimeMeasure.upTo T)) = _
    rw [hEnergy]
    simp only [discrete, Finset.sum_sub_distrib]
    congr 1
    apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
    intro i _
    congr 1
    dsimp only [row]
    rw [← Finset.sum_sub_distrib]
    exact Finset.sum_congr rfl (fun j _ => hpoint i j)

steps.title: Pass from mean square to mean absolute error
steps.text: The predictable row theorem gives an L² error and convergence of its second moment to zero. The Brownian sample measure is a probability measure, so Cauchy–Schwarz gives the L¹ conclusion.
steps.lean:
have hmem (level : ℕ) : MemLp (error level) 2 mu :=
    (memLp_congr_ae (hEq level)).2 (hDis.1 level)
  have hSqLim : Tendsto (fun level => ∫ omega, (error level omega)^2 ∂mu) atTop (nhds 0) := by
    have hEqIntegral (level : ℕ) :
        (∫ omega, (error level omega)^2 ∂mu) = ∫ omega, (discrete level omega)^2 ∂mu :=
      integral_congr_ae ((hEq level).mono fun _ h => congrArg (· ^ (2 : ℕ)) h)
    exact (tendsto_congr' (Eventually.of_forall hEqIntegral)).2 hDis.2
  have hUpper (level : ℕ) :
      (∫ omega, |error level omega| ∂mu) ≤ Real.sqrt (∫ omega, (error level omega)^2 ∂mu) := by
    have hholder : Real.HolderConjugate 2 2 := by
      rw [Real.holderConjugate_iff]
      norm_num
    have h := integral_mul_norm_le_Lp_mul_Lq hholder (μ := mu)
      (f := error level) (g := fun _ : Omega => (1 : ℝ))
      (by simpa using hmem level) (memLp_const 1)
    simpa [Real.norm_eq_abs, Real.rpow_two, sq_abs, Real.sqrt_eq_rpow] using h
  have hRoot : Tendsto (fun level => Real.sqrt (∫ omega, (error level omega)^2 ∂mu))
      atTop (nhds 0) := by
    simpa only [Function.comp_def, Real.sqrt_zero] using
      Real.continuous_sqrt.continuousAt.tendsto.comp hSqLim
  exact ⟨hmem, tendsto_const_nhds.squeeze hRoot (fun _ => integral_nonneg fun _ => abs_nonneg _) hUpper⟩

units.title: Quadratic variation of a progressive Itô row
units.statement: For one fixed row of progressive square-integrable real inputs, form the sum of their completed coordinate Itô integrals. Its dyadic squared-increment sum converges in L¹ to the total pathwise square energy. The signed error is integrable at every level.
assumptions: One Euclidean Brownian motion under the sample measure μ, relative to the given filtration. The coordinates in a finite index set J come from this same motion.
The sample measure is finite. The horizon T is positive and the filtration satisfies the usual conditions.
Each coordinate input is real, progressive, and square integrable on the product of μ and time measure restricted to [0,T]. The input row is fixed across levels and can be unbounded.

steps.title: Compare two inputs on the same grid
steps.text: The cell isometry gives square-integrable coordinate increments, so each row increment square is integrable. Fubini gives integrability of the literal path energy. Apply the row increment stability bound and the path energy stability bound to compare two input families on the same grid.
steps.lean:
have hInt (f : Inputs) (level : ℕ) : Integrable (err f level) mu := by
    have hRow (i : Fin (2 ^ level)) : MemLp (fun omega =>
        I f (times level i.succ) omega - I f (times level i.castSucc) omega) 2 mu := by
      simp only [I, ← Finset.sum_sub_distrib]
      exact memLp_finsetSum Finset.univ (fun j _ =>
        (itoIntegralProcess_increment_isometry (f j) hT (hcoord j) hUsual
          (hmono level (Fin.castSucc_le_succ (i := i))) (htime level i.succ)).1)
    have hQ : Integrable (Q f level) mu :=
      integrable_finsetSum Finset.univ (fun i _ => (hRow i).integrable_sq)
    have hE : Integrable (E f) mu :=
      integrable_finsetSum Finset.univ (fun j _ => (f j).memLp.integrable_sq.integral_prod_left)
    exact hQ.sub hE
  have hCompare (f g : Inputs) (level : ℕ) :
      (∫ omega, |err f level omega| ∂mu) ≤ bound f g + ∫ omega, |err g level omega| ∂mu := by
    have hQ := itoIntegralProcess_row_grid_quadraticVariation_L1_le f g hT hcoord hUsual
      (times level) (hmono level) (hlast level).le
    have hE := progressiveL2_row_pathEnergy_L1_le f g
    let qdiff := fun omega => Q f level omega - Q g level omega
    let ediff := fun omega => E f omega - E g omega
    have hqi : Integrable qdiff mu := hQ.1
    have hei : Integrable ediff mu := hE.1
    have hgi := (hInt g level).abs
    calc
      _ ≤ ∫ omega, (|qdiff omega| + |ediff omega|) + |err g level omega| ∂mu := by
        apply integral_mono (hInt f level).abs ((hqi.abs.add hei.abs).add hgi)
        intro omega
        calc
          |err f level omega| = |(qdiff omega + -ediff omega) + err g level omega| := by
            congr 1
            dsimp only [err, qdiff, ediff]
            ring
          _ ≤ |qdiff omega| + |ediff omega| + |err g level omega| := by
            exact (abs_add_le _ _).trans (add_le_add (by simpa using abs_add_le (qdiff omega) (-ediff omega)) le_rfl)
      _ = ((∫ omega, |qdiff omega| ∂mu) + ∫ omega, |ediff omega| ∂mu) +
            ∫ omega, |err g level omega| ∂mu := by
        have hqe : Integrable (fun omega => |qdiff omega| + |ediff omega|) mu := hqi.abs.add hei.abs
        rw [integral_add hqe hgi, integral_add hqi.abs hei.abs]
      _ ≤ _ := add_le_add (add_le_add hQ.2 hE.2) le_rfl
  have hBoundLim (f : Inputs) (g : ℕ → Inputs)
      (hg : ∀ j, Tendsto (fun level => (g level j).toLp) atTop (nhds (f j).toLp)) :
      Tendsto (fun level => bound f (g level)) atTop (nhds 0) := by
    have hF (j : J) : Tendsto (fun _ : ℕ => (f j).toLp) atTop (nhds (f j).toLp) :=
      tendsto_const_nhds
    have hP (j : J) : Tendsto (fun n => P f (g n) j) atTop
        (nhds ‖(f j).toLp + (f j).toLp‖) := by
      simpa only [P, ProgressiveL2Algebra.toLp_add] using ((hF j).add (hg j)).norm
    have hD (j : J) : Tendsto (fun n => D f (g n) j) atTop (nhds 0) := by
      simpa only [D, ProgressiveL2Algebra.toLp_sub, sub_self, norm_zero]
        using ((hF j).sub (hg j)).norm
    have hPsum := tendsto_finsetSum (Finset.univ : Finset J) (fun j _ => (hP j).pow 2)
    have hDsum := tendsto_finsetSum (Finset.univ : Finset J) (fun j _ => (hD j).pow 2)
    have hProot := Real.continuous_sqrt.continuousAt.tendsto.comp hPsum
    have hDroot := Real.continuous_sqrt.continuousAt.tendsto.comp hDsum
    have hProd := tendsto_finsetSum (Finset.univ : Finset J) (fun j _ => (hP j).mul (hD j))
    simpa [bound, Function.comp_def] using ((hProot.const_mul (Fintype.card J : ℝ)).mul hDroot).add hProd

steps.title: Prove the limit at fixed clipping
steps.text: The lagged dyadic approximants have coefficients bounded by M at fixed clipping M. They satisfy the elementary theorem and converge in L² to the clipped integrands. Apply the comparison at each matching level.
steps.lean:
let clip (M : ℕ) : Inputs := fun j => clipped (eta j) M
  let q (M level : ℕ) (j : J) : DyadicElementaryProcess filtration T :=
    ⟨level, laggedDyadicApprox (eta j) hT level M, laggedDyadicApprox_times _ _ _ _⟩
  let approx (M level : ℕ) : Inputs := fun j => elementaryIntegrand (q M level j) (hcoord j)
  have hApprox (M : ℕ) (j : J) :
      Tendsto (fun level => (approx M level j).toLp) atTop (nhds (clip M j).toLp) :=
    tendsto_laggedDyadicApprox_toLp_clipped (eta j) hT M
  have hMom (M level : ℕ) (j : J) (i : Fin (2 ^ (q M level j).level)) :
      (∫ omega, ((q M level j).process.coeff i omega)^4 ∂mu) ≤ (M : ℝ)^4 := by
    let c := (q M level j).process.coeff i
    have hc := (coeff_memLp (q M level j).process mu i 4).integrable_norm_pow' (p := 4)
    have hci : Integrable (fun omega => (c omega)^4) mu := by
      exact hc.congr (Eventually.of_forall fun omega => by
        simp only [Real.norm_eq_abs, ← abs_pow]
        exact abs_of_nonneg (by positivity))
    have hp (omega : Omega) : (c omega)^4 ≤ (M : ℝ)^4 := by
      have hbound : |c omega| ≤ (M : ℝ) :=
        laggedDyadicCoeff_abs_le (eta j) hT level M i omega
      simpa only [← abs_pow, abs_of_nonneg (show 0 ≤ (c omega)^4 by positivity)] using
        pow_le_pow_left₀ (abs_nonneg (c omega)) hbound 4
    calc
      _ ≤ ∫ _ : Omega, (M : ℝ)^4 ∂mu := integral_mono hci (integrable_const _) hp
      _ = _ := by simp
  have hApproxQV (M : ℕ) :
      Tendsto (fun level => ∫ omega, |err (approx M level) level omega| ∂mu) atTop (nhds 0) :=
    (tendsto_dyadic_elementary_ito_row_quadraticVariation_L1 hB hT hUsual (q M)
      (fun _ _ => rfl) ((M : ℝ)^4) (hMom M)).2
  have hClipQV (M : ℕ) :
      Tendsto (fun level => ∫ omega, |err (clip M) level omega| ∂mu) atTop (nhds 0) := by
    refine tendsto_const_nhds.squeeze ?_
      (fun _ => integral_nonneg fun _ => abs_nonneg _)
      (fun level => hCompare (clip M) (approx M level) level)
    simpa only [add_zero] using (hBoundLim (clip M) (approx M) (hApprox M)).add (hApproxQV M)

steps.title: Remove the clipping
steps.text: Choose M so the comparison error is small uniformly over all levels. Then take the dyadic level large enough for that fixed M.
steps.lean:
refine ⟨hInt eta, tendsto_order.2 ⟨?_, ?_⟩⟩
  · intro x hx
    exact Eventually.of_forall (fun _ => hx.trans_le (integral_nonneg fun _ => abs_nonneg _))
  · intro epsilon heps
    have he : 0 < epsilon / 2 := by positivity
    obtain ⟨M, hM⟩ := ((tendsto_order.1
      (hBoundLim eta clip (fun j => tendsto_clipped_toLp (eta j)))).2 (epsilon / 2) he).exists
    filter_upwards [(tendsto_order.1 (hClipQV M)).2 (epsilon / 2) he] with level hlevel
    exact (hCompare eta (clip M) level).trans_lt (by linarith)

units.title: Quadratic variation up to a common stop
units.statement: Evaluate the original finite Itô row at a common bounded stopping time capped by the evaluation time. The dyadic squared-increment sum of this stopped row converges in L¹ to the original square energy accumulated up to that stop, with integrable signed error at every level.
assumptions: One Euclidean Brownian motion under the sample measure μ, relative to the given filtration. The coordinates in a finite index set J come from this same motion.
The sample measure is finite. The horizon T is positive and the filtration satisfies the usual conditions.
Each coordinate input is progressive and product-space square integrable. One [0,T]-valued stopping time τ is shared by all coordinates and satisfies 0 ≤ τ(ω) ≤ T at every sample point.

steps.title: Identify the stopped row at every grid endpoint
steps.text: Use the fixed-time stopping theorem at all endpoints of one finite grid. This identifies the actual stopped row with the completed row of closed stopped integrands almost surely.
steps.lean:
have hAt (level : ℕ) (k : Fin (2 ^ level + 1)) (j : J) :
      ∀ᵐ omega ∂mu,
        itoIntegralProcess (stoppedEta j) hT (hcoord j) hUsual (times level k) omega =
          itoIntegralProcess (eta j) hT (hcoord j) hUsual (min (tau omega) (times level k)) omega :=
    itoIntegralProcess_stop_ae (eta j) hT tau htau htauT (hcoord j) hUsual (htime level k)

steps.title: Identify the stopped energy
steps.text: Squaring the stopped integrand preserves its indicator. Integrate the original coefficient squared on the closed interval ending at τ.
steps.lean:
have hEnergy (j : J) (omega : Omega) :
      (∫ t, (stoppedEta j).process t omega ^ 2 ∂(TimeMeasure.upTo T)) =
        ∫ t in Set.Iic (tau omega), (eta j).process t omega ^ 2 ∂(TimeMeasure.upTo T) := by
    rw [← integral_indicator measurableSet_Iic]
    apply integral_congr_ae
    filter_upwards [] with t
    change (if (t : WithTop ℝ≥0) ≤ (tau omega : WithTop ℝ≥0)
      then (eta j).process t omega else 0)^2 = _
    by_cases ht : t ≤ tau omega
    · rw [if_pos (WithTop.coe_le_coe.mpr ht),
        Set.indicator_of_mem (show t ∈ Set.Iic (tau omega) from ht)]
    · rw [if_neg (fun h => ht (WithTop.coe_le_coe.mp h)),
        Set.indicator_of_notMem (show t ∉ Set.Iic (tau omega) from ht)]
      norm_num

steps.title: Apply the progressive-row theorem
steps.text: Stopping preserves progressive L². Replace the row values and energy at each level by their identified counterparts and use the already proved L¹ limit.
steps.lean:
have hEq (level : ℕ) : stoppedError level =ᵐ[mu] error level := by
    filter_upwards [ae_all_iff.2 fun k => ae_all_iff.2 (hAt level k)] with omega homega
    have hRow (k : Fin (2 ^ level + 1)) : stoppedRow (times level k) omega =
        row (times level k) omega :=
      Finset.sum_congr rfl (fun j _ => homega k j)
    simp only [stoppedError, error, hEnergy, hRow]
    rfl
  have hLimit : (∀ level, Integrable (stoppedError level) mu) ∧
      Tendsto (fun level => ∫ omega, |stoppedError level omega| ∂mu) atTop (nhds 0) :=
    tendsto_dyadic_ito_row_quadraticVariation_L1 hB hT hUsual stoppedEta
  refine ⟨fun level => (hLimit.1 level).congr (hEq level), ?_⟩
  exact (tendsto_congr' (Eventually.of_forall fun level =>
    integral_congr_ae ((hEq level).mono fun _ h => congrArg abs h))).1 hLimit.2

units.title: Sum the Itô energy over a time grid
units.statement: Take a scalar completed Itô integral of a progressive square-integrable integrand. The sum of its squared increments along a finite nondecreasing deterministic grid is integrable. Its expectation is the integrand's squared energy over the half-open span of the grid.
assumptions: On a positive finite time horizon, the given filtration and finite sample measure satisfy the usual conditions used to construct the completed Itô integral.
The integrand is real and progressive with finite product-space squared energy, and the scalar Brownian driver is relative to the given filtration.
The grid satisfies 0 ≤ t₀ ≤ ⋯ ≤ tₙ ≤ T. A grid with no cells and repeated endpoints are allowed.

steps.title: Apply the isometry on each cell
steps.text: The scalar increment is square integrable on each cell. Therefore its square and their finite sum are integrable.
steps.lean:
have hc (i : Fin n) :=
    itoIntegralProcess_increment_isometry eta hT hB hUsual
      (hmono (Fin.castSucc_le_succ (i := i))) ((hmono (Fin.le_last _)).trans hlast)
  have hi (i : Fin n) : Integrable (fun omega => (inc i omega)^2) mu :=
    (hc i).1.integrable_sq
  refine ⟨integrable_finsetSum Finset.univ (fun i _ => hi i), ?_⟩

steps.title: Combine the adjacent intervals
steps.text: Exchange the finite sum and integral. The cell intervals are disjoint and concatenate to the grid span. Equal adjacent endpoints contribute an empty interval.
steps.lean:
rw [integral_finsetSum _ (fun i _ => hi i)]
  calc
    _ = ∑ i : Fin n, ∫ z in Prod.snd ⁻¹' Ico (times i.castSucc) (times i.succ),
          (processFunction eta.process z)^2 ∂(processTimeMeasure mu T) :=
      Finset.sum_congr rfl (fun i _ => (hc i).2)
    _ = _ := sum_setIntegral_grid_cells eta.memLp.integrable_sq times hmono

units.boundary: This equality is for the expectation over a fixed deterministic grid. It does not assert a pathwise quadratic-variation identity.

units.title: Compare squared increments of two Itô rows
units.statement: For each of finitely many coordinates, integrate two progressive square-integrable integrands against the same coordinate Brownian motion. Sum the resulting coordinate integrals to form each row. The difference of their squared-increment sums is integrable, and its expected absolute value is bounded uniformly over finite deterministic grids.
units.formula: \begin{gathered}R_f(t)=\sum_{j\in J} I_j(f_j)(t),\qquad Q(f)=\sum_i(\Delta_i R_f)^2,\\ E(f)=\sum_{j\in J}\|f_j\|_{L^2(\Omega\times[0,T],\,\mu\otimes dt)}^2,\\ \int |Q(\eta)-Q(\xi)|\,d\mu\le |J|\sqrt{E(\eta+\xi)}\,\sqrt{E(\eta-\xi)}.\end{gathered}
assumptions: On a positive finite time horizon, the given filtration and finite sample measure satisfy the usual conditions used to construct the completed Itô integral.
The grid lies in [0,T] and is nondecreasing. The coordinate index type J is finite and may be empty.
For each j, both integrands are real, progressive and square integrable. They share the same Brownian motion Bⱼ relative to the given filtration. The drivers at different indices may be dependent.

steps.title: Factor the difference of squares
steps.text: At the two deterministic endpoints in each cell, linearity identifies the increments of the sum and difference of the integrands. Multiply these two increments and add over cells.
steps.formula: Q(\eta)-Q(\xi)=\sum_i U_iV_i\quad\mu\text{-a.e.},\qquad U_i=\Delta_i R_{\eta+\xi},\quad V_i=\Delta_i R_{\eta-\xi}.
steps.lean:
have hfactor (i : Fin n) : ∀ᵐ omega ∂mu,
      (inc eta i omega)^2 - (inc xi i omega)^2 = inc plus i omega * inc minus i omega := by
    filter_upwards [hend _ (htime i.succ), hend _ (htime i.castSucc)] with omega hr hl
    dsimp only [inc]
    rw [hr.1, hr.2, hl.1, hl.2]
    ring
  have hq : (fun omega => qv eta omega - qv xi omega) =ᵐ[mu]
      (fun omega => ∑ i : Fin n, inc plus i omega * inc minus i omega) := by
    filter_upwards [ae_all_iff.2 hfactor] with omega homega
    change (∑ i : Fin n, (inc eta i omega)^2) - (∑ i : Fin n, (inc xi i omega)^2) = _
    rw [← Finset.sum_sub_distrib]
    exact Finset.sum_congr rfl (fun i _ => homega i)

steps.title: Apply Cauchy–Schwarz twice
steps.text: Each row increment is in L² by the scalar cell isometries and finite summation. The products are therefore integrable, as is the signed difference. Bound the absolute value of the finite sum by the sum of the absolute products. Apply integral Cauchy–Schwarz in each cell, then finite Cauchy–Schwarz to the resulting list of square roots.
steps.lean:
have hprod (i) : Integrable (fun omega => u i omega * v i omega) mu :=
    (hu i).integrable_mul (hv i)
  have hsum := integrable_finsetSum Finset.univ (fun i _ => hprod i)
  refine ⟨hsum, ?_⟩
  have hholder : Real.HolderConjugate 2 2 := by
    rw [Real.holderConjugate_iff]
    norm_num
  have hcell (i) : (∫ omega, |u i omega * v i omega| ∂mu) ≤
      Real.sqrt (A i) * Real.sqrt (B i) := by
    have h := integral_mul_norm_le_Lp_mul_Lq hholder
      (by simpa using hu i) (by simpa using hv i)
    simpa [A, B, Real.norm_eq_abs, abs_mul, Real.rpow_two, sq_abs, Real.sqrt_eq_rpow]
      using h
  calc
    _ ≤ ∫ omega, ∑ i : I, |u i omega * v i omega| ∂mu :=
      integral_mono hsum.abs
        (integrable_finsetSum Finset.univ (fun i _ => (hprod i).abs))
        (fun omega => Finset.abs_sum_le_sum_abs _ _)
    _ = ∑ i : I, ∫ omega, |u i omega * v i omega| ∂mu :=
      integral_finsetSum _ (fun i _ => (hprod i).abs)
    _ ≤ ∑ i : I, Real.sqrt (A i) * Real.sqrt (B i) :=
      Finset.sum_le_sum (fun i _ => hcell i)
    _ ≤ Real.sqrt (∑ i : I, A i) * Real.sqrt (∑ i : I, B i) := by
      rw [← Real.sqrt_mul (Finset.sum_nonneg fun i _ => hA i)]
      apply Real.le_sqrt_of_sq_le
      simpa only [Real.sq_sqrt (hA _), Real.sq_sqrt (hB _)]
        using Finset.sum_mul_sq_le_sq_mul_sq Finset.univ
          (fun i : I => Real.sqrt (A i)) (fun i : I => Real.sqrt (B i))

steps.title: Control the row energies
steps.text: Cauchy–Schwarz across the coordinates bounds the square of each row increment by the coordinate count times the sum of the coordinate squares. Apply the exact scalar grid isometry to each coordinate and enlarge the grid span to [0,T]. Each square root contributes a factor √|J|.
steps.lean:
have henergy (f) :
      (∑ i : Fin n, ∫ omega, (inc f i omega)^2 ∂mu) ≤
        (Fintype.card J : ℝ) * ∑ j : J, ‖(f j).toLp‖^2 := by
    have hsq (i : Fin n) (omega : Omega) :
        (inc f i omega)^2 ≤ (Fintype.card J : ℝ) * ∑ j : J, (coordinate f j i omega)^2 := by
      rw [hinc]
      simpa [mul_comm] using Finset.sum_mul_sq_le_sq_mul_sq Finset.univ
        (fun j : J => coordinate f j i omega) (fun _ : J => (1 : ℝ))
    have hsingle (j : J) :
        (∑ i : Fin n, ∫ omega, (coordinate f j i omega)^2 ∂mu) ≤ ‖(f j).toLp‖^2 := by
      have hgrid := (itoIntegralProcess_grid_isometry (f j) hT (hB j) hUsual
        times hmono hlast).2
      change (∫ omega, ∑ i : Fin n, (coordinate f j i omega)^2 ∂mu) = _ at hgrid
      rw [integral_finsetSum _ (fun i _ => (hcoord f j i).integrable_sq)] at hgrid
      rw [hgrid]
      change _ ≤ ‖(f j).memLp.toLp (processFunction (f j).process)‖^2
      rw [norm_sq_toLp_eq_integral_sq]
      exact integral_mono_measure Measure.restrict_le_self (Eventually.of_forall fun _ => sq_nonneg _)
        (f j).memLp.integrable_sq
    calc
      _ ≤ ∑ i : Fin n, (Fintype.card J : ℝ) * ∑ j : J,
          ∫ omega, (coordinate f j i omega)^2 ∂mu := by
        refine Finset.sum_le_sum (fun i _ => ?_)
        rw [← integral_finsetSum _ (fun j _ => (hcoord f j i).integrable_sq), ← integral_const_mul]
        exact integral_mono (hmem f i).integrable_sq
          ((integrable_finsetSum Finset.univ (fun j _ => (hcoord f j i).integrable_sq)).const_mul _)
          (hsq i)
      _ = (Fintype.card J : ℝ) * ∑ j : J, ∑ i : Fin n,
          ∫ omega, (coordinate f j i omega)^2 ∂mu := by
        rw [← Finset.mul_sum, Finset.sum_comm]
      _ ≤ _ := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left (Finset.sum_le_sum (fun j _ => hsingle j)) (by positivity)

units.title: Read one increment of an elementary Itô integral
units.statement: On any cell of an adapted dyadic elementary integrand's own grid, its completed Itô integral increment agrees almost surely with the cell coefficient times the corresponding Brownian increment.
assumptions: On a positive finite time horizon, the given filtration and finite sample measure satisfy the usual conditions used to construct the completed Itô integral.
The integrand is a dyadic elementary adapted process with its bounded, left-endpoint measurable cell coefficients.

The scalar driver is Brownian under μ relative to the given filtration. It is the driver for both the completed integral and the increment on the right. The chosen cell belongs to the elementary process's own grid.

steps.title: Identify the endpoint values
steps.text: At a positive deterministic grid point, use the terminal restriction identity for the elementary integrand. At time zero, both constructions have zero value.
steps.lean:
have hcomplete (t : ℝ≥0) (htT : t ≤ T) :
      I t =ᵐ[mu] elementaryItoProcess q.process B T t := by
    by_cases ht : t = 0
    · subst t
      dsimp only [I]
      rw [itoIntegralProcess_at_zero, elementaryItoProcess_zero]
    · exact (itoIntegralProcess_at_eq_terminal _ hT hB hUsual htT).trans

units.title: A progressive integrand for a sphere noise coordinate

assumptions: The sample measure is finite. The filtration is indexed by nonnegative time. $I$ is finite and has decidable equality.

    Real.sqrt (2 * temperature q.1) * (projectedNoiseColumn j (q.2 : E)) i

    continuous_subtype_val.comp continuous_snd

    continuous_const.sub (((L j).continuous.comp hState).smul hState)

assumptions: The probability space has a filtration and standard Euclidean Brownian motion relative to it, with the usual conditions. The Euclidean coordinate set is finite with decidable equality.

The sphere-valued process is jointly measurable and strongly progressive, with almost surely continuous paths. The ambient field is jointly continuous, and the deterministic temperature is continuous and nonnegative.

intro T hT

    temperature hTemperature i j
  let b (i : I) (t : ℝ≥0) (ω : Ω) := sphereDriftCoordinate u temperature i t (X t ω)
  let L (i : I) : E →L[ℝ] ℝ := PiLp.proj (p := 2) (𝕜 := ℝ) (β := fun _ : I => ℝ) i
  letI : CompactSpace S := isCompact_iff_compactSpace.mp (isCompact_sphere _ _)
  have hDrift (i : I) :

        ∀ ω, Integrable (fun t => b i t ω) (TimeMeasure.upTo T) := by
    let c (q : ℝ≥0 × S) := sphereDriftCoordinate u temperature i q.1 q.2
    have hState : Continuous (fun q : ℝ≥0 × S => (q.2 : E)) :=

    have hTemperatureFactor : Continuous (fun q : ℝ≥0 × S =>
        temperature q.1 * ((Fintype.card I - 1 : ℕ) : ℝ)) :=
      (hTemperature.comp continuous_fst).mul continuous_const
    have hc : Continuous c :=

    have h := continuous_coefficient_along_compact_process

    exact ⟨h.1, h.2.1⟩

    ext i

      ext i

  · exact Eventually.of_forall fun ω t _ j => by

units.statement: For two distinct coordinates of one Euclidean Brownian motion, the predictably weighted dyadic mixed increment sum is in L² at each level and converges to zero in mean square.
units.formula: C_n=\sum_i w_{n,i}\Delta_i B^j\,\Delta_i B^k,\qquad C_n\in L^2,\qquad \mathbb E[C_n^2]\longrightarrow0.

steps.title: Build a third unit projection
steps.text: Use the normalized sum of the two orthogonal coordinate vectors.
steps.lean:
let basis := EuclideanSpace.basisFun kappa ℝ
  let a := (Real.sqrt 2)⁻¹
  let ell := InnerProductSpace.toDualMap ℝ (EuclideanSpace ℝ kappa)
    (a • (basis j + basis k))
  have hBasis : ‖basis j + basis k‖ = Real.sqrt 2 := by
    have hSq : ‖basis j + basis k‖^2 = 2 := by
      rw [norm_add_sq_real, basis.orthonormal.norm_eq_one j, basis.orthonormal.norm_eq_one k,
        basis.orthonormal.inner_eq_zero hjk]
      norm_num
    rw [← hSq, Real.sqrt_sq (norm_nonneg _)]
  have hEll : ‖ell‖ = 1 := by
    dsimp [ell]
    rw [LinearIsometry.norm_map, norm_smul, Real.norm_eq_abs, abs_of_nonneg
      (inv_nonneg.mpr (Real.sqrt_nonneg _)), hBasis, inv_mul_cancel₀ (by positivity)]
  have ha : a^2 = 1/2 := by
    dsimp [a]
    rw [inv_pow, Real.sq_sqrt (by norm_num)]
    norm_num
  have hValue (x : EuclideanSpace ℝ kappa) : ell x = a * (x j + x k) := by
    change inner ℝ (a • (basis j + basis k)) x = _
    rw [real_inner_smul_left, inner_add_left]
    simp only [basis, EuclideanSpace.basisFun_inner]
  let U : ℝ≥0 → Omega → ℝ := fun t omega => ell (B t omega)
  let J : ℝ≥0 → Omega → ℝ := fun t omega => B t omega j
  let K : ℝ≥0 → Omega → ℝ := fun t omega => B t omega k
  have hU : IsBrownianMotionWithFiltration U filtration mu := standardBrownian_unit_projection hB ell hEll
  have hJ : IsBrownianMotionWithFiltration J filtration mu := (coordinateFamily hB).isBrownian j
  have hK : IsBrownianMotionWithFiltration K filtration mu := (coordinateFamily hB).isBrownian k
  let times (level : ℕ) := regularGridTimes (dyadicMesh T level) (2 ^ level)
  let err (X : ℝ≥0 → Omega → ℝ) (level : ℕ) (omega : Omega) : ℝ :=
    ∑ i, weight level i omega * centeredSquaredIncrement X (times level) i omega
  let cross (level : ℕ) (omega : Omega) : ℝ :=
    ∑ i, weight level i omega *
      ((J (times level i.succ) omega - J (times level i.castSucc) omega) *
        (K (times level i.succ) omega - K (times level i.castSucc) omega))

steps.text: The compensated time terms cancel, leaving the product of the two actual coordinate increments.
steps.lean:

          (K (times level i.succ) omega - K (times level i.castSucc) omega) =
        centeredSquaredIncrement U (times level) i omega -
          centeredSquaredIncrement J (times level) i omega / 2 -

      simp only [U,J,K,hValue]

    ring

    simp only [cross,err,hPolar,mul_sub,mul_div_assoc,Finset.sum_sub_distrib,Finset.sum_div]

      gcongr
      exact_mod_cast hpq
    exact (predictable_weighted_quadraticVariationError_L2 hX hmono

    have hm := ((hMem U hU level).sub ((hMem J hJ level).const_mul (1/2 : ℝ))).sub

steps.title: Control the product weights
steps.text: The average of two fourth powers bounds the square of the product. This gives the L² domain and the required uniform second moments.
steps.lean:
let _ : IsProbabilityMeasure mu :=
    (hB.isStandard.2.2.1 0 1 (by norm_num)
      (0 : StrongDual ℝ (EuclideanSpace ℝ kappa))).isProbabilityMeasure

    ((times level i.succ - times level i.castSucc : ℝ≥0) : ℝ)
  let inc (level : ℕ) (i : Fin (2^level)) (j : kappa) (omega : Omega) : ℝ :=
    B (times level i.succ) omega j - B (times level i.castSucc) omega j
  let weight (p : kappa × kappa) (level : ℕ) (i : Fin (2^level)) (omega : Omega) : ℝ :=
    coeff level i p.1 omega * coeff level i p.2 omega
  have hWeightAdapt (p : kappa × kappa) (level : ℕ) (i : Fin (2^level)) :
      StronglyMeasurable[filtration (times level i.castSucc)] (weight p level i) :=
    (hAdapted level i p.1).mul (hAdapted level i p.2)
  have hFourth (level : ℕ) (i : Fin (2^level)) (j : kappa) :
      Integrable (fun omega => (coeff level i j omega)^4) mu := by
    have h := (hCoeff level i j).integrable_norm_pow' (p := 4)
    exact h.congr (Eventually.of_forall fun omega => by
      simp only [Real.norm_eq_abs, ← abs_pow]
      exact abs_of_nonneg (by positivity))
  have hPoint (x y : ℝ) : (x*y)^2 ≤ (1/2)*(x^4+y^4) := by
    nlinarith [sq_nonneg (x^2-y^2)]
  have hWeight (p : kappa × kappa) (level : ℕ) (i : Fin (2^level)) :
      MemLp (weight p level i) 2 mu := by
    have hMeas : AEStronglyMeasurable (weight p level i) mu :=
      (hWeightAdapt p level i).mono (filtration.le _)|>.aestronglyMeasurable
    apply (memLp_two_iff_integrable_sq hMeas).2
    refine (((hFourth level i p.1).add (hFourth level i p.2)).const_mul (1/2 : ℝ)).mono'
      (hMeas.pow 2) (Eventually.of_forall fun omega => ?_)
    rw [Real.norm_eq_abs, abs_of_nonneg (sq_nonneg _)]
    exact hPoint _ _

      (∫ omega, (weight p level i omega)^2 ∂mu) ≤ C := by
    have hJ := hFourth level i p.1
    have hK := hFourth level i p.2
    calc
      _ ≤ ∫ omega, (1/2 : ℝ) *
          ((coeff level i p.1 omega)^4 + (coeff level i p.2 omega)^4) ∂mu :=
        integral_mono (hWeight p level i).integrable_sq ((hJ.add hK).const_mul _) (fun omega => by
          exact hPoint _ _)
      _ = (1/2 : ℝ) * ((∫ omega, (coeff level i p.1 omega)^4 ∂mu) +
          (∫ omega, (coeff level i p.2 omega)^4 ∂mu)) := by
        rw [integral_const_mul]
        congr 1
        exact integral_add hJ hK
      _ ≤ C := by linarith [hC level i p.1, hC level i p.2]

steps.title: Apply the diagonal and mixed results
steps.text: The diagonal subtracts the elapsed time; distinct coordinates use the actual mixed increment product.
steps.lean:
let entry (p : kappa × kappa) (level : ℕ) (omega : Omega) : ℝ :=
    ∑ i, weight p level i omega *
      (inc level i p.1 omega * inc level i p.2 omega -
        if p.1 = p.2 then length level i else 0)
  have hEntry (p : kappa × kappa) :
      (∀ level, MemLp (entry p level) 2 mu) ∧
        Tendsto (fun level => ∫ omega, (entry p level omega)^2 ∂mu) atTop (nhds 0) := by
    rcases p with ⟨j,k⟩
    by_cases hjk : j = k
    · subst k
      have hj := (coordinateFamily hB).isBrownian j
      refine ⟨fun level => ?_, ?_⟩
      · have hmono : Monotone (times level) := by
          intro a b hab
          unfold times regularGridTimes
          gcongr
          exact_mod_cast hab
        simpa only [entry,inc,length,if_pos rfl,if_true,← pow_two,centeredSquaredIncrement,coordinateFamily]
          using (predictable_weighted_quadraticVariationError_L2 hj hmono
            (weight (j,j) level) (hWeightAdapt (j,j) level) (hWeight (j,j) level)).1
      · simpa only [entry,inc,length,if_pos rfl,if_true,← pow_two,centeredSquaredIncrement,coordinateFamily]
          using tendsto_integral_dyadic_predictable_weighted_quadraticVariationError_sq hj T
            (weight (j,j)) (hWeightAdapt (j,j)) (hWeight (j,j)) C (hMoment (j,j))
    · simpa only [entry,inc,if_neg hjk,sub_zero] using
        dyadic_predictable_mixed_increment_sum_L2 hB hjk T (weight (j,k))
          (hWeightAdapt (j,k)) (hWeight (j,k)) C (hMoment (j,k))

steps.title: Expand the actual row square
steps.text: Expanding the square and the compensator gives the finite sum over all ordered coordinate pairs.
steps.lean:
intro error
  have hCell (level : ℕ) (i : Fin (2^level)) (omega : Omega) :
      (∑ j, coeff level i j omega * inc level i j omega)^2 -
          (∑ j, (coeff level i j omega)^2) * length level i =
        ∑ j, ∑ k, weight (j,k) level i omega *
          (inc level i j omega * inc level i k omega - if j = k then length level i else 0) := by
    simp_rw [mul_sub, Finset.sum_sub_distrib]
    congr 1
    · simp only [pow_two, Finset.sum_mul_sum]
      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
      intro j _
      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
      intro k _
      simp only [weight]
      ring
    · rw [Finset.sum_mul]
      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
      intro j _
      simp [weight, mul_ite, pow_two]
  have hError (level : ℕ) (omega : Omega) :
      error level omega = ∑ p : kappa × kappa, entry p level omega := by
    change (∑ i, ((∑ j, coeff level i j omega * inc level i j omega)^2 -
      (∑ j, (coeff level i j omega)^2) * length level i)) = _
    simp_rw [hCell]
    rw [← Finset.univ_product_univ, Finset.sum_product, Finset.sum_comm]
    apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
    intro j _
    rw [Finset.sum_comm]

steps.title: Transfer the finite-sum limit
steps.text: Each pair sum is square integrable and its squared expectation tends to zero. The square of the whole sum is bounded by the number of pairs times the sum of squares.
steps.lean:
have hErrorMem (level : ℕ) : MemLp (error level) 2 mu :=
    (memLp_congr_ae (Eventually.of_forall (hError level))).2
      (memLp_finsetSum Finset.univ (fun p _ => (hEntry p).1 level))
  have hUpper (level : ℕ) :
      (∫ omega, (error level omega)^2 ∂mu) ≤
        (Fintype.card (kappa × kappa) : ℝ) *
          ∑ p : kappa × kappa, ∫ omega, (entry p level omega)^2 ∂mu := by
    have hInt (p : kappa × kappa) := ((hEntry p).1 level).integrable_sq
    have hSum := integrable_finsetSum Finset.univ (fun p _ => hInt p)
    calc
      _ ≤ ∫ omega, (Fintype.card (kappa × kappa) : ℝ) *
          ∑ p : kappa × kappa, (entry p level omega)^2 ∂mu :=
        integral_mono (hErrorMem level).integrable_sq (hSum.const_mul _) (fun omega => by
          rw [hError]
          simpa only [Finset.card_univ] using
            (sq_sum_le_card_mul_sum_sq (s := Finset.univ) (f := fun p => entry p level omega)))
      _ = _ := by
        rw [integral_const_mul, integral_finsetSum Finset.univ (fun p _ => hInt p)]
  have hLimit := (tendsto_finsetSum (Finset.univ : Finset (kappa × kappa))
    (fun p _ => (hEntry p).2)).const_mul (Fintype.card (kappa × kappa) : ℝ)
  refine ⟨hErrorMem, tendsto_const_nhds.squeeze ?_ (fun level => integral_nonneg fun _ => sq_nonneg _) hUpper⟩
  simpa using hLimit

units.title: Isometry on one deterministic Itô cell
units.statement: The increment of the actual completed Itô process between two deterministic times is in L². Its squared expectation equals the probability-time energy of the original integrand on that cell.
assumptions: The progressive real integrand belongs to the probability-time L² domain.
The driver is scalar Brownian relative to a filtration satisfying the usual conditions, with finite sample measure and a positive construction horizon T.
The deterministic times satisfy s≤t≤T; the interval may be empty.

steps.title: Use the two terminal representations
steps.text: At each endpoint the actual completed process is the terminal integral of the endpoint-restricted integrand. Linearity puts the increment in L².
steps.lean:
intro increment
  let right := eta.restrictAt t
  let left := eta.restrictAt s
  let difference := ProgressiveL2Algebra.sub right left
  let L := itoIntegralTerminal difference hT hB
  have hL : L = itoIntegralTerminal right hT hB - itoIntegralTerminal left hT hB :=
    itoIntegralTerminal_sub right left hT hB
  have hCoe := Lp.coeFn_sub (itoIntegralTerminal right hT hB) (itoIntegralTerminal left hT hB)
  have hInc : increment =ᵐ[mu] fun omega => L omega := by
    rw [hL]
    filter_upwards [itoIntegralProcess_at_eq_terminal eta hT hB hUsual htT,
      itoIntegralProcess_at_eq_terminal eta hT hB hUsual (hst.trans htT),hCoe] with omega hRt hLt hSub
    exact (congrArg₂ (· - ·) hRt hLt).trans hSub.symm

steps.title: Identify the restricted process
steps.text: The two restrictions agree before s and after t. Their difference on the intervening cell is the original integrand.
steps.lean:
refine ⟨(memLp_congr_ae hInc).2 (Lp.memLp L), ?_⟩
  let cell : Set (Omega × ℝ≥0) := Prod.snd ⁻¹' Set.Ico s t
  have hRep : processFunction difference.process =
      cell.indicator (processFunction eta.process) := by
    funext z
    change (if z.2 < t then eta.process z.2 z.1 else 0) -
        (if z.2 < s then eta.process z.2 z.1 else 0) = _
    by_cases hs : z.2 < s
    · simp [cell, hs, hs.trans_le hst, not_le.mpr hs]
    · by_cases ht : z.2 < t
      · simp [cell, hs, ht, le_of_not_gt hs, processFunction]
      · simp [cell, hs, ht]
  have hSq : (fun z => (processFunction difference.process z)^2) =
      cell.indicator (fun z => (processFunction eta.process z)^2) := by
    funext z
    rw [hRep]
    by_cases hz : z ∈ cell <;> simp [hz]

steps.title: Apply the completed isometry
steps.text: The terminal map preserves the L² norm. The square of the indicator-restricted function integrates over the same cell.
steps.lean:
calc
    _ = ∫ omega, (L omega)^2 ∂mu :=
      integral_congr_ae (hInc.mono fun _ h => congrArg (· ^ (2 : ℕ)) h)
    _ = ‖L‖^2 := by
      have h := norm_sq_toLp_eq_integral_sq (Lp.memLp L)
      rw [Lp.toLp_coeFn] at h
      exact h.symm
    _ = ‖integrandToLp difference hB‖^2 := by
      rw [show ‖L‖ = ‖integrandToLp difference hB‖ from itoIntegralTerminal_norm difference hT hB]
    _ = ∫ z, (processFunction difference.process z)^2 ∂(processTimeMeasure mu T) :=
      norm_sq_toLp_eq_integral_sq difference.memLp
    _ = _ := by
      rw [hSq, integral_indicator (measurable_snd measurableSet_Ico)]
