units.title: A time primitive has bounded variation
units.statement: The prefix integral of an integrable real time density has finite variation on the closed horizon.
assumptions: The horizon T is nonnegative. The real density b is integrable against nonnegative time measure restricted to [0,T].

steps.title: Control one increment
steps.text: A prefix increment is the integral of b over one time cell. Its absolute value is bounded by the integral of |b| over the same cell.
steps.lean:
have hinc (i : ℕ) : 0 ≤ V (u (i + 1)) - V (u i) :=
    sub_nonneg.mpr (prefixIntegral_mono hb.abs (fun _ => abs_nonneg _) (hu (Nat.le_succ i)))
  have hcell (i : ℕ) : edist (P (u (i + 1))) (P (u i)) ≤
      ENNReal.ofReal (V (u (i + 1)) - V (u i)) := by
    have hmono := hu (Nat.le_succ i)
    have hT := (hmem (i + 1)).2
    rw [edist_dist, Real.dist_eq]
    apply ENNReal.ofReal_le_ofReal
    dsimp only [P, V]
    rw [prefix_sub_eq_Ioc hb hmono hT, prefix_sub_eq_Ioc hb.abs hmono hT]
    simpa only [Real.norm_eq_abs] using
      norm_integral_le_integral_norm b (μ := (TimeMeasure.upTo T).restrict (Ioc (u i) (u (i + 1))))

steps.title: Telescope the bound
steps.text: Sum the bounds on any finite nondecreasing list of times in the horizon. The absolute-density prefixes telescope, and the final prefix is finite.
steps.lean:
have hV0 : 0 ≤ V (u 0) := by
    have h : V (0 : ℝ≥0) ≤ V (u 0) :=
      prefixIntegral_mono hb.abs (fun _ => abs_nonneg _) (show (0 : ℝ≥0) ≤ u 0 from bot_le)
    simpa only [V, prefixIntegral_zero] using h
  calc
    _ ≤ ∑ i ∈ Finset.range n, ENNReal.ofReal (V (u (i + 1)) - V (u i)) :=
      Finset.sum_le_sum (fun i _ => hcell i)
    _ = ENNReal.ofReal (∑ i ∈ Finset.range n, (V (u (i + 1)) - V (u i))) :=
      (ENNReal.ofReal_sum_of_nonneg (fun i _ => hinc i)).symm
    _ = ENNReal.ofReal (V (u n) - V (u 0)) := by
      rw [Finset.sum_range_sub (fun i => V (u i))]
    _ ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (V T) :=
      ENNReal.ofReal_le_ofReal ((sub_le_self _ hV0).trans
        (prefixIntegral_mono hb.abs (fun _ => abs_nonneg _) (hmem n).2))

units.title: Left-weighted sums against an integrable drift
units.statement: Multiply each increment of the drift primitive by the continuous weight at the left endpoint. The dyadic sums converge to the time integral of the weight times the original density.
assumptions: The horizon T is positive. The real weight w is continuous on [0,T].
The real density b is integrable for the time measure on [0,T].

steps.title: Read each prefix increment
steps.text: The difference of two strict prefixes is the integral over the half-open interval from the left endpoint. Each deterministic endpoint has zero time measure, so the integral agrees with the right-closed cell integral.
steps.lean:
private theorem prefix_sub_eq_Ioc {T s t : ℝ≥0} {b : ℝ≥0 → ℝ}
    (hb : Integrable b (TimeMeasure.upTo T)) (hst : s ≤ t) (htT : t ≤ T) :
    prefixIntegral b T t - prefixIntegral b T s =
      ∫ r in Ioc s t, b r ∂(TimeMeasure.upTo T) := by
  rw [prefixIntegral_eq_setIntegral, prefixIntegral_eq_setIntegral,
    min_eq_left htT, min_eq_left (hst.trans htT)]
  rw [← setIntegral_sdiff measurableSet_Iio hb.integrableOn (Iio_subset_Iio hst)]
  have hIco : Iio t \ Iio s = Ico s t := by
    ext r
    simp only [Set.mem_sdiff, mem_Iio, mem_Ico, not_lt]
    exact and_comm
  rw [hIco]
  apply setIntegral_congr_set
  have hne (a : ℝ≥0) : ∀ᵐ r ∂TimeMeasure.upTo T, r ≠ a := by
    rw [ae_iff]
    simp
  filter_upwards [hne s, hne t] with r hrs hrt
  exact propext ⟨fun h => ⟨lt_of_le_of_ne h.1 (Ne.symm hrs), h.2.le⟩,
    fun h => ⟨h.1.le, lt_of_le_of_ne h.2 hrt⟩⟩

steps.title: Take the left samples to the weight
steps.text: Every positive time through T lies in one cell. Its left endpoint approaches the time, so its sampled weight converges. Compact continuity gives a common bound, and |b| is integrable.
steps.lean:
let F (level : ℕ) (r : ℝ≥0) := sample w T level r * b r
  have hLim : Tendsto (fun level => ∫ r, F level r ∂(TimeMeasure.upTo T))
      atTop (nhds (∫ r, w r * b r ∂(TimeMeasure.upTo T))) := by
    refine tendsto_integral_of_dominated_convergence (fun r => C * |b r|)
      (fun level => (sample_measurable w T level).aestronglyMeasurable.mul hb.aestronglyMeasurable)
      (hb.abs.const_mul C) ?_ ?_
    · intro level
      filter_upwards [TimeMeasure.ae_mem_Ioc_zero_upTo T] with r hr
      rw [Real.norm_eq_abs, show F level r = sample w T level r * b r from rfl, abs_mul]
      exact mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right (sample_bound w hT level hr hBound) (abs_nonneg _)
    · filter_upwards [TimeMeasure.ae_mem_Ioc_zero_upTo T] with r hr
      exact (tendsto_sample w hT hw hr).mul_const (b r)
  refine (tendsto_congr' (Eventually.of_forall fun level => ?_)).2 hLim

steps.title: Identify the finite sums
steps.text: Integrating the piecewise left weight times b gives exactly the sum of the weighted prefix increments. Apply the dominated limit to this identity.
steps.lean:
let cell := fun (i : Fin (2 ^ level)) => Ioc (grid T level i.castSucc) (grid T level i.succ)
  let part := fun (i : Fin (2 ^ level)) =>
    (cell i).indicator (fun r => w (grid T level i.castSucc) * b r)
  have hpart (i : Fin (2 ^ level)) : Integrable (part i) (TimeMeasure.upTo T) :=
    (hb.const_mul _).indicator measurableSet_Ioc
  have hF (r : ℝ≥0) : F level r = ∑ i : Fin (2 ^ level), part i r := by
    dsimp only [F, sample]
    rw [Finset.sum_mul]
    apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
    intro i _
    change (if r ∈ cell i then w (grid T level i.castSucc) else 0) * b r = part i r
    by_cases hr : r ∈ cell i
    · rw [if_pos hr]
      exact (Set.indicator_of_mem hr (fun r => w (grid T level i.castSucc) * b r)).symm
    · rw [if_neg hr, zero_mul]
      exact (Set.indicator_of_notMem hr (fun r => w (grid T level i.castSucc) * b r)).symm
  simp_rw [hF]
  rw [integral_finsetSum _ (fun i _ => hpart i)]
  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
  intro i _
  change w (grid T level i.castSucc) *
    (prefixIntegral b T (grid T level i.succ) - prefixIntegral b T (grid T level i.castSucc)) =
    ∫ r, part i r ∂(TimeMeasure.upTo T)
  rw [prefix_sub_eq_Ioc hb (grid_mono hT level (Fin.castSucc_le_succ i)) (grid_le hT level i.succ)]
  rw [show part i = (cell i).indicator (fun r => w (grid T level i.castSucc) * b r) from rfl,
    integral_indicator (show MeasurableSet (cell i) from measurableSet_Ioc), integral_const_mul]

units.title: Left-weighted sums of completed Itô increments
units.statement: The dyadic sums of the original completed scalar Itô increments, weighted at left endpoints, converge in measure to the completed terminal integral of the literal product of the weight and the original input.
assumptions: There is one scalar Brownian motion relative to a filtration satisfying the usual conditions, a finite sample measure μ, and a positive deterministic horizon T.
The input η is real, progressive and product-space L². The weight is strongly progressive globally, almost surely continuous on [0,T], and uniformly bounded pointwise for t∈[0,T].

steps.title: Construct the literal product
steps.text: Strong progressiveness is closed under multiplication. The product time measure is supported on [0,T], so the horizon bound suffices for square integrability of the global literal product.
steps.lean:
classical
  let pm := processTimeMeasure mu T
  have hTime : ∀ᵐ z : Omega × ℝ≥0 ∂pm, z.2 ∈ Ioc 0 T :=
    Measure.quasiMeasurePreserving_snd.ae (TimeMeasure.ae_mem_Ioc_zero_upTo T)
  have hLift : @Measurable (Omega × ℝ≥0) (Set.Iic T × Omega) _
      (Subtype.instMeasurableSpace.prod (filtration T))
      (fun z : Omega × ℝ≥0 => ((⟨min z.2 T, Set.mem_Iic.2 (min_le_right _ _)⟩ : Set.Iic T), z.1)) :=
    ((measurable_snd.min measurable_const).subtype_mk).prodMk
      (measurable_fst.mono le_rfl (filtration.le T))
  have hW : MemLp (processFunction w) ∞ pm := by
    have hm : StronglyMeasurable (fun z : Omega × ℝ≥0 => w (min z.2 T) z.1) :=
      (hw T).comp_measurable hLift
    refine (memLp_congr_ae ?_).1 (memLp_top_of_bound hm.aestronglyMeasurable C ?_)
    · filter_upwards [hTime] with z hz
      simp [processFunction, min_eq_left hz.2]
    · exact Eventually.of_forall fun z => by
        simpa only [Real.norm_eq_abs] using hBound (min z.2 T) (min_le_right _ _) z.1
  let theta : ProgressiveL2Integrand filtration mu T :=
    ⟨fun r omega => w r omega * eta.process r omega, hw.mul eta.progressive, eta.memLp.mul' hW⟩
  refine ⟨theta, fun _ _ => rfl, ?_⟩

steps.title: Assemble the single-cell integrals
steps.text: Each left value is strongly measurable in its left filtration and bounded. The single-cell multiplier identity converts the weighted increment to a completed integral on that cell. Add the finite family.
steps.lean:
have hApprox (level : ℕ) : ∃ g : ProgressiveL2Integrand filtration mu T,
      (∀ r omega, g.process r omega = sample (fun t => w t omega) T level r * eta.process r omega) ∧
      itoIntegralProcess g hT hB hUsual T =ᵐ[mu] fun omega =>
        ∑ i : Fin (2 ^ level), w (grid T level i.castSucc) omega *
          (I (grid T level i.succ) omega - I (grid T level i.castSucc) omega) := by
    have hCell (i : Fin (2 ^ level)) :=
      itoIntegralProcess_bounded_past_cell_multiplier eta hT hB hUsual
        (grid_mono hT level (Fin.castSucc_le_succ (i := i))) (grid_le hT level i.succ)
        (w (grid T level i.castSucc)) (hw.stronglyAdapted _)
        (hBound _ (grid_le hT level i.castSucc))

    obtain ⟨g, hg, hG⟩ := assemble_integrands hT hB hUsual cell Finset.univ
    refine ⟨g, ?_, ?_⟩
    · intro r omega
      rw [hg, sample, Finset.sum_mul]
      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
      intro i _
      rw [hCellValue]
      by_cases h : grid T level i.castSucc < r ∧ r ≤ grid T level i.succ <;>
        simp [Set.mem_Ioc, h]
    · filter_upwards [hG, ae_all_iff.2 hCellIto] with omega hSum hCoord

steps.text: Left samples converge along continuous paths. Their squared product errors are dominated by a constant times |η|². The terminal Itô isometry carries product L² convergence to convergence in measure of the actual terminal processes.
steps.formula: w_n\eta\to w\eta\text{ in product }L^2,\qquad I_T(w_n\eta)\to I_T(w\eta)\text{ in measure}.
steps.lean:
let F (level : ℕ) (z : Omega × ℝ≥0) :=

      F level z = ((sample (fun t => w t z.1) T level z.2 - w z.2 z.1) *
        processFunction eta.process z)^2 := by
    simp only [F, processFunction, hApp, theta, sub_mul]
  let K := |C|

    filter_upwards [hTime] with z hz
    let error := sample (fun t => w t z.1) T level z.2 - w z.2 z.1

    rw [hF, Real.norm_eq_abs, abs_of_nonneg (sq_nonneg _), mul_pow]
    exact mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right hsq (sq_nonneg _)
  have hPt : ∀ᵐ z ∂pm, Tendsto (fun level => F level z) atTop (nhds 0) := by
    have hC : ∀ᵐ z : Omega × ℝ≥0 ∂pm, ContinuousOn (fun t => w t z.1) (Icc 0 T) :=
      Measure.quasiMeasurePreserving_fst.ae hCont

    have h := tendsto_integral_of_dominated_convergence (μ := pm) (F := F) (f := fun _ => (0 : ℝ))
      (fun z => (2 * K)^2 * (processFunction eta.process z)^2)
      (fun level => ((approx level).memLp.sub theta.memLp).integrable_sq.aestronglyMeasurable)
      (eta.memLp.integrable_sq.const_mul _) hDom hPt
    simpa only [integral_zero] using h
  have hNorm (level : ℕ) : ‖(approx level).toLp - theta.toLp‖^2 = ∫ z, F level z ∂pm := by
    have h := norm_sq_toLp_eq_integral_sq ((approx level).memLp.sub theta.memLp)
    rw [MemLp.toLp_sub] at h
    exact h
  have hLp : Tendsto (fun level => (approx level).toLp) atTop (nhds theta.toLp) := by
    apply tendsto_iff_norm_sub_tendsto_zero.mpr
    have h := Real.continuous_sqrt.continuousAt.tendsto.comp hSq
    simpa only [Function.comp_def, ← hNorm, Real.sqrt_sq (norm_nonneg _), Real.sqrt_zero] using h
  have hTerminal : Tendsto (fun level => itoIntegralTerminal (approx level) hT hB) atTop
      (nhds (itoIntegralTerminal theta hT hB)) := by
    apply tendsto_iff_norm_sub_tendsto_zero.mpr
    simpa only [itoIntegralTerminal_isometry_sub, integrandToLp] using
      (tendsto_iff_norm_sub_tendsto_zero.mp hLp)
  have hIto : TendstoInMeasure mu (fun level => itoIntegralProcess (approx level) hT hB hUsual T)
      atTop (itoIntegralProcess theta hT hB hUsual T) :=
    (tendstoInMeasure_of_tendsto_Lp hTerminal).congr
      (fun level => (itoIntegralProcess_terminal_eq (approx level) hT hB hUsual).symm)
      (itoIntegralProcess_terminal_eq theta hT hB hUsual).symm
  exact hIto.congr_left hAppIto

units.title: Continuous finite variation leaves the square-increment limit unchanged
units.statement: Add a continuous bounded-variation path A to a continuous real path X. The signed change in the sum of squared increments tends to zero on the full dyadic grid over the horizon.
assumptions: The horizon T is nonnegative. Both paths are continuous on [0,T].
The path A has finite total variation on [0,T]. The path X may have infinite total variation.

steps.title: Bound the total increments of A
steps.text: The grid is nondecreasing, so the sum of the absolute increments of A is at most its total variation. At T=0 every grid increment is zero.
steps.lean:
have hSum (level : ℕ) :
      (∑ i : Fin (2 ^ level), |A (times level i.succ) - A (times level i.castSucc)|) ≤ V := by
    have h := eVariationOn.sum_le_of_monotoneOn_Iic (f := A) (s := I)
      ((hu level).monotoneOn (Iic (2 ^ level)))
      (fun k hk => ⟨bot_le, (hu level hk).trans_eq (hEnd level)⟩)
    have hr := ENNReal.toReal_mono hVar h
    rw [ENNReal.toReal_sum (fun k _ => edist_ne_top _ _)] at hr
    rw [show (∑ i : Fin (2 ^ level), |A (times level i.succ) - A (times level i.castSucc)|) =
        ∑ k ∈ Finset.range (2 ^ level), |A (u level (k + 1)) - A (u level k)| from
          Fin.sum_univ_eq_sum_range (fun k => |A (u level (k + 1)) - A (u level k)|) _]
    simpa only [← Real.dist_eq, edist_dist, ENNReal.toReal_ofReal dist_nonneg, V] using hr

steps.title: Factor the square difference
steps.text: Expand both squares. Each term is the increment of A times a combination of the two path increments.
steps.lean:
have hFactor (i : Fin (2 ^ level)) :
      ((X (times level i.succ) + A (times level i.succ)) -
        (X (times level i.castSucc) + A (times level i.castSucc)))^2 -
        (X (times level i.succ) - X (times level i.castSucc))^2 =
        a i * (2 * x i + a i) := by dsimp [a, x]; ring

steps.title: Use continuity on the compact interval
steps.text: As the mesh shrinks, both largest increments vanish by uniform continuity. Multiply their combined bound by the finite total variation.
steps.lean:
have habs (i : Fin (2 ^ level)) : |2 * x i + a i| ≤ 3 * c := by
    have hx' : |x i| < c := by
      simpa only [x, Real.dist_eq] using hx _ (hMem level i.succ) _ (hMem level i.castSucc)
        ((hCellDist level i).trans_lt hmx)
    have ha' : |a i| < c := by
      simpa only [a, Real.dist_eq] using ha _ (hMem level i.succ) _ (hMem level i.castSucc)
        ((hCellDist level i).trans_lt hma)
    have h := abs_add_le (2 * x i) (a i)
    rw [abs_mul, abs_of_pos (by norm_num : (0 : ℝ) < 2)] at h
    linarith
  calc
    _ ≤ ∑ i : Fin (2 ^ level), |a i * (2 * x i + a i)| := Finset.abs_sum_le_sum_abs _ _
    _ ≤ ∑ i : Fin (2 ^ level), |a i| * (3 * c) := by
      simp only [abs_mul]
      exact Finset.sum_le_sum (fun i _ => mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left (habs i) (abs_nonneg _))
    _ ≤ V * (3 * c) := by
      rw [← Finset.sum_mul]
      exact mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right (hSum level) (by positivity)
    _ < epsilon := by
      dsimp [c]
      rw [← mul_assoc, ← mul_div_assoc]
      apply (div_lt_iff₀ (show 0 < 4 * (V + 1) by positivity)).2
      nlinarith

units.title: Use a past event on one Itô cell
units.statement: Restrict a progressive integrand to the cell (s,t] and an event known at s. The restricted process is progressive and square integrable. Its completed Itô integral at each fixed time is the original cell increment, truncated at that time, multiplied by the event indicator.
units.formula: \begin{gathered}\theta_r(\omega)=\mathbf1_A(\omega)\mathbf1_{\{s<r\le t\}}\eta_r(\omega)\quad\text{for all }r,\omega,\\ I_u(\theta)=\mathbf1_A\bigl(I_{t\wedge u}(\eta)-I_{s\wedge u}(\eta)\bigr)\quad\mu\text{-a.e. for each fixed }u\le T.\end{gathered}
assumptions: A progressive, real, product-space L² integrand on a positive deterministic horizon T with finite sample measure μ.
One scalar Brownian motion under μ relative to the given filtration. The filtration satisfies the usual conditions.
The deterministic endpoints satisfy 0 ≤ s ≤ t ≤ T.
The event A is measurable in the filtration at time s. The evaluation time u is any fixed time in [0,T].

steps.title: Switch between two stopping times
steps.text: Take the stop to be t on A and s on its complement. The event and its complement are already known at s, so Mathlib's piecewise constant theorem applies.
steps.lean:
let tau (omega : Omega) := if omega ∈ event then t else s
  have htau : IsChewiStoppingTime filtration (fun omega => (tau omega : WithTop ℝ≥0)) := by
    have hComplement : MeasurableSet[filtration s] eventᶜ :=
      @MeasurableSet.compl Omega event (filtration s) hEvent
    have heq : (fun omega => (tau omega : WithTop ℝ≥0)) =
        eventᶜ.piecewise (fun _ => (s : WithTop ℝ≥0)) (fun _ => (t : WithTop ℝ≥0)) := by
      funext omega
      by_cases he : omega ∈ event <;> simp [tau, Set.piecewise, he] <;> rfl
    rw [heq]
    exact isStoppingTime_piecewise_const hst hComplement
  have htauT (omega : Omega) : tau omega ≤ T := by
    by_cases he : omega ∈ event
    · simpa [tau, he] using htT
    · simpa [tau, he] using hst.trans htT

steps.title: Subtract the two closed stopped inputs
steps.text: Subtract the input stopped at s from the input stopped at the switch. This yields the exact pointwise event and cell restriction.
steps.lean:
let p := stop eta (fun omega => (tau omega : WithTop ℝ≥0)) htau
  let q := stop eta (fun _ => (s : WithTop ℝ≥0)) (isChewiStoppingTime_const filtration s)
  let theta := ProgressiveL2Algebra.sub p q
  refine ⟨theta, ?_, ?_⟩
  · intro r omega
    change ((if (r : WithTop ℝ≥0) ≤ (tau omega : WithTop ℝ≥0) then eta.process r omega else 0) -
      (if (r : WithTop ℝ≥0) ≤ (s : WithTop ℝ≥0) then eta.process r omega else 0)) = _
    by_cases he : omega ∈ event
    · rw [show tau omega = t from if_pos he]
      by_cases hrs : r ≤ s
      · rw [if_pos (WithTop.coe_le_coe.mpr (hrs.trans hst)), if_pos (WithTop.coe_le_coe.mpr hrs),
          if_neg (fun h => (not_lt.mpr hrs) h.2.1), sub_self]
      · have hsr : s < r := lt_of_not_ge hrs
        rw [if_neg (fun h => hrs (WithTop.coe_le_coe.mp h)), sub_zero]
        by_cases hrt : r ≤ t
        · rw [if_pos (WithTop.coe_le_coe.mpr hrt), if_pos ⟨he, hsr, hrt⟩]
        · rw [if_neg (fun h => hrt (WithTop.coe_le_coe.mp h)), if_neg (fun h => hrt h.2.2)]
    · rw [show tau omega = s from if_neg he, sub_self, if_neg (fun h => he h.1)]

steps.title: Use linearity and stopping compatibility
steps.text: The completed integral of the difference equals the difference of the two completed stopped integrals. Evaluate each one at the capped time.
steps.lean:
· intro u hu
    have heq : (ProgressiveL2Algebra.add theta q).toLp = p.toLp := by
      rw [ProgressiveL2Algebra.toLp_add]
      dsimp only [theta]
      rw [ProgressiveL2Algebra.toLp_sub, sub_add_cancel]
    filter_upwards [itoIntegralProcess_add theta q hT hB hUsual hu,
      itoIntegralProcess_congr_toLp_ae _ _ hT hB hUsual heq hu,
      itoIntegralProcess_stop_ae eta hT tau htau htauT hB hUsual hu,
      itoIntegralProcess_stop_ae eta hT (fun _ => s) (isChewiStoppingTime_const filtration s)
        (fun _ => hst.trans htT) hB hUsual hu] with omega hadd hcon hp hq
    have h := eq_sub_of_add_eq (hadd.symm.trans hcon)
    change itoIntegralProcess theta hT hB hUsual u omega =
      itoIntegralProcess p hT hB hUsual u omega -
        itoIntegralProcess q hT hB hUsual u omega at h
    change itoIntegralProcess p hT hB hUsual u omega =
      itoIntegralProcess eta hT hB hUsual (min (tau omega) u) omega at hp
    change itoIntegralProcess q hT hB hUsual u omega =
      itoIntegralProcess eta hT hB hUsual (min s u) omega at hq
    rw [hp, hq] at h
    by_cases he : omega ∈ event <;> simpa [tau, he] using h

units.title: Use a bounded past weight on one Itô cell
units.statement: Multiply the input on one Itô cell by a bounded real random variable known at the left endpoint. The literal weighted input is progressive and square integrable. Its terminal integral agrees almost surely with the weight times the original completed increment.
assumptions: A progressive, real, product-space L² integrand on a positive deterministic horizon T with finite sample measure μ.
One scalar Brownian motion under μ relative to the given filtration. The filtration satisfies the usual conditions.
The deterministic endpoints satisfy 0 ≤ s ≤ t ≤ T.
The multiplier w is strongly measurable at s and satisfies |w(ω)|≤C pointwise for a real bound C.

steps.title: Construct the literal weighted input
steps.text: The unweighted cell process vanishes up to s. At later times the left-endpoint multiplier is available in the filtration. Multiplication by the bounded variable preserves the product L² condition.
steps.lean:
obtain ⟨base, hBase, _⟩ := itoIntegralProcess_event_cell_multiplier
    eta hT hB hUsual hst htT Set.univ (@MeasurableSet.univ Omega (filtration s))
  have hZero (r : ℝ≥0) (hr : r ≤ s) (omega : Omega) : base.process r omega = 0 := by
    rw [hBase, if_neg (fun h => (not_lt.mpr hr) h.2.1)]
  let theta := multiplyPast base hZero w hw hC
  have hTheta (r : ℝ≥0) (omega : Omega) :
      theta.process r omega = if s < r ∧ r ≤ t then w omega * eta.process r omega else 0 := by
    change w omega * base.process r omega = _
    rw [hBase]
    by_cases hr : s < r ∧ r ≤ t <;> simp [hr]
  refine ⟨theta, hTheta, ?_⟩

steps.title: Prove the identity for simple weights
steps.text: Each fiber of a finite-range simple weight is a past event. Apply the event multiplier to each fiber, scale by its value and add the resulting integrals.
steps.lean:
have hEntry (c : ℝ) : ∃ p : ProgressiveL2Integrand filtration mu T,
      (∀ r omega, p.process r omega = entry c r omega) ∧
        I p T =ᵐ[mu] value c := by
    have hFibre : MeasurableSet[filtration s] (w ⁻¹' {c}) := by
      let : MeasurableSpace Omega := filtration s
      exact w.measurableSet_preimage {c}
    obtain ⟨p, hp, hi⟩ := itoIntegralProcess_event_cell_multiplier
      eta hT hB hUsual hst htT (w ⁻¹' {c}) hFibre
    refine ⟨ProgressiveL2Algebra.smul c p, ?_, ?_⟩
    · intro r omega
      change c * p.process r omega = _
      rw [hp]
      by_cases he : w omega = c ∧ s < r ∧ r ≤ t <;> simp [entry, he]
    · filter_upwards [itoIntegralProcess_smul c p hT hB hUsual (le_refl T), hi T (le_refl T)]
        with omega hScale hEval
      change itoIntegralProcess (ProgressiveL2Algebra.smul c p) hT hB hUsual T omega = _
      rw [hScale, hEval]
      by_cases he : w omega = c <;>
        simp [value, D, I, he, min_eq_left htT, min_eq_left (hst.trans htT)]

steps.title: Pass to the original bounded multiplier
steps.text: Approximate w pointwise by simple weights taking values in the same compact interval. The squared product errors are dominated by the square of the unweighted cell process times a finite constant, giving product-space L² convergence.
steps.lean:
let R := |C|
  let S := Set.Icc (-R) R
  have h0 : (0 : ℝ) ∈ S := ⟨neg_nonpos.mpr (abs_nonneg _), abs_nonneg _⟩
  let W (n : ℕ) : @SimpleFunc Omega (filtration s) ℝ := by
    letI : MeasurableSpace Omega := filtration s
    exact SimpleFunc.approxOn w hw.measurable S 0 h0 n
  have hLim (omega : Omega) : Tendsto (fun n => W n omega) atTop (nhds (w omega)) := by
    let : MeasurableSpace Omega := filtration s
    exact SimpleFunc.tendsto_approxOn hw.measurable h0
      (subset_closure (abs_le.mp ((hC omega).trans (le_abs_self _))))
  have hBound (n : ℕ) (omega : Omega) : |W n omega| ≤ R := by
    let : MeasurableSpace Omega := filtration s
    exact abs_le.mpr (SimpleFunc.approxOn_mem hw.measurable h0 n omega)
  choose approx hApprox hApproxIto using
    fun n => simple_cell_multiplier eta hT hB hUsual hst htT (W n)
  let u := processFunction base.process
  let F (n : ℕ) (z : Omega × ℝ≥0) := ((W n z.1 - w z.1) * u z)^2
  have hPoint (n : ℕ) (z : Omega × ℝ≥0) :
      (processFunction (approx n).process z - processFunction theta.process z)^2 = F n z := by
    simp only [processFunction, hApprox, hTheta, F, u, hBase, Set.mem_univ, true_and]
    by_cases hz : s < z.2 ∧ z.2 ≤ t <;> simp [hz, sub_mul]
  let hMeasure := processTimeMeasure mu T
  have hInt (n : ℕ) : Integrable (F n) hMeasure := by
    exact ((approx n).memLp.sub theta.memLp).integrable_sq.congr
      (Eventually.of_forall (hPoint n))
  have hDom (n : ℕ) (z : Omega × ℝ≥0) : ‖F n z‖ ≤ (2 * R)^2 * (u z)^2 := by
    have hA : |W n z.1 - w z.1| ≤ 2 * R := by
      have h : |W n z.1 - w z.1| ≤ |W n z.1| + |w z.1| := by
        simpa only [sub_eq_add_neg, abs_neg] using abs_add_le (W n z.1) (-w z.1)
      have hW := hBound n z.1
      have hw' := (hC z.1).trans (le_abs_self _)
      dsimp [R] at *
      linarith
    have hA2 : (W n z.1 - w z.1)^2 ≤ (2 * R)^2 := by
      have h := pow_le_pow_left₀ (abs_nonneg _) hA 2
      simpa only [← abs_pow, abs_of_nonneg (sq_nonneg (W n z.1 - w z.1))] using h
    rw [Real.norm_eq_abs, abs_of_nonneg (show 0 ≤ F n z from sq_nonneg _)]
    dsimp only [F]
    rw [mul_pow]
    exact mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right hA2 (sq_nonneg _)
  have hLimSq : Tendsto (fun n => ∫ z, F n z ∂hMeasure) atTop (nhds 0) := by
    have h :=
      tendsto_integral_of_dominated_convergence (μ := hMeasure) (F := F)
        (f := fun _ => (0 : ℝ)) (fun z => (2 * R)^2 * (u z)^2)
        (fun n => (hInt n).aestronglyMeasurable) (base.memLp.integrable_sq.const_mul _)
        (fun n => Eventually.of_forall (hDom n)) (Eventually.of_forall fun z => by
          simpa [F, sub_self] using (((hLim z.1).sub
            (tendsto_const_nhds (x := w z.1))).mul
              (tendsto_const_nhds (x := u z))).pow 2)
    simpa using h
  have hNorm (n : ℕ) : ‖(approx n).toLp - theta.toLp‖^2 = ∫ z, F n z ∂hMeasure := by
    calc
      _ = ∫ z, (processFunction (approx n).process z - processFunction theta.process z)^2 ∂hMeasure := by
        have h := norm_sq_toLp_eq_integral_sq ((approx n).memLp.sub theta.memLp)
        rw [MemLp.toLp_sub] at h
        exact h
      _ = _ := integral_congr_ae (Eventually.of_forall (hPoint n))
  have hLp : Tendsto (fun n => (approx n).toLp) atTop (nhds theta.toLp) := by
    apply tendsto_iff_norm_sub_tendsto_zero.mpr
    have h := Real.continuous_sqrt.continuousAt.tendsto.comp hLimSq
    simpa only [Function.comp_def, ← hNorm, Real.sqrt_sq (norm_nonneg _), Real.sqrt_zero] using h

steps.title: Identify the two limits
steps.text: The terminal Itô isometry carries the L² convergence to convergence in measure on the sample space. The weighted original increments also converge pointwise. Uniqueness of the limit in measure gives the identity.
steps.lean:
have hTerminal : Tendsto (fun n => itoIntegralTerminal (approx n) hT hB) atTop
      (nhds (itoIntegralTerminal theta hT hB)) := by
    apply tendsto_iff_norm_sub_tendsto_zero.mpr
    simpa only [itoIntegralTerminal_isometry_sub, integrandToLp] using
      (tendsto_iff_norm_sub_tendsto_zero.mp hLp)
  let D := fun omega => itoIntegralProcess eta hT hB hUsual t omega -
    itoIntegralProcess eta hT hB hUsual s omega
  have hIto : TendstoInMeasure mu (fun n => itoIntegralProcess (approx n) hT hB hUsual T)
      atTop (itoIntegralProcess theta hT hB hUsual T) :=
    (tendstoInMeasure_of_tendsto_Lp hTerminal).congr
      (fun n => (itoIntegralProcess_terminal_eq (approx n) hT hB hUsual).symm)
      (itoIntegralProcess_terminal_eq theta hT hB hUsual).symm
  have hRhs : TendstoInMeasure mu (fun n omega => W n omega * D omega)
      atTop (fun omega => w omega * D omega) := by
    apply tendstoInMeasure_of_tendsto_ae
    · intro n
      exact ((itoIntegralProcess_stronglyAdapted (approx n) hT hB hUsual T).mono
        (filtration.le _)).aestronglyMeasurable.congr (hApproxIto n)
    · exact Eventually.of_forall fun omega => (hLim omega).mul_const (D omega)
  exact tendstoInMeasure_ae_unique (hIto.congr_left hApproxIto) hRhs

units.title: Quadratic variation of a stopped Itô row with drift
units.statement: Add a continuous finite-variation drift to a finite row of original completed Itô integrals evaluated at a common bounded stop. The squared dyadic increments of the sum converge in measure to the original integrated square energy up to the stop.
assumptions: One actual finite-dimensional Euclidean Brownian motion under a finite sample measure μ, relative to a filtration satisfying the usual conditions.
A positive deterministic horizon T, one common finite-valued stopping time with τ(ω)≤T at every sample point, and progressive product-space L² input in each coordinate.
The drift A is almost surely continuous and of bounded variation on [0,T]. Its deterministic-time values are almost everywhere strongly measurable. No moment of the total variation is required.

steps.title: Check the stopped row as a process
steps.text: The stopped coordinate integrals are adapted and are continuous along the paths. Finite sums give the same properties for the row and give measurability of its square-increment sums.
steps.lean:
have hCont (j : J) (omega : Omega) : Continuous (fun t => coordinate j t omega) :=
    itoIntegralProcess_continuous (eta j) hT (hcoord j) hUsual omega
  have hMC (omega : Omega) : Continuous (fun t => M t omega) :=
    continuous_finsetSum _ (fun j _ => (hCont j omega).comp (continuous_const.min continuous_id))
  have hM (t : ℝ≥0) : AEStronglyMeasurable (M t) mu := by
    have hCoordinate (j : J) : AEStronglyMeasurable
        (fun omega => coordinate j (min (tau omega) t) omega) mu := by
      have hs := ((itoIntegralProcess_stronglyAdapted (eta j) hT (hcoord j) hUsual).stoppedProcess
        (hCont j) htau) t
      apply (hs.mono (filtration.le t)).aestronglyMeasurable.congr
      exact Eventually.of_forall fun omega => by
        rw [stoppedProcess_coe_apply, min_comm]
    apply (Finset.aestronglyMeasurable_sum Finset.univ (fun j _ => hCoordinate j)).congr
    filter_upwards [] with omega
    simp only [M, Finset.sum_apply]

steps.title: Use the stopped Itô bracket limit
steps.text: The stopped row's squared increments converge in L¹ to the literal stopped energy. Therefore they converge to that energy in measure.
steps.lean:
have hLimit : (∀ level, Integrable (fun omega => Q M level omega - E omega) mu) ∧
      Tendsto (fun level => ∫ omega, |Q M level omega - E omega| ∂mu) atTop (nhds 0) :=
    tendsto_dyadic_stopped_ito_row_quadraticVariation_L1 hB hT hUsual eta tau htau htauT
  have hE : AEStronglyMeasurable E mu := by
    apply ((hQ M (fun t _ => hM t) 0).sub (hLimit.1 0).aestronglyMeasurable).congr
    exact Eventually.of_forall fun omega => sub_sub_cancel _ _
  have hMeasure : TendstoInMeasure mu (Q M) atTop E := by
    apply tendstoInMeasure_of_tendsto_eLpNorm (p := 1) (by norm_num) (hQ M (fun t _ => hM t)) hE
    have hNorm (level : ℕ) : eLpNorm (Q M level - E) 1 mu =
        ENNReal.ofReal (∫ omega, |Q M level omega - E omega| ∂mu) := by
      rw [eLpNorm_one_eq_lintegral_enorm]
      simpa only [Real.norm_eq_abs, Pi.sub_apply] using
        (ofReal_integral_norm_eq_lintegral_enorm (hLimit.1 level)).symm
    simpa only [hNorm, Function.comp_def, ENNReal.ofReal_zero] using
      ENNReal.continuous_ofReal.continuousAt.tendsto.comp hLimit.2

steps.title: Pass through the drift perturbation
steps.text: The deterministic perturbation theorem holds on the full-measure event of continuous finite variation. Every subsequence of the stopped row squares has a further almost surely convergent subsequence. Add the vanishing pathwise drift difference and use the subsequence criterion.
steps.lean:
change TendstoInMeasure mu (Q X) atTop E
  refine (exists_seq_tendstoInMeasure_atTop_iff (hQ X hX)).2 ?_
  intro n hn
  obtain ⟨k, hk, hPath⟩ := (hMeasure.comp hn.tendsto_atTop).exists_seq_tendsto_ae
  refine ⟨k, hk, ?_⟩

units.title: Differentiate a projected coordinate field
units.statement: For any coordinate j, ambient base point x and direction u, the Fréchet derivative of the field σ_j applied to u is −(x_j u+u_j x).
assumptions: I is a finite coordinate type with decidable equality. The space is real Euclidean space on I.
Write e_j for the j-th coordinate vector and σ_j(x)=e_j−x_j x.
Both x and u are arbitrary ambient vectors.

steps.title: Differentiate the scalar and vector factors
steps.text: The coordinate functional has derivative u↦u_j and the identity has derivative u↦u. The fixed coordinate vector has derivative zero.
steps.lean:
theorem fderiv_projectedNoiseColumn_apply (j : ι) (x u : V) :
    fderiv ℝ (projectedNoiseColumn j) x u = -(x j • u + u j • x) := by
  let L : V →L[ℝ] ℝ := PiLp.proj (p := 2) (𝕜 := ℝ) (β := fun _ : ι => ℝ) j
  have h := L.hasFDerivAt.smul (hasFDerivAt_id (𝕜 := ℝ) x)
  have hF := ((hasFDerivAt_const (𝕜 := ℝ) (EuclideanSpace.single j (1 : ℝ)) x).sub h).fderiv
  change fderiv ℝ (projectedNoiseColumn j) x =
    0 - (L x • ContinuousLinearMap.id ℝ V + L.smulRight x) at hF
  rw [hF]
  simp [L]

assumptions: I is a finite coordinate type with decidable equality. The space is real Euclidean space on I.

    simp only [PiLp.norm_sq_eq_of_L2, Real.norm_eq_abs, sq_abs]
  have hTerm (j k : ι) :
      (fderiv ℝ (projectedNoiseColumn j) x (projectedNoiseColumn j x)) k =
        (2 * (x j) ^ 2) * x k - (if k = j then x j else 0) - x k := by
    rw [fderiv_projectedNoiseColumn_apply]
    simp only [projectedNoiseColumn, PiLp.neg_apply, PiLp.add_apply, PiLp.sub_apply,
      PiLp.smul_apply, smul_eq_mul, PiLp.single_apply]

units.title: The projected Hessian trace removes the radial term
units.statement: Let $w$ be a unit vector in a real Euclidean space with finite coordinate set $I$, let $(e_j)_{j\in I}$ be its coordinate basis, and let $f$ be a real ambient test function. Write $p_j=e_j-w_jw$. The trace of the ambient second Fréchet derivative evaluated on the pairs $(p_j,p_j)$ equals the ambient Laplacian minus the radial Hessian entry.
assumptions: The finite coordinate set has decidable equality. The point $w$ has Euclidean norm one.

For an analytic interpretation of the Hessian, take a twice continuously differentiable ambient test near $w$. The Lean equality itself is algebraic in the totalized Fréchet derivatives and has no smoothness premise.

steps.title: Expand the projected arguments
steps.text: Bilinearity gives two mixed radial terms and one term with two radial arguments for each coordinate.
steps.formula: D^2 f[p_j,p_j]=D^2 f[e_j,e_j]-w_jD^2 f[e_j,w]-w_jD^2 f[w,e_j]+w_j^2D^2 f[w,w].
steps.lean:
have hcolumn (j : I) :
      H (projectedNoiseColumn j w) (projectedNoiseColumn j w) =
        H (e j) (e j) - w j * H (e j) w - w j * H w (e j) + (w j) ^ 2 * H w w := by
    simp only [projectedNoiseColumn, ← EuclideanSpace.basisFun_apply, ← show
        EuclideanSpace.basisFun I ℝ = e from rfl, map_sub, map_smul,
      sub_apply, smul_apply, smul_eq_mul]
    ring

steps.title: Sum the radial contributions
steps.text: The coordinate expansion of $w$ makes each mixed sum equal to the radial Hessian entry. The unit norm makes the squared-coordinate sum one. The remaining diagonal sum is Mathlib's ambient Laplacian.
steps.lean:
let e := EuclideanSpace.basisFun I ℝ
  let H := fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ f) w
  have hrepr : (∑ j : I, w j • e j) = w := by
    simpa only [e, EuclideanSpace.basisFun_repr] using e.sum_repr w
  have happly (L : E →L[ℝ] ℝ) : (∑ j : I, w j * L (e j)) = L w := by
    calc
      _ = L (∑ j : I, w j • e j) := by simp only [map_sum, map_smul, smul_eq_mul]
      _ = L w := congrArg L hrepr
  have hright : (∑ j : I, w j * H w (e j)) = H w w := happly (H w)
  have hleft : (∑ j : I, w j * H (e j) w) = H w w := by
    calc
      _ = H (∑ j : I, w j • e j) w := by
        simp only [map_sum, sum_apply, map_smul, smul_apply, smul_eq_mul]
      _ = H w w := congrArg (fun v => H v w) hrepr
  have hsq : (∑ j : I, (w j) ^ 2) = 1 := by
    rw [← one_pow (M := ℝ) 2, ← hw]
    simp only [PiLp.norm_sq_eq_of_L2, Real.norm_eq_abs, sq_abs]

units.title: The algebraic sphere-generator identity
units.statement: Fix a unit vector \(w\in\mathbb R^I\), a real function \(f\), an ambient vector \(u\), and \(\lambda\ge0\). Interpret \(Df\) and \(D^2f\) as the total Fréchet-derivative operators used in Lean. With projected columns \(p_j=e_j-w_jw\), the displayed algebraic equality holds. For a C² ambient test near the unit sphere, it is the usual identity for the Itô generator with noise columns \(\sqrt{2\lambda}\,p_j\) and radial drift \(-\lambda(d-1)w\), where \(d=|I|\).
assumptions: The coordinate set is finite with decidable equality, $\|w\|=1$, and $\lambda\ge 0$.

The vector \(u\) is arbitrary. No smoothness hypothesis is needed for the total-derivative algebra equality. The interpretation as a classical generator requires a C² ambient test; when \(u\) is also tangent, its first-order term is the directional derivative of the restricted test.
The operators are total: Lean assigns zero to a Fréchet derivative where differentiability fails. The classical derivative interpretation is only asserted under the smooth-test qualification above.

        fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ f) w (projectedNoiseColumn j w) (projectedNoiseColumn j w) := by
    simp only [σ, map_smul, smul_apply, smul_eq_mul, ← mul_assoc,
      ← pow_two, Real.sq_sqrt (by positivity : 0 ≤ 2 * temperature)]

units.title: The terminal Itô formula for a unit-sphere diffusion
units.statement: On a positive finite horizon $[0,T]$, form the Euclidean process $X$ from its initial vector, progressive drift integral and completed Brownian coordinate integrals. Assume the process stays on the unit sphere almost surely throughout the horizon. If its drift and noise columns have the spherical coefficients below, then the increment of a twice continuously differentiable ambient test equals the time integral of the sphere generator plus the terminal value of a martingale starting at zero.
assumptions: The coordinate index set is finite with decidable equality. The ambient measure is finite. Brownian motion is standard relative to the filtration, and the filtration satisfies the usual conditions.

The initial coordinates are strongly measurable for the time-zero sigma algebra. The drift coordinates are strongly progressive with almost surely integrable time sections. The Brownian integrands are progressive and square-integrable on the horizon.

The process stays on the unit sphere for every time in the horizon on a common full-measure event. A sphere point supplies a measurable fallback for exceptional samples in the compact Itô construction. The test is $C^2$ at each sphere point.

The deterministic temperature is continuous and nonnegative on the horizon. The vector field evaluated along the process has almost surely continuous time paths. Almost surely throughout the horizon the drift is $-u_s-\lambda_s(d-1)X_s$ and the $j$th noise column is $\sqrt{2\lambda_s}(e_j-(X_s)_jX_s)$.

steps.title: Apply the compact Itô formula on the unit sphere
steps.text: The sphere is compact. On the event where all time points are on the sphere, the compact formula uses the original process and yields its two finite-variation integrals and a genuine completed martingale.

  have hK := isCompact_sphere (0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ I) 1
  obtain ⟨θ, _, hM, hM0, hIto⟩ :=
    ito_formula_compact_euclidean_at_horizon hB hT hUsual η x hx b hb hbi hK fallback f hf hSphere
  let M (s : ℝ≥0) (ω : Ω) := ∑ q : I × I,
    itoIntegralProcess (θ q) hT ((coordinateFamily hB).isBrownian q.2) hUsual s ω
  refine ⟨M, hM, hM0, ?_⟩

    (((hA i).1.stronglyAdapted s).mono (filtration.le s)).aestronglyMeasurable
  obtain ⟨_, hXc⟩ := measurable_continuousOn_euclidean_ito_rows hB hT hUsual η A hAmeas
    (fun i => (hA i).2.2.mono fun _ h => h.1)
  filter_upwards [hIto, hSphere, hDrift, hColumns, hXc, hu] with ω hω hS hbω hηω hcX hU
  let ν := TimeMeasure.upTo T

units.title: Expand a Euclidean bilinear form in coordinates
units.statement: Let H be a continuous real bilinear form on a finite-dimensional Euclidean coordinate space. Evaluating H on vectors x and y gives the sum over ordered coordinate pairs of their coordinates multiplied by the corresponding basis entry.
assumptions: The coordinate type is finite with decidable equality. The vectors eᵢ are the standard Euclidean orthonormal basis.
H is linear in each argument and continuous. The vectors x and y are arbitrary.

steps.title: Use the underlying bilinear map
steps.text: Forget continuity in each of the two linear maps. This keeps every evaluation equal.
steps.lean:
let E := EuclideanSpace ℝ I
  let e := EuclideanSpace.basisFun I ℝ
  let L : E →ₗ[ℝ] E →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ :=

units.title: Measurable slices and continuous paths of completed Euclidean Itô rows
units.statement: Construct a finite-dimensional Euclidean process from scalar completed Itô rows with almost surely continuous drift paths. Every slice up to the horizon is measurable, and almost every vector path is continuous on the horizon.
units.formula: X_t^i=A_i(t)+\sum_j\int_0^t\eta_{ij}(s)\,dB^j_s.\qquad X_t:\Omega\to\mathbb R^I\text{ measurable for each }t\le T,\quad X_\cdot(\omega)\text{ continuous on }[0,T]\text{ a.e.}
assumptions: The positive horizon is T. The sample measure is finite, the filtration satisfies the usual conditions, and the driving standard vector Brownian motion is relative to that filtration and measure.
The finite coordinate rows have progressive product-square-integrable diffusion coefficients. Their drift evaluations at each fixed time t≤T are almost-everywhere strongly measurable.
Each drift coordinate is continuous on [0,T] almost surely.

steps.title: Assemble measurable slices
steps.text: Strong adaptation gives measurable slices of each completed integral. A finite sum with the drift is almost-everywhere strongly measurable. Completeness from the usual conditions gives ordinary measurability of that slice.
steps.lean:
intro X
  let M (i : I) (j : J) := itoIntegralProcess (η i j) hT ((coordinateFamily hB).isBrownian j) hUsual
  let _ : μ.IsComplete := Measure.isComplete_iff.2
    (fun s hs => filtration.le 0 _ (hUsual.completeAt 0 s hs))
  constructor
  · intro t ht
    have hM (i : I) : AEStronglyMeasurable (fun ω => ∑ j : J, M i j t ω) μ :=
      (Finset.aestronglyMeasurable_sum Finset.univ fun j _ =>
        (((itoIntegralProcess_stronglyAdapted (η i j) hT
          ((coordinateFamily hB).isBrownian j) hUsual) t).mono
            (filtration.le t)).aestronglyMeasurable).congr
        (Eventually.of_forall fun ω => by simp only [Finset.sum_apply, M])
    have hRow (i : I) : Measurable (fun ω => A i t ω + ∑ j : J, M i j t ω) :=
      ((hAmeas i t ht).add (hM i)).aemeasurable.nullMeasurable.measurable_of_complete
    exact (MeasurableEquiv.toLp 2 (I → ℝ)).measurable.comp (measurable_pi_lambda _ hRow)

steps.title: Assemble continuous paths
steps.text: The completed integrals have continuous paths on the horizon. Intersect the finitely many drift continuity events and use continuity of each coordinate to get continuity in the Euclidean topology.
steps.formula: \bigl(\forall i,\ X_\cdot^i(\omega)\text{ continuous on }[0,T]\bigr)\Longrightarrow X_\cdot(\omega)\text{ continuous on }[0,T].
steps.lean:
· filter_upwards [ae_all_iff.2 hA] with ω hω
    have hRow (i : I) : ContinuousOn (fun t => A i t ω + ∑ j : J, M i j t ω) (Icc 0 T) :=
      (hω i).add (continuousOn_finsetSum _ fun j _ =>
        itoIntegralProcess_continuousOn (η i j) hT ((coordinateFamily hB).isBrownian j) hUsual ω)
    exact (PiLp.continuous_toLp 2 (fun _ : I => ℝ)).comp_continuousOn (continuousOn_pi.2 hRow)

units.lean_statement: The process is constructed as a Euclidean vector of the actual completed coordinate rows.
units.lean_proof: Use ordinary finite-coordinate measurability and continuity after proving the properties of each row.
units.boundary: Only continuity and measurable slices on the horizon are asserted. The drift path hypothesis is continuity.

units.title: The quadratic Taylor term converges to the diffusion Hessian contraction
units.statement: Construct a Euclidean process from completed Itô rows. Suppose it stays in compact K almost surely throughout the horizon and the scalar test is twice continuously Fréchet differentiable at every point of K. The dyadic sum of half the Hessian applied twice to the actual increment converges in measure to the time integral of half the sum of the Hessian on the diffusion columns.
assumptions: The positive horizon is T. The sample measure is finite, the filtration satisfies the usual conditions, and the driving standard vector Brownian motion is relative to that filtration and measure.
The finite coordinate rows have progressive product-square-integrable diffusion coefficients. Their drift evaluations at each fixed time t≤T are almost-everywhere strongly measurable.
Almost every drift path is continuous with bounded variation on [0,T].

The compact set K has a selected fallback point k₀. On one event of full measure, the process belongs to K at every time in [0,T]. The test is twice continuously Fréchet differentiable at each point of K.

notation.text: The process rows use the actual completed integrals. The jth diffusion column has ith coordinate ηᵢⱼ.

steps.title: Use each Hessian entry as a weight
steps.text: The Hessian is continuous on K, so the weight path is continuous on the common event. Compose each measurable slice with the measurable fallback into K, then with the continuous restricted Hessian entry. This representative equals the actual Hessian entry almost everywhere, so the actual weight slice is almost everywhere strongly measurable.
steps.lean:
intro X H σ hRange
  let t (n : ℕ) := regularGridTimes (dyadicMesh T n) (2 ^ n)
  let e := EuclideanSpace.basisFun I ℝ
  let W (q : I × I) (s : ℝ≥0) (ω : Ω) := (1 / 2 : ℝ) * H (X s ω) (e q.1) (e q.2)
  let Δ (n : ℕ) (i : Fin (2 ^ n)) (ω : Ω) := X (t n i.succ) ω - X (t n i.castSucc) ω
  let b (q : I × I) (s : ℝ≥0) (ω : Ω) :=
    ∑ j : J, (η q.1 j).process s ω * (η q.2 j).process s ω
  let F (q : I × I) (n : ℕ) (ω : Ω) :=
    ∑ i : Fin (2 ^ n), W q (t n i.castSucc) ω * (Δ n i ω q.1 * Δ n i ω q.2)
  let G (q : I × I) (ω : Ω) := ∫ s, W q s ω * b q s ω ∂(TimeMeasure.upTo T)
  have hH : ContinuousOn H K := fun x hx =>
    (((hf x hx).fderiv_right (m := 1) (by decide)).continuousAt_fderiv
      (by decide)).continuousWithinAt
  have hEntry (q : I × I) :
      ContinuousOn (fun x => (1 / 2 : ℝ) * H x (e q.1) (e q.2)) K :=
    continuousOn_const.mul ((hH.clm_apply continuousOn_const).clm_apply continuousOn_const)
  obtain ⟨hXm, hXc⟩ := measurable_continuousOn_euclidean_ito_rows
    hB hT hUsual η A hAmeas (fun i => (hA i).mono fun _ h => h.1)
  have hWm (q : I × I) (s : ℝ≥0) (hs : s ≤ T) : AEStronglyMeasurable (W q s) μ := by
    have hY := (measurable_restrictState hK.isClosed.measurableSet fallback).comp (hXm s hs)
    refine ((hEntry q).domRestrict.measurable.comp hY).aestronglyMeasurable.congr ?_
    filter_upwards [hRange] with ω hr
    change (1 / 2 : ℝ) * H (restrictState fallback (X s ω) : EuclideanSpace ℝ I)
      (e q.1) (e q.2) = W q s ω
    rw [coe_restrictState_of_mem fallback (hr s hs)]
  have hWc : ∀ᵐ ω ∂μ, ∀ q : I × I, ContinuousOn (fun s => W q s ω) (Icc 0 T) := by
    filter_upwards [hXc, hRange] with ω hω hr q
    exact (hEntry q).comp hω (fun s hs => hr s hs.2)

steps.title: Take the coordinate-pair limits
steps.text: Apply continuous-weight covariation to the corresponding completed rows, and sum over the finite set of ordered coordinate pairs.
steps.lean:
have hLim (q : I × I) : TendstoInMeasure μ (F q) atTop (G q) :=
    tendstoInMeasure_dyadic_weighted_covariation_of_ito_rows hB hT hUsual
      (η q.1) (η q.2) (A q.1) (A q.2) (W q) (hAmeas q.1) (hAmeas q.2)
      (hWm q) (hA q.1) (hA q.2) (hWc.mono fun _ h => h q)
  have ht (n : ℕ) (i : Fin (2 ^ n + 1)) : t n i ≤ T :=
    ((regularGridTimes_strictMono (dyadicMesh_pos hT n) _).monotone (Fin.le_last i)).trans_eq
      (regularDyadic_last_time T n)
  have hFm (q : I × I) (n : ℕ) : AEStronglyMeasurable (F q n) μ := by
    have hΔm (i : Fin (2 ^ n)) (j : I) : AEStronglyMeasurable (fun ω => Δ n i ω j) μ :=
      ((EuclideanSpace.proj j).continuous.measurable.comp
        ((hXm _ (ht n i.succ)).sub (hXm _ (ht n i.castSucc)))).aestronglyMeasurable
    have hCell (i : Fin (2 ^ n)) :
        AEStronglyMeasurable (fun ω => W q (t n i.castSucc) ω *
          (Δ n i ω q.1 * Δ n i ω q.2)) μ :=
      (hWm q _ (ht n i.castSucc)).mul ((hΔm i q.1).mul (hΔm i q.2))
    exact (Finset.aestronglyMeasurable_sum Finset.univ fun i _ => hCell i).congr
      (Eventually.of_forall fun ω => by simp only [F, Finset.sum_apply])

steps.title: Recover the bilinear evaluations
steps.text: The ordered coordinate expansion recovers the actual quadratic term on each increment and the Hessian on each diffusion column. Product L² gives integrable coefficient products on almost every time section. Continuity bounds the weights on each such sample's compact time interval.
steps.lean:
have hHalf (x v : EuclideanSpace ℝ I) :
      (1 / 2 : ℝ) * H x v v = ∑ q : I × I,
        ((1 / 2 : ℝ) * H x (e q.1) (e q.2)) * (v q.1 * v q.2) := by
    rw [euclidean_bilinear_eq_sum_basis (H x) v v, Finset.mul_sum, Fintype.sum_prod_type]
    apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
    intro i _
    rw [Finset.mul_sum]
    apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
    intro j _
    ring
  have hSum := tendstoInMeasure_fintype_sum hFm hLim
  refine TendstoInMeasure.congr ?_ ?_ hSum
  · intro n
    exact Eventually.of_forall fun ω => by
      change (∑ q : I × I, ∑ i : Fin (2 ^ n),
        W q (t n i.castSucc) ω * (Δ n i ω q.1 * Δ n i ω q.2)) =
        ∑ i : Fin (2 ^ n), (1 / 2 : ℝ) * H (X (t n i.castSucc) ω) (Δ n i ω) (Δ n i ω)
      rw [Finset.sum_comm]
      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
      intro i _
      exact (hHalf _ _).symm
  · have hProduct : ∀ᵐ ω ∂μ, ∀ q : I × I, ∀ j : J,
        Integrable (fun s => (η q.1 j).process s ω * (η q.2 j).process s ω)
          (TimeMeasure.upTo T) :=
      ae_all_iff.2 fun q => ae_all_iff.2 fun j =>
        ((η q.1 j).memLp.integrable_mul (η q.2 j).memLp).prod_right_ae
    filter_upwards [hProduct, hWc] with ω hp hw
    let ν := TimeMeasure.upTo T
    have hMem : ∀ᵐ s ∂ν, s ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ≥0) T :=
      (TimeMeasure.ae_mem_Ioc_zero_upTo T).mono fun _ hs => ⟨hs.1.le, hs.2⟩
    have hRest : ν.restrict (Icc 0 T) = ν := Measure.restrict_eq_self_of_ae_mem hMem
    have hInt (q : I × I) : Integrable (fun s => W q s ω * b q s ω) ν := by
      have hDensity : Integrable (fun s => b q s ω) ν := integrable_finsetSum _ (fun j _ => hp q j)
      obtain ⟨C, hC⟩ := isCompact_Icc.bddAbove_image (hw q).norm
      have hMeas : AEStronglyMeasurable (fun s => W q s ω) ν := by
        rw [← hRest]
        exact (hw q).aestronglyMeasurable measurableSet_Icc
      exact hDensity.bdd_mul hMeas (hMem.mono fun s hs => hC ⟨s, hs, rfl⟩)
    change (∑ q : I × I, ∫ s, W q s ω * b q s ω ∂ν) =
      ∫ s, (1 / 2 : ℝ) * (∑ j : J, H (X s ω) (σ j s ω) (σ j s ω)) ∂ν
    rw [← integral_finsetSum _ (fun q _ => hInt q)]
    apply integral_congr_ae
    exact Eventually.of_forall fun s => by
      simp only [b, Finset.mul_sum]
      rw [Finset.sum_comm]
      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
      intro j _
      exact (hHalf _ (σ j s ω)).symm

units.lean_proof: Use coordinate weighted covariation and exact finite summation, with the pathwise integral justified by product L² and continuity.
units.boundary: The Hessian-entry bounds use compactness of the time interval along each continuous sample path. The fallback supplies a measurable representative for the fixed-time weights.

units.title: The actual vector Itô Taylor residual vanishes
units.statement: For the completed Euclidean Itô process staying in a compact K throughout the horizon almost surely, and a scalar test twice continuously Fréchet differentiable at every point of K, the sum of second-order Taylor residuals along its dyadic increments converges in measure to zero.
assumptions: The positive horizon is T. The sample measure is finite, the filtration satisfies the usual conditions, and the driving standard vector Brownian motion is relative to that filtration and measure.
The finite coordinate rows have progressive product-square-integrable diffusion coefficients. Their drift evaluations at each fixed time t≤T are almost-everywhere strongly measurable.
The drift paths are almost surely continuous and have bounded variation on [0,T].

The compact set K has a selected fallback point k₀. On one event of full measure, the process belongs to K at every time in [0,T]. The test is twice continuously Fréchet differentiable at each point of that range.

steps.title: Place the paths in the compact range
steps.text: Clip the time at T and apply the Borel fallback outside K. On the event where the original path stays in K, the resulting K-valued path agrees with it at every dyadic grid point.
steps.lean:
intro X hRange
  let t (n : ℕ) := regularGridTimes (dyadicMesh T n) (2 ^ n)
  let Y (s : ℝ≥0) (ω : Ω) : K := restrictState fallback (X (min s T) ω)
  have ht (n : ℕ) (i : Fin (2 ^ n + 1)) : t n i ≤ T :=
    ((regularGridTimes_strictMono (dyadicMesh_pos hT n) _).monotone (Fin.le_last i)).trans_eq
      (regularDyadic_last_time T n)
  obtain ⟨hXm, hXc⟩ := measurable_continuousOn_euclidean_ito_rows
    hB hT hUsual η A hAmeas (fun i => (hA i).mono fun _ h => h.1)
  have hY (s : ℝ≥0) : Measurable (Y s) :=
    (measurable_restrictState hK.isClosed.measurableSet fallback).comp
      (hXm _ (min_le_right s T))
  have hYc : ∀ᵐ ω ∂μ, ContinuousOn (fun s => Y s ω) (Icc 0 T) := by
    filter_upwards [hXc, hRange] with ω hω hr
    apply Topology.IsEmbedding.subtypeVal.continuousOn_iff.2
    refine hω.congr fun s hs => ?_
    change (restrictState fallback (X (min s T) ω) : EuclideanSpace ℝ I) = X s ω
    rw [min_eq_left hs.2, coe_restrictState_of_mem fallback (hr s hs.2)]

steps.title: Derive the coordinate square-sum limits
steps.text: At the terminal grid point the inclusive prefix contains all fine cells. The scalar quadratic-variation theorem supplies the limit for each actual coordinate.
steps.lean:
let Q (i : I) (ω : Ω) :=
    ∑ j : J, ∫ s in Iic T, (η i j).process s ω ^ 2 ∂(TimeMeasure.upTo T)
  have hQV (j : I) : TendstoInMeasure μ (fun n ω =>
      ∑ i : Fin (2 ^ n), ((Y (t n i.succ) ω : EuclideanSpace ℝ I) j -
        (Y (t n i.castSucc) ω : EuclideanSpace ℝ I) j) ^ 2) atTop (Q j) := by
    have h := tendstoInMeasure_dyadic_prefix_sq_increments_of_ito_row hB hT hUsual
      (η j) (A j) (hAmeas j) (hA j) 0 (Fin.last (2 ^ (0 : ℕ)))
    simp only [regularDyadic_last_time] at h
    apply TendstoInMeasure.congr_left ?_ h
    intro n
    filter_upwards [hRange] with ω hr
    apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
    intro i _
    have hs : regularGridTimes (dyadicMesh T n) (2 ^ n) i.succ ≤ T := ht n i.succ
    simp only [if_pos hs, Y, min_eq_left (ht n i.succ), min_eq_left (ht n i.castSucc),
      coe_restrictState_of_mem fallback (hr _ (ht n i.succ)),
      coe_restrictState_of_mem fallback (hr _ (ht n i.castSucc))]
    rfl

steps.title: Apply the Taylor residual estimate
steps.text: Apply the existing Euclidean residual theorem using these coordinate limits. Equality of the clipped and original paths on the grids gives the claimed sum.
steps.lean:
have h := tendstoInMeasure_dyadic_sum_secondOrderRemainder_of_coordinate_qv
    hK f hf hT Y hY hYc Q hQV
  apply TendstoInMeasure.congr_left ?_ h
  intro n
  filter_upwards [hRange] with ω hr
  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
  intro i _
  change secondOrderRemainder f (Y (t n i.castSucc) ω : EuclideanSpace ℝ I)
    ((Y (t n i.succ) ω : EuclideanSpace ℝ I) - Y (t n i.castSucc) ω) = _
  dsimp only [Y]
  rw [min_eq_left (ht n i.succ), min_eq_left (ht n i.castSucc),
    coe_restrictState_of_mem fallback (hr _ (ht n i.succ)),
    coe_restrictState_of_mem fallback (hr _ (ht n i.castSucc))]

units.title: The initialized progressive drift has continuous finite-variation paths
units.statement: Let the scalar initial value be strongly measurable at time zero and the scalar drift be strongly progressive. Suppose its time section is integrable on the horizon almost surely. The initial value plus the drift integral is strongly progressive and has almost surely continuous finite-variation paths on the horizon. At every sample and time in the horizon it equals the initialized primitive computed with the fixed horizon measure.
assumptions: T is a nonnegative horizon. The sample space carries a measure and the filtration is indexed by nonnegative time.
The initial value is strongly measurable for the time-zero sigma algebra. The drift is strongly progressive, and almost every drift section is integrable against the horizon time measure.

steps.title: Use one horizon measure for the time primitive
steps.text: On the active time prefix, clipping the drift's time argument at the horizon leaves it unchanged. The two Lean integral expressions agree at every sample. Almost every sample has an integrable time section, where the expressions have their ordinary integrable-path interpretation.
steps.lean:
intro A
  have hInitial : StronglyAdapted filtration (fun _ => x) :=
    fun t => hx.mono (filtration.mono (show (0 : ℝ≥0) ≤ t from bot_le))
  have hEq (t : ℝ≥0) (ht : t ≤ T) (ω : Ω) :
      prefixIntegralProcess b t ω = prefixIntegral (fun s => b s ω) T t := by
    rw [prefixIntegralProcess_eq_fixedHorizon b ht, prefixIntegral, min_eq_left ht]
    apply integral_congr_ae
    exact Eventually.of_forall fun s => by
      by_cases hs : s < t
      · simp only [if_pos hs, min_eq_left (hs.le.trans ht)]
      · simp only [if_neg hs]
  have hAeq (t : ℝ≥0) (ht : t ≤ T) (ω : Ω) :
      A t ω = x ω + prefixIntegral (fun s => b s ω) T t :=
    congrArg (x ω + ·) (hEq t ht ω)

steps.title: Prove the path properties
steps.text: A time-zero measurable initial value gives a constant progressive process. The integral primitive is progressive, continuous along integrable paths and of bounded variation. Adding the initial value leaves each increment unchanged.
steps.lean:
refine ⟨(hInitial.isStronglyProgressive_of_continuous fun _ => continuous_const).add
    (prefixIntegralProcess_stronglyProgressive b hb), hAeq, ?_⟩
  filter_upwards [hbi] with ω hω
  let P := prefixIntegral (fun s => b s ω) T
  have hSame : EqOn (fun t => A t ω) (fun t => x ω + P t) (Icc 0 T) :=
    fun t ht => hAeq t ht.2 ω
  refine ⟨(continuous_const.add (continuous_prefixIntegral hω)).continuousOn.congr hSame, ?_⟩
  unfold BoundedVariationOn
  rw [eVariationOn.congr hSame]
  have hVar : eVariationOn (fun t => x ω + P t) (Icc 0 T) =
      eVariationOn P (Icc 0 T) := by
    unfold eVariationOn
    simp only [edist_dist, Real.dist_eq, add_sub_add_left_eq_sub]
  rw [hVar]
  exact boundedVariationOn_prefixIntegral hω

units.lean_proof: Move the drift integral to one time measure, apply the existing primitive theorems and use invariance under addition of the initial value.
units.boundary: The fixed-horizon equality holds at all samples. The continuity and variation conclusions are almost sure.

units.title: Derivative weights of the clipped Euclidean Itô process
units.statement: Take actual completed Euclidean Itô rows with strongly progressive drifts and almost surely continuous drift paths. Evaluate the test derivative on a coordinate basis vector at the time-clipped state, using the fallback when the state is outside K. The weight is strongly progressive, almost surely continuous on the horizon and bounded there by a deterministic constant.
assumptions: The horizon T is positive and the sample measure is finite. The filtration satisfies the usual conditions and the standard vector Brownian motion is relative to that filtration and measure.
The state and Brownian coordinate types are finite with decidable equality. Each diffusion entry is progressive and square-integrable in the product of sample and horizon time measures.
The compact set K has a selected fallback point k₀. On one event of full measure, the process belongs to K at every time in [0,T].
The drift coordinates are strongly progressive with almost surely continuous paths on [0,T]. The scalar test is continuously Fréchet differentiable at each point of K.

steps.title: Clip time in the progressive domain
steps.text: Clip time at T, keep the state when it belongs to K and use the selected point otherwise. The state replacement is Borel measurable, and agrees with the original state throughout the horizon almost surely.
steps.lean:
· intro t
    let _ : MeasurableSpace Ω := filtration t
    let cut (p : Iic t × Ω) : Iic t × Ω :=
      (⟨min (p.1 : ℝ≥0) T, mem_Iic.2
        ((min_le_left (p.1 : ℝ≥0) T).trans (mem_Iic.1 p.1.property))⟩, p.2)
    have hcut : Measurable cut :=
      ((measurable_subtype_coe.comp measurable_fst).min measurable_const).subtype_mk.prodMk
        measurable_snd
    have hMeas : Measurable (fun p : Iic t × Ω => X (min (p.1 : ℝ≥0) T) p.2) := by
      apply (MeasurableEquiv.toLp 2 (I → ℝ)).measurable.comp
      apply measurable_pi_lambda
      intro k
      exact ((hRow k t).comp_measurable hcut).measurable
    let Y (p : Iic t × Ω) : K := restrictState fallback (X (min (p.1 : ℝ≥0) T) p.2)
    have hY : Measurable Y := (measurable_restrictState hK.isClosed.measurableSet fallback).comp hMeas
    exact (hD.domRestrict.measurable.comp hY).stronglyMeasurable

steps.title: Compose with the derivative entry
steps.text: The derivative entry is continuous on K. Its composition is progressive and almost surely continuous on the horizon. Compactness of K bounds the absolute value uniformly over samples and times.
steps.lean:
· filter_upwards [hXc, hRange] with ω hω hr
    have hComp := hD.comp hω (fun t ht => hr t ht.2)
    refine hComp.congr fun t ht => ?_
    change D (restrictState fallback (X (min t T) ω) : EuclideanSpace ℝ I) = D (X t ω)
    rw [min_eq_left ht.2, coe_restrictState_of_mem fallback (hr t ht.2)]
  · obtain ⟨C, hC⟩ := hK.bddAbove_image hD.abs
    exact ⟨C, fun t _ ω => hC ⟨restrictState fallback (X (min t T) ω), (restrictState fallback _).property, rfl⟩⟩

units.title: The linear Itô term and its completed martingale
units.statement: Take the almost surely compact-range Euclidean process built from initialized drift time primitives and completed stochastic integrals. For a continuously Fréchet differentiable test on that range, the left-endpoint derivative sums converge in measure to the integral of the derivative applied to the drift vector plus the terminal value of a genuine martingale.
assumptions: The horizon T is positive and the sample measure is finite. The filtration satisfies the usual conditions and the standard vector Brownian motion is relative to that filtration and measure.
The state and Brownian coordinate types are finite with decidable equality. Each diffusion entry is progressive and square-integrable in the product of sample and horizon time measures.
The compact set K has a selected fallback point k₀. On one event of full measure, the process belongs to K at every time in [0,T].
Each initial coordinate is strongly measurable at time zero. Each drift coordinate is strongly progressive and has almost surely integrable time sections on the horizon.
The scalar test is continuously Fréchet differentiable at each point of K.

notation.text: The initial value, moving time primitive and completed Itô integrals define the vector process.
Each gradient entry uses the time-clipped process. The sum of the completed integrals is a martingale starting at zero.

steps.title: Take the weighted stochastic limits
steps.text: For each coordinate use the progressive bounded derivative weight. Apply the weighted stochastic-sum theorem to each actual completed integral to obtain the progressive L² product integrand.
steps.lean:
intro A X hRange
  let e := EuclideanSpace.basisFun I ℝ
  let W (i : I) (t : ℝ≥0) (ω : Ω) :=
    fderiv ℝ f (restrictState fallback (X (min t T) ω) : EuclideanSpace ℝ I) (e i)
  let N (q : I × J) := itoIntegralProcess (η q.1 q.2) hT
    ((coordinateFamily hB).isBrownian q.2) hUsual
  have hA i := initialized_drift_progressive_continuous_boundedVariation
    (fun ω => x ω i) (hx i) (b i) (hb i) (hbi i)
  have hAp (i : I) : IsStronglyProgressive filtration (A i) := (hA i).1
  have hAeq (i : I) (s : ℝ≥0) (hs : s ≤ T) (ω : Ω) :
      A i s ω = x ω i + prefixIntegral (fun r => b i r ω) T s := (hA i).2.1 s hs ω
  have hW i := euclidean_ito_gradient_weight_progressive_bounded hB hT hUsual η A hAp
    (fun j => (hA j).2.2.mono fun _ h => h.1) hK fallback f hf i hRange
  have hWp (i : I) : IsStronglyProgressive filtration (W i) := (hW i).1
  have hWc (i : I) : ∀ᵐ ω ∂μ, ContinuousOn (fun t => W i t ω) (Icc 0 T) := (hW i).2.1
  choose C hC using fun i => (hW i).2.2
  have hNoise (q : I × J) := tendstoInMeasure_dyadic_weighted_ito_sums
    (η q.1 q.2) hT ((coordinateFamily hB).isBrownian q.2) hUsual (W q.1)
    (hWp q.1) (hWc q.1) (hC q.1)
  choose θ hθ hN using hNoise

steps.title: Take the weighted drift limit
steps.text: On almost every path, the initialized drift increments are increments of the integrable time primitive. The continuous derivative weight therefore gives the ordinary weighted time-integral limit. Almost-sure convergence implies convergence in measure under the finite sample measure.
steps.lean:
have hF (i : I) : TendstoInMeasure μ (F i) atTop (D i) := by
    apply tendstoInMeasure_of_tendsto_ae (hFm i)
    filter_upwards [hWc i, hbi i] with ω hw hi
    have hlim := tendsto_dyadic_weighted_prefixIntegral_sums
      (fun s => W i s ω) (fun s => b i s ω) T hT hw hi
    refine (tendsto_congr' (Eventually.of_forall fun n => ?_)).2 hlim
    apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
    intro k _
    rw [hAeq i _ (ht n k.succ) ω, hAeq i _ (ht n k.castSucc) ω,
      add_sub_add_left_eq_sub]

steps.title: Assemble the genuine martingale
steps.text: Each weighted diffusion entry is a progressive L² integrand. Its completed stochastic integral is a martingale. Add them over the finite coordinate pairs. The sum is zero at time zero for every sample.
steps.lean:
let L (q : I × J) := itoIntegralProcess (θ q) hT
    ((coordinateFamily hB).isBrownian q.2) hUsual
  let M (t : ℝ≥0) (ω : Ω) := ∑ q : I × J, L q t ω
  have hMart (s : Finset (I × J)) : Martingale (∑ q ∈ s, L q) filtration μ := by
    induction s using Finset.induction_on with
    | empty => simpa only [Finset.sum_empty] using (martingale_zero (E := ℝ) filtration μ)
    | insert q s hq ih =>
      rw [Finset.sum_insert hq]
      exact (itoIntegralProcess_martingale (θ q) hT
        ((coordinateFamily hB).isBrownian q.2) hUsual).add ih
  have hM : Martingale M filtration μ := by
    have hEq : M = ∑ q : I × J, L q := by
      funext t ω
      simp only [M, Finset.sum_apply]
    rw [hEq]
    exact hMart Finset.univ
  have hZero (ω : Ω) : M 0 ω = 0 := by
    simp only [M, L, itoIntegralProcess_at_zero, Pi.zero_apply, Finset.sum_const_zero]
  refine ⟨θ, ?_, hM, hZero, ?_⟩
  · filter_upwards [hRange] with ω hr q t
    rw [hθ]
    dsimp only [W, e]
    rw [coe_restrictState_of_mem fallback (hr _ (min_le_right _ _))]

steps.title: Recover the derivative on the actual vectors
steps.text: The finite limits sum in measure. Expand the derivative on the actual increment in its basis, and move the finite drift sum inside the time integral using bounded weights and integrable drift sections.
steps.lean:
let t (n : ℕ) := regularGridTimes (dyadicMesh T n) (2 ^ n)
  have ht (n : ℕ) (i : Fin (2 ^ n + 1)) : t n i ≤ T :=
    ((regularGridTimes_strictMono (dyadicMesh_pos hT n) _).monotone (Fin.le_last i)).trans_eq
      (regularDyadic_last_time T n)
  let F (i : I) := weightedIncrementSum T (W i) (A i)
  let G (q : I × J) := weightedIncrementSum T (W q.1) (N q)
  let D (i : I) (ω : Ω) := ∫ s, W i s ω * b i s ω ∂(TimeMeasure.upTo T)
  have hFromProg {P : ℝ≥0 → Ω → ℝ} (h : IsStronglyProgressive filtration P)
      (s : ℝ≥0) (_ : s ≤ T) : AEStronglyMeasurable (P s) μ :=
    ((h.stronglyAdapted s).mono (filtration.le s)).aestronglyMeasurable
  have hFm (i : I) (n : ℕ) : AEStronglyMeasurable (F i n) μ :=
    aestronglyMeasurable_weightedIncrementSum hT (hFromProg (hWp i)) (hFromProg (hAp i)) n
  have hGm (q : I × J) (n : ℕ) : AEStronglyMeasurable (G q n) μ :=
    aestronglyMeasurable_weightedIncrementSum hT (hFromProg (hWp q.1)) (fun s _ =>
      ((itoIntegralProcess_stronglyAdapted (η q.1 q.2) hT ((coordinateFamily hB).isBrownian q.2)
        hUsual s).mono (filtration.le s)).aestronglyMeasurable) n
  have hF (i : I) : TendstoInMeasure μ (F i) atTop (D i) := by
    apply tendstoInMeasure_of_tendsto_ae (hFm i)
    filter_upwards [hWc i, hbi i] with ω hw hi
    have hlim := tendsto_dyadic_weighted_prefixIntegral_sums
      (fun s => W i s ω) (fun s => b i s ω) T hT hw hi
    refine (tendsto_congr' (Eventually.of_forall fun n => ?_)).2 hlim
    apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
    intro k _
    rw [hAeq i _ (ht n k.succ) ω, hAeq i _ (ht n k.castSucc) ω,
      add_sub_add_left_eq_sub]
  have hG (q : I × J) : TendstoInMeasure μ (G q) atTop (L q T) := hN q
  have hSum : TendstoInMeasure μ
      (fun n ω => (∑ i : I, F i n ω) + ∑ q : I × J, G q n ω) atTop
      (fun ω => (∑ i : I, D i ω) + M T ω) := by
    let S : I ⊕ (I × J) → ℕ → Ω → ℝ := Sum.elim F G
    let Q : I ⊕ (I × J) → Ω → ℝ := Sum.elim D (fun q => L q T)
    have hS (k : I ⊕ (I × J)) (n : ℕ) : AEStronglyMeasurable (S k n) μ := by
      cases k with
      | inl i => exact hFm i n
      | inr q => exact hGm q n
    have hQ (k : I ⊕ (I × J)) : TendstoInMeasure μ (S k) atTop (Q k) := by
      cases k with
      | inl i => exact hF i
      | inr q => exact hG q
    simpa only [S, Q, Fintype.sum_sum_type, Sum.elim_inl, Sum.elim_inr, M] using
      tendstoInMeasure_fintype_sum hS hQ
  have hExpand (l : EuclideanSpace ℝ I →L[ℝ] ℝ) (v : EuclideanSpace ℝ I) :
      l v = ∑ i : I, l (e i) * v i := by
    have h : (∑ i : I, v i • e i) = v := by
      simpa only [e, EuclideanSpace.basisFun_repr] using e.sum_repr v
    calc
      l v = l (∑ i : I, v i • e i) := congrArg l h.symm
      _ = _ := by simp only [map_sum, map_smul, smul_eq_mul, mul_comm]
  refine TendstoInMeasure.congr ?_ ?_ hSum
  · intro n
    filter_upwards [hRange] with ω hr
    simp only [F, G, weightedIncrementSum, Fintype.sum_prod_type]
    change ((∑ i : I, ∑ k : Fin (2 ^ n), W i (t n k.castSucc) ω *
      (A i (t n k.succ) ω - A i (t n k.castSucc) ω)) +
      ∑ i : I, ∑ j : J, ∑ k : Fin (2 ^ n), W i (t n k.castSucc) ω *
        (N (i, j) (t n k.succ) ω - N (i, j) (t n k.castSucc) ω)) =
      ∑ k : Fin (2 ^ n), fderiv ℝ f (X (t n k.castSucc) ω)
        (X (t n k.succ) ω - X (t n k.castSucc) ω)
    have hSwap (i : I) : (∑ j : J, ∑ k : Fin (2 ^ n), W i (t n k.castSucc) ω *
        (N (i, j) (t n k.succ) ω - N (i, j) (t n k.castSucc) ω)) =
        ∑ k : Fin (2 ^ n), ∑ j : J, W i (t n k.castSucc) ω *
          (N (i, j) (t n k.succ) ω - N (i, j) (t n k.castSucc) ω) := Finset.sum_comm
    simp_rw [hSwap]
    simp_rw [← Finset.sum_add_distrib]
    rw [Finset.sum_comm]
    apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
    intro k _
    rw [hExpand]
    apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
    intro i _
    rw [← Finset.mul_sum, ← mul_add, Finset.sum_sub_distrib]
    simp only [W, min_eq_left (ht n k.castSucc),
      coe_restrictState_of_mem fallback (hr _ (ht n k.castSucc)), X, PiLp.sub_apply, N]
    ring
  · filter_upwards [ae_all_iff.2 hWc, ae_all_iff.2 hbi, hRange] with ω hw hi hr
    let ν := TimeMeasure.upTo T
    have hMem : ∀ᵐ s ∂ν, s ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ≥0) T :=
      (TimeMeasure.ae_mem_Ioc_zero_upTo T).mono fun _ hs => ⟨hs.1.le, hs.2⟩
    have hRest : ν.restrict (Icc 0 T) = ν := Measure.restrict_eq_self_of_ae_mem hMem
    have hInt (i : I) : Integrable (fun s => W i s ω * b i s ω) ν := by
      have hm : AEStronglyMeasurable (fun s => W i s ω) ν := by
        rw [← hRest]
        exact (hw i).aestronglyMeasurable measurableSet_Icc
      exact (hi i).bdd_mul hm (hMem.mono fun s hs => by
        simpa only [Real.norm_eq_abs] using hC i s hs.2 ω)
    apply congrArg (· + M T ω)
    change (∑ i : I, ∫ s, W i s ω * b i s ω ∂ν) =
      ∫ s, fderiv ℝ f (X s ω) (WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i : I => b i s ω)) ∂ν
    rw [← integral_finsetSum _ (fun i _ => hInt i)]
    apply integral_congr_ae
    filter_upwards [hMem] with s hs
    rw [hExpand]
    simp only [W, min_eq_left hs.2, coe_restrictState_of_mem fallback (hr s hs.2)]

units.boundary: This convergence identifies the first-order Taylor term. The quadratic term and the residual enter the full identity separately.

units.title: Smooth Itô formula at the terminal horizon
units.statement: For the actual Euclidean process built from initialized progressive time integrals and completed stochastic integrals, suppose its path lies in a compact K throughout the horizon almost surely. A scalar test twice continuously Fréchet differentiable at every point of K satisfies the terminal Itô identity almost surely, with the genuine completed derivative martingale starting at zero.
assumptions: The horizon T is positive and the sample measure is finite. The filtration satisfies the usual conditions and the standard vector Brownian motion is relative to that filtration and measure.
The state and Brownian coordinate types are finite with decidable equality. Each diffusion entry is progressive and square-integrable in the product of sample and horizon time measures.
The compact set K has a selected fallback point k₀. On one event of full measure, the process belongs to K at every time in [0,T].
Each initial coordinate is strongly measurable at time zero. Each drift coordinate is strongly progressive and has almost surely integrable time sections on the horizon.
The scalar test is twice continuously Fréchet differentiable at every point of K.

notation.text: The jth diffusion column has ith coordinate ηᵢⱼ.
The derivative integrands are specified by the theorem and are progressively square-integrable. The completed sum has M₀=0 for every sample.

steps.title: Use the three actual Taylor limits
steps.text: The initialized drift supplies continuity, variation and measurability. Apply the first-order limit with its martingale, the half-Hessian limit and the Taylor residual limit. Choose one subsequence on which all three limits hold almost everywhere.
steps.lean:
intro A X v σ H hRange
  have hf1 (y : EuclideanSpace ℝ I) (hy : y ∈ K) : ContDiffAt ℝ 1 f y :=
    (hf y hy).of_le (by decide)
  obtain ⟨θ, hθ, hM, h0, hLinear⟩ :=
    tendstoInMeasure_dyadic_linear_ito_term hB hT hUsual η x hx b hb hbi hK fallback f hf1 hRange
  let M (s : ℝ≥0) (ω : Ω) := ∑ q : I × J,
    itoIntegralProcess (θ q) hT ((coordinateFamily hB).isBrownian q.2) hUsual s ω
  refine ⟨θ, hθ, hM, h0, ?_⟩
  have hDrift (i : I) := initialized_drift_progressive_continuous_boundedVariation
    (fun ω => x ω i) (hx i) (b i) (hb i) (hbi i)
  have hAmeas (i : I) (s : ℝ≥0) (_ : s ≤ T) : AEStronglyMeasurable (A i s) μ :=
    (((hDrift i).1.stronglyAdapted s).mono (filtration.le s)).aestronglyMeasurable
  have hAc (i : I) : ∀ᵐ ω ∂μ, ContinuousOn (fun s => A i s ω) (Icc 0 T) ∧
      BoundedVariationOn (fun s => A i s ω) (Icc 0 T) := (hDrift i).2.2
  have hHessian := tendstoInMeasure_dyadic_half_hessian_increments hB hT hUsual η A
    hAmeas hAc hK fallback f hf hRange
  have hRemainder := tendstoInMeasure_dyadic_actual_ito_taylor_remainder hB hT hUsual η A
    hAmeas hAc hK fallback f hf hRange
  let t (n : ℕ) := regularGridTimes (dyadicMesh T n) (2 ^ n)
  let Δ (n : ℕ) (i : Fin (2 ^ n)) (ω : Ω) := X (t n i.succ) ω - X (t n i.castSucc) ω
  let L (n : ℕ) (ω : Ω) := ∑ i : Fin (2 ^ n), fderiv ℝ f (X (t n i.castSucc) ω) (Δ n i ω)
  let Q (n : ℕ) (ω : Ω) := ∑ i : Fin (2 ^ n),
    (1 / 2 : ℝ) * H (X (t n i.castSucc) ω) (Δ n i ω) (Δ n i ω)
  let R (n : ℕ) (ω : Ω) := ∑ i : Fin (2 ^ n), secondOrderRemainder f (X (t n i.castSucc) ω) (Δ n i ω)
  let D (ω : Ω) := ∫ s, fderiv ℝ f (X s ω) (v s ω) ∂(TimeMeasure.upTo T)
  let E (ω : Ω) := ∫ s, (1 / 2 : ℝ) * (∑ j : J, H (X s ω) (σ j s ω) (σ j s ω))
    ∂(TimeMeasure.upTo T)
  let F : Option Bool → ℕ → Ω → ℝ
    | none => L
    | some false => Q
    | some true => R
  let G : Option Bool → Ω → ℝ
    | none => fun ω => D ω + M T ω
    | some false => E
    | some true => fun _ => 0
  have hData (k : Option Bool) : TendstoInMeasure μ (F k) atTop (G k) := by
    cases k with
    | none => exact hLinear
    | some b =>
      cases b
      · exact hHessian
      · exact hRemainder
  obtain ⟨k, _, hPath⟩ := exists_seq_tendsto_ae_of_countable hData
  filter_upwards [hPath] with ω hω

steps.title: Telescope exactly at each dyadic level
steps.text: On each cell, adding the linear term, half the Hessian term and the signed remainder gives the test increment exactly. These increments telescope between the first and last grid points.
steps.lean:
have hTel (n : ℕ) : L n ω + Q n ω + R n ω = f (X T ω) - f (X 0 ω) := by
    dsimp only [L, Q, R]
    rw [← Finset.sum_add_distrib, ← Finset.sum_add_distrib]
    calc
      _ = ∑ i : Fin (2 ^ n), (f (X (t n i.succ) ω) - f (X (t n i.castSucc) ω)) := by
        apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
        intro i _
        have hInc : X (t n i.castSucc) ω + Δ n i ω = X (t n i.succ) ω := by
          dsimp only [Δ]
          abel
        rw [secondOrderRemainder, hInc, smul_eq_mul]
        dsimp only [H]
        ring
      _ = _ := by
        let g (i : Fin (2 ^ n + 1)) := f (X (t n i) ω)
        change (∑ i : Fin (2 ^ n), (g i.succ - g i.castSucc)) = _
        have hFirst : t n 0 = 0 := by simp [t, regularGridTimes]
        have hLast : t n (Fin.last (2 ^ n)) = T := regularDyadic_last_time T n
        rw [← hFirst, ← hLast, Finset.sum_sub_distrib]
        change (∑ i : Fin (2 ^ n), g i.succ) - (∑ i : Fin (2 ^ n), g i.castSucc) =
          g (Fin.last (2 ^ n)) - g 0
        linarith [Fin.sum_univ_succ g, Fin.sum_univ_castSucc g]

steps.title: Identify the almost-sure limit
steps.text: The sum is the same for every grid level. On the event where the three terms converge, uniqueness of the limit gives the identity.
steps.lean:
have hLim : Tendsto (fun n => L (k n) ω + Q (k n) ω + R (k n) ω) atTop
      (𝓝 ((D ω + M T ω) + E ω + 0)) :=
    ((hω none).add (hω (some false))).add (hω (some true))
  have hConst : Tendsto (fun n => L (k n) ω + Q (k n) ω + R (k n) ω) atTop
      (𝓝 (f (X T ω) - f (X 0 ω))) :=
    (tendsto_congr' (Eventually.of_forall fun n => hTel (k n))).2 tendsto_const_nhds
  change f (X T ω) - f (X 0 ω) = D ω + E ω + M T ω
  rw [tendsto_nhds_unique hConst hLim]
  ring
