units.title: Weighted mixed products of Brownian increments
units.statement: For distinct coordinates of the same Euclidean Brownian motion, the predictably weighted sum of their simultaneous increment products vanishes in mean square on dyadic grids.
assumptions: One Euclidean Brownian driver and its given filtration.
Distinct coordinates and square-integrable weights measurable at each left endpoint.
One uniform second-moment bound on the weights. T may be zero.

steps.title: Read the mean-square conclusion of the mixed-increment theorem
steps.text: The preceding theorem proves both square integrability at each dyadic level and the asserted vanishing second moment. Select its second conclusion; no extra moment or independence assumption is introduced.
steps.lean:
theorem tendsto_integral_dyadic_predictable_mixed_increment_sum_sq
    {Omega kappa : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Omega] [Fintype kappa] [DecidableEq kappa]
    {filtration : Filtration ℝ≥0 (inferInstance : MeasurableSpace Omega)} {mu : Measure Omega}
    {B : ℝ≥0 → Omega → EuclideanSpace ℝ kappa}
    (hB : IsStandardBrownianMotionWithFiltration B filtration mu)
    {j k : kappa} (hjk : j ≠ k) (T : ℝ≥0)
    (weight : (level : ℕ) → Fin (2 ^ level) → Omega → ℝ)
    (hAdapted : ∀ level i,
      StronglyMeasurable[filtration
        (regularGridTimes (dyadicMesh T level) (2 ^ level) i.castSucc)] (weight level i))
    (hWeight : ∀ level i, MemLp (weight level i) 2 mu)
    (C : ℝ) (hC : ∀ level i, (∫ omega, (weight level i omega)^2 ∂mu) ≤ C) :
    Tendsto (fun level =>
      let times := regularGridTimes (dyadicMesh T level) (2 ^ level)
      ∫ omega, (∑ i, weight level i omega *
        ((B (times i.succ) omega j - B (times i.castSucc) omega j) *
          (B (times i.succ) omega k - B (times i.castSucc) omega k)))^2 ∂mu)
      atTop (nhds 0) :=
  (dyadic_predictable_mixed_increment_sum_L2 hB hjk T weight hAdapted hWeight C hC).2

units.title: The weak forward equation from a martingale balance
units.statement: Let P be a probability law on a measurable sample space and E a compact second-countable topological space with its Borel sigma algebra. Let X be a jointly measurable process on nonnegative time with values in E and continuous paths almost surely. Let g be a continuous real test, A a jointly continuous real field on time and state, and M a real martingale for a filtration on nonnegative time under P. Suppose that for each fixed t≥0, the increment \(g(X_t)−g(X_0)\) equals the time integral of \(A(v,X_v)\) plus \(M_t−M_0\) almost surely. At every s≥0, the expectation of \(g(X_t)\) has derivative within the nonnegative half-line equal to the expectation of \(A(s,X_s)\).
assumptions: The time parameter is nonnegative and the state space is compact, second-countable and Borel. The process is jointly measurable.
A single almost-sure path continuity statement holds for the whole nonnegative time domain.
The real test g is continuous, and the drift field A is jointly continuous in time and state.
M is a real martingale for the stated filtration and law. For each fixed t, the displayed pathwise increment identity holds almost surely at that t.

steps.title: Center the martingale increment
steps.text: Both martingale values are integrable and have the same expectation. Their difference therefore provides an integrable centered residual in the stated path balance.
steps.lean:
intro t
  have hMi := hM.integrable t
  have hM0 := hM.integrable 0

units.title: When the two Itô generator terms are time integrable
units.statement: Let $v$ be the vector with the given scalar drift rows and $\sigma_j$ the vector with the $j$th given noise column. Both generator terms displayed below are integrable in time for almost every sample.
assumptions: The sample measure $\mu$ is finite. Time is nonnegative and the fixed horizon $T$ may equal zero. The coordinate set $I$ and noise index set $J$ are finite, with decidable equality on $I$. The filtration is indexed by nonnegative real time.

Each drift coordinate has integrable time sections for $\mu$-almost every sample. Each noise entry is a strongly progressive integrand with $L^2(\mu\otimes\ell_T)$ membership, where $\ell_T=\mathrm{Leb}|_{[0,T]}$.
The Euclidean path $X$ is almost surely continuous on $[0,T]$ and almost surely stays in the set $K$ at all horizon times. The ambient test $f$ is $C^2$ at each point of $K$.

    ae_all_iff.2 fun i => ae_all_iff.2 fun k => ae_all_iff.2 fun j =>
      ((η i j).memLp.integrable_mul (η k j).memLp).prod_right_ae

  have hH : ContinuousOn H (Icc 0 T) :=

units.title: Terminal Itô formula for sphere-valued integrated rows
units.statement: For the initialized row process $X$ specified below, the generator is $\mathcal L_t f(X_t)$ with field value $u_t$ at the sample. There exists a real martingale $M$ for the given filtration with $M_0(\omega)=0$ at every sample, and the terminal increment has the displayed almost-sure decomposition.
assumptions: The sample measure is finite. A standard Euclidean Brownian motion is given relative to a filtration satisfying the usual conditions. The finite coordinate set $I$ has decidable equality and the horizon $T$ is strictly positive.

Each initialized row is $x_i+\int_0^t b_i(s)\,ds+\sum_j\int_0^t\eta_{ij}(s)\,dB_j(s)$ using the library's completed stochastic integral on that horizon. The initial coordinates are strongly measurable in $\mathcal F_0$. Each drift coordinate is strongly progressive with an integrable time section almost surely. Each noise entry is a strongly progressive product-space $L^2$ integrand.

On full-measure horizon events, the row process stays on the unit sphere at every $t\le T$ and the coefficients are $b(t)=-u_t-\lambda(t)(|I|-1)X_t$ and $\sigma_j(t)=\sqrt{2\lambda(t)}P_{X_t}e_j$ at all such times and all $j$. Here $P_we_j=e_j-w_jw$.
The real deterministic temperature is pointwise nonnegative up to $T$. The ambient test is $C^2$ at every sphere point, and a sphere point is supplied for the compact-range construction.
The ambient sphere Laplacian is $\Delta_S^{\mathrm{ext}}f(w)=\sum_j D^2f(w)[P_we_j,P_we_j]-(|I|-1)Df(w)[w]$.

steps.title: Apply Itô to the integrated rows
steps.text: The existing compact-range Itô formula gives a first-order term, the quadratic term with factor one half, and a zero-start martingale.
steps.lean:
have hK := isCompact_sphere (0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ I) 1
  obtain ⟨θ, _, hM, hM0, hIto⟩ :=
    ito_formula_compact_euclidean_at_horizon hB hT hUsual η x hx b hb hbi hK fallback f hf hSphere
  let M (s : ℝ≥0) (ω : Ω) := ∑ q : I × I,
    itoIntegralProcess (θ q) hT ((coordinateFamily hB).isBrownian q.2) hUsual s ω
  refine ⟨M, hM, hM0, ?_⟩
  have hA (i : I) := initialized_drift_progressive_continuous_boundedVariation
    (fun ω => x ω i) (hx i) (b i) (hb i) (hbi i)
  have hAmeas (i : I) (s : ℝ≥0) (_ : s ≤ T) : AEStronglyMeasurable (A i s) μ :=
    (((hA i).1.stronglyAdapted s).mono (filtration.le s)).aestronglyMeasurable
  obtain ⟨_, hXc⟩ := measurable_continuousOn_euclidean_ito_rows hB hT hUsual η A hAmeas
    (fun i => (hA i).2.2.mono fun _ h => h.1)
steps.detail: Obtain the initialized drift regularity and apply the compact Euclidean formula.

steps.title: Add the drift and Hessian integrals
steps.text: The row integrability theorem makes both terms integrable on the same almost-sure horizon event. The projected column identity combines their integrands.
steps.lean:
have hInt := ae_integrable_euclidean_generator_terms η b hbi X hXc hSphere f hf
  filter_upwards [hIto, hSphere, hDrift, hColumns, hInt] with ω hω hS hbω hηω hint
  let ν := TimeMeasure.upTo T
  let v (s : ℝ≥0) := WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => b i s ω)
  let σ (j : I) (s : ℝ≥0) := WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => (η i j).process s ω)
  let D (s : ℝ≥0) := fderiv ℝ f (X s ω) (v s)
  let Q (s : ℝ≥0) := (1 / 2 : ℝ) * ∑ j : I,
    fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ f) (X s ω) (σ j s) (σ j s)
  have hD : Integrable D ν := hint.1
  have hQ : Integrable Q ν := hint.2
  change f (X T ω) - f (X 0 ω) =
    (∫ s, D s ∂ν) + (∫ s, Q s ∂ν) + M T ω at hω
  rw [hω, ← integral_add hD hQ]
  apply congrArg (· + M T ω)
  apply integral_congr_ae
  filter_upwards [TimeMeasure.ae_le_terminal T] with s hs
  have hUnit : ‖X s ω‖ = 1 := mem_sphere_zero_iff_norm.1 (hS s hs)
  simp only [D, Q, v, σ, hbω s hs, hηω s hs]
  exact ito_generator_eq_sphereLaplacian f hUnit (u s ω) (hNonneg s hs)

units.title: Weak marginal evolution from sphere diffusion rows
units.statement: Use the actual laws $\rho_t=(X_t)_\#P$. Put $F(t)=\int f(w)\,d\rho_{t^+}(w)$ and $B(t)=\int\mathcal L_{t^+}f(w)\,d\rho_{t^+}(w)$. The generator average $B$ is locally integrable on the real line. The expectation $F$ is absolutely continuous on each finite nonnegative interval and has the signed two-time balance and almost-everywhere derivative below.
assumptions: The sample space carries a probability measure $P$, a filtration indexed by nonnegative real time satisfying the usual conditions, and a standard Euclidean Brownian motion relative to that filtration. The coordinate set $I$ is finite with decidable equality.
The process $X$ is jointly measurable and takes values in the Euclidean unit sphere $S$. The field $u(t,w)$ is jointly continuous and ambient-vector-valued.
The deterministic temperature $\lambda$ is Borel measurable, nonnegative at each time, and bounded pointwise on each finite horizon. The ambient real test $f$ is $C^2$ at every point of $S$.

For each strictly positive horizon, supply initialized coordinates strongly measurable in $\mathcal F_0$, strongly progressive drift rows with almost-sure integrable sections, and strongly progressive product-$L^2$ noise rows. Their initialized integral equation agrees with $X$ almost surely simultaneously for all horizon times. On the corresponding full-measure events the drift is $-u(t,X_t)-\lambda(t)(|I|-1)X_t$ and each noise column is $\sqrt{2\lambda(t)}P_{X_t}e_j$ throughout the horizon.
Here $P_we_j=e_j-w_jw$ and $t^+=\max(t,0)$. Both endpoints in the signed balance are arbitrary nonnegative times.
The sphere generator is $\mathcal L_t f(w)=-Df(w)[u(t,w)]+\lambda(t)\Delta_S^{\mathrm{ext}}f(w)$, with $\Delta_S^{\mathrm{ext}}f(w)=\sum_j D^2f(w)[P_we_j,P_we_j]-(|I|-1)Df(w)[w]$.

steps.title: Bound the generator on compact horizons
steps.text: The derivative weights and continuous field give uniform bounds on the compact state and time sets. Multiply the Laplacian bound by the horizon bound for the Borel temperature.

  have hDriftCont : Continuous drift := ((hD.comp continuous_snd).clm_apply hu).neg
  have hA : Measurable (Function.uncurry A) :=
    hDriftCont.measurable.add ((hTemperature.comp measurable_fst).mul
      (hLap.measurable.comp measurable_snd))
  have hBound (T : ℝ≥0) : ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ t ≤ T, ∀ w, ‖A t w‖ ≤ C := by
    have hcompact : IsCompact (Icc (0 : ℝ≥0) T ×ˢ (univ : Set S)) :=
      isCompact_Icc.prod isCompact_univ
    obtain ⟨C₁, h₁⟩ := hcompact.bddAbove_image hDriftCont.norm.continuousOn
    obtain ⟨C₂, h₂⟩ := (isCompact_univ (X := S)).bddAbove_image hLap.norm.continuousOn
    obtain ⟨C₃, h₃⟩ := hTemperatureBound T
    have h₃pos : 0 ≤ C₃ := (norm_nonneg _).trans (h₃ 0 bot_le)
    refine ⟨C₁ + C₃ * C₂, fun t ht w => ?_⟩
    calc
      ‖A t w‖ ≤ ‖drift (t, w)‖ + ‖temperature t‖ * ‖sphereLaplacian f (w : E)‖ := by
        dsimp only [A, drift]
        simpa only [norm_mul] using norm_add_le
          (-fderiv ℝ f (w : E) (u t w)) (temperature t * sphereLaplacian f (w : E))
      _ ≤ C₁ + C₃ * C₂ :=
        add_le_add (h₁ ⟨(t,w), ⟨⟨bot_le, ht⟩, mem_univ w⟩, rfl⟩)
          (mul_le_mul (h₃ t ht) (h₂ ⟨w, mem_univ w, rfl⟩) (norm_nonneg _) h₃pos)

steps.title: Center the terminal increment
steps.text: The horizon-specific rows satisfy the sphere Itô formula. The martingale has expectation zero at the terminal time because it starts at zero. Convert the restricted nonnegative time integral into the real interval integral.

obtain ⟨M, hM, hM0, hIto⟩ := ito_formula_sphere_of_integrated_rows hB hPos hUsual η x hx b hb hbi
    (X 0 ω₀) f hf (fun t ω => u t (X t ω)) temperature
    (fun t _ => hNonneg t) hSphere hDrift hColumns

        integral_upTo_restrict_Ioc_eq_real (fun t => A t (X t ω)) (show 0 ≤ T from bot_le) le_rfl]

assumptions: The filtration is indexed by nonnegative real time. The sample measure is finite, and the coordinate set $I$ is finite with decidable equality.

steps.text: The sphere projection has continuous coordinates, and the square root of the Borel temperature factor is Borel.

  let c₀ (w : S) : ℝ := (projectedNoiseColumn j (w : E)) i
  let c (q : ℝ≥0 × S) : ℝ := Real.sqrt (2 * temperature q.1) * c₀ q.2
  have hState : Continuous (fun w : S => (w : E)) := continuous_subtype_val
  have hProjected : Continuous (fun w : S => projectedNoiseColumn j (w : E)) :=
    continuous_const.sub (((L j).continuous.comp hState).smul hState)
  have hC₀ : Continuous c₀ := (L i).continuous.comp hProjected
  have hRoot : Measurable (fun q : ℝ≥0 × S => Real.sqrt (2 * temperature q.1)) :=

units.title: Centered terminal residuals give a weak forward derivative
units.statement: Let $X_t$ be a jointly measurable process taking values in a compact state space, with almost surely continuous paths. Let $g$ be a continuous real test and $A(t,x)$ a jointly continuous real drift observable. If at each horizon the increment of $g(X_t)$ equals the time integral of $A(s,X_s)$ plus an integrable centered residual almost surely, then the time derivative of the expectation is the expectation of $A(t,X_t)$. This is the ordinary derivative at positive times and the right derivative at time zero.
assumptions: The sample space carries a probability measure. Time is nonnegative. The state space is compact and second countable, with its Borel measurable structure.
The process is jointly measurable and almost surely continuous in time. The test is continuous and the drift observable is jointly continuous.
For each nonnegative horizon there is a possibly horizon-dependent integrable real residual with mean zero. The pathwise balance with that residual holds almost surely.

steps.title: Take expectations in the horizon identity
steps.text: Joint continuity bounds the drift observable on each compact time-by-state set. Fubini and the centered residual give the integral balance of expected values.

    let q := volume.restrict (uIoc (0 : ℝ) (t : ℝ))
    have : IsFiniteMeasure q := by
      apply isFiniteMeasure_restrict.2
      rw [Real.volume_uIoc]
      exact ENNReal.ofReal_ne_top
    have hcompact : IsCompact (uIcc (0 : ℝ) (t : ℝ) ×ˢ (univ : Set E)) :=
      isCompact_uIcc.prod isCompact_univ
    obtain ⟨C, hC⟩ := hcompact.bddAbove_image hA'.norm.continuousOn
    have hd : Integrable (Function.uncurry fun v ω => A' v (Y v ω)) (q.prod (P : Measure Ω)) := by
      have hm : Measurable (Function.uncurry fun v ω => A' v (Y v ω)) :=
        hA'.measurable.comp (measurable_fst.prodMk hYpair)
      apply Integrable.of_bound hm.aestronglyMeasurable C
      have hq : ∀ᵐ v ∂q, v ∈ uIoc (0 : ℝ) (t : ℝ) := ae_restrict_mem measurableSet_uIoc
      filter_upwards [Measure.quasiMeasurePreserving_fst.ae hq] with p hp
      exact hC ⟨(p.1, Y p.1 p.2), ⟨uIoc_subset_uIcc hp, mem_univ _⟩, rfl⟩
    obtain ⟨Z, hZi, hmean, hZ⟩ := hbalance t
    have hinc : ∀ᵐ ω ∂(P : Measure Ω),
        g (Y t ω) - g (Y 0 ω) =
          (∫ v in (0 : ℝ)..(t : ℝ), A' v (Y v ω)) + Z ω := by
      simpa [Y, A'] using hZ
    have h := weak_integral_balance_of_centered_increment P Y hY hg.measurable hAsection
      0 (t : ℝ) (hgi 0) (hgi t) hd hZi hmean hinc
    rw [hmap _ hg.measurable, hmap _ hg.measurable] at h
    exact eq_add_of_sub_eq' h

steps.text: Almost surely continuous paths give weakly continuous marginal laws. Joint continuity of the observable on compact sets gives a continuous expected drift. The fundamental theorem of calculus differentiates the balance.

    have h := hF t.toNNReal

  exact hderiv

units.title: The integrated sphere diffusion satisfies the weak forward equation
units.statement: Let $X_t$ be a jointly measurable unit-sphere-valued process with almost surely continuous paths. Suppose its actual coordinates satisfy the specified integrated Brownian equation at every positive finite horizon with projected noise and its radial drift. For each twice continuously differentiable ambient test, the derivative of its expectation is the expected spherical generator. This is the ordinary derivative at positive times and the right derivative at time zero.
assumptions: The coordinate set is finite with decidable equality. The ambient measure is a probability measure. Standard vector Brownian motion is relative to the filtration, which satisfies the usual conditions.

The sphere-valued process is jointly measurable and its paths are almost surely continuous. The field $u(t,w)$ is jointly continuous and takes ambient vector values. The deterministic temperature is continuous and nonnegative.

At each positive horizon, the integrated rows use initial coordinates strongly measurable for the time-zero filtration σ-algebra, strongly progressive drift with almost surely integrable time sections, and progressive product-square-integrable Brownian integrands. The Euclidean representation agrees with the supplied sphere process at all times in that horizon almost surely.
Almost surely throughout each horizon, the drift is $-u(t,X_t)-\lambda_t(d-1)X_t$ and the $j$th noise column is $\sqrt{2\lambda_t}(e_j-(X_t)_jX_t)$. The test is $C^2$ at every sphere point.

steps.title: Obtain a centered increment on each horizon
steps.text: On each positive horizon, the integrated Euclidean rows agree with the supplied sphere process throughout the horizon on a common full-measure event. Transfer the terminal Itô identity along this agreement. Its zero-start martingale has an integrable terminal value with mean zero. At horizon zero take the residual to be zero.

      Eventually.of_forall fun _ => by simp⟩
  have hPos : 0 < T := bot_lt_iff_ne_bot.mpr hT
  obtain ⟨η, x, b, hx, hb, hbi, hEq, hbEq, hηEq⟩ := hEquation T hPos
  let Y (t : ℝ≥0) (ω : Ω) : E := WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i : I =>
    x ω i + prefixIntegralProcess (b i) t ω +
      ∑ j : I, itoIntegralProcess (η i j) hPos ((coordinateFamily hB).isBrownian j) hUsual t ω)
  have hYEq : ∀ᵐ ω ∂(P : Measure Ω), ∀ t ≤ T, Y t ω = (X t ω : E) := hEq
  have hSphere : ∀ᵐ ω ∂(P : Measure Ω), ∀ t ≤ T, Y t ω ∈ S :=
    hYEq.mono fun ω heq t ht => (heq t ht).symm ▸ (X t ω).property
  have hU : ∀ᵐ ω ∂(P : Measure Ω), ContinuousOn (fun t => u t (X t ω)) (Icc 0 T) :=
    hPaths.mono fun _ hω => (hu.comp (continuous_id.prodMk hω)).continuousOn
  have hDrift : ∀ᵐ ω ∂(P : Measure Ω), ∀ t ≤ T, WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => b i t ω) =

    filter_upwards [hYEq, hbEq] with ω heq hcoeff t ht

  obtain ⟨M, hM, hM0, hIto⟩ := ito_formula_sphere_at_horizon hB hPos hUsual η x hx b hb hbi

units.title: The second-order Taylor residual
units.statement: For any map f:E→F and points x,v∈E, define the residual after removing the constant, linear and quadratic terms by the displayed formula.
assumptions: Let E and F be real normed vector spaces. Derivatives are real Fréchet derivatives; D²f(x) is viewed as a continuous bilinear map.

steps.title: Subtract the quadratic Taylor polynomial
steps.text: This is a literal algebraic definition. Its use as a small error requires differentiability; the definition itself is total for every f.
steps.lean:
noncomputable def secondOrderRemainder (f : E → F) (x v : E) : F :=
  f (x + v) - f x - fderiv ℝ f x v - (1 / 2 : ℝ) • fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ f) x v v

units.boundary: This definition alone gives no estimate. Lean uses its total Fréchet-derivative convention when differentiability is absent.

units.title: A Hessian oscillation bound controls the Taylor residual
units.statement: If f is C² at every point of the segment from x to x+v and its Hessian differs there from D²f(x) in operator norm by at most ε, then the Taylor residual has norm at most ε‖v‖².
assumptions: Let E and F be real normed vector spaces. Derivatives are real Fréchet derivatives; D²f(x) is viewed as a continuous bilinear map.
For every t∈[0,1], f is C² at x+tv and ‖D²f(x+tv)−D²f(x)‖≤ε. The constant ε is real; these assumptions imply ε≥0.

steps.title: Differentiate along the segment
steps.text: After subtracting the first derivative and the Hessian at x, the derivative of the first-order error is exactly the Hessian variation applied twice to v.
steps.lean:
let line (t : ℝ) := x + t • v
  let H := fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ f)
  let a := fderiv ℝ f x v
  let b := H x v v
  let D (t : ℝ) := fderiv ℝ f (line t) v - a - t • b
  let R (t : ℝ) := f (line t) - f x - t • a - (t ^ 2 / 2) • b
  let C := ε * ‖v‖ ^ 2
  have hzero : (0 : ℝ) ∈ Icc 0 1 := left_mem_Icc.2 zero_le_one
  have hε : 0 ≤ ε := (norm_nonneg (H (line 0) - H x)).trans (hvar 0 hzero)
  have hC : 0 ≤ C := mul_nonneg hε (sq_nonneg _)
  have hline (t : ℝ) : HasDerivAt line v t := by
    simpa [line] using ((hasDerivAt_id t).smul_const v).const_add x
  have hD' (t : ℝ) (ht : t ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 1) :
      HasDerivAt D ((H (line t) - H x) v v) t := by
    have hh : DifferentiableAt ℝ (fderiv ℝ f) (line t) :=
      ((hf t ht).fderiv_right (m := 1) (by norm_num)).differentiableAt one_ne_zero
    have hd : HasDerivAt (fun r => fderiv ℝ f (line r)) (H (line t) v) t :=
      hh.hasFDerivAt.comp_hasDerivAt t (hline t)
    have hvalue : HasDerivAt (fun r => fderiv ℝ f (line r) v) (H (line t) v v) t :=
      (ContinuousLinearMap.apply ℝ F v).hasFDerivAt.comp_hasDerivAt t hd
    simpa only [D, b, sub_apply, id_eq, one_smul] using
      (hvalue.sub_const a).fun_sub ((hasDerivAt_id t).smul_const b)

steps.title: Bound the first-order error
steps.text: The operator-norm bound controls D′. Since D(0)=0, the mean-value inequality on the unit interval bounds D by the same constant.
steps.lean:
have hH (t : ℝ) (ht : t ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 1) : ‖(H (line t) - H x) v v‖ ≤ C := by
    calc
      _ ≤ ‖(H (line t) - H x) v‖ * ‖v‖ := ((H (line t) - H x) v).le_opNorm v
      _ ≤ (‖H (line t) - H x‖ * ‖v‖) * ‖v‖ :=
        mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right ((H (line t) - H x).le_opNorm v) (norm_nonneg v)
      _ ≤ C := by
        rw [mul_assoc, ← pow_two]
        exact mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right (hvar t ht) (sq_nonneg _)
  have hD0 : D 0 = 0 := by simp [D, line, a]
  have hD (t : ℝ) (ht : t ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 1) : ‖D t‖ ≤ C := by
    have h := norm_image_sub_le_of_norm_deriv_le_segment'
      (fun r hr => (hD' r hr).hasDerivWithinAt)
      (fun r hr => hH r (Ico_subset_Icc_self hr)) t ht
    rw [hD0, sub_zero, sub_zero] at h
    exact h.trans (mul_le_of_le_one_right hC ht.2)

steps.title: Apply the mean-value inequality a second time
steps.text: The residual along the segment has derivative D and starts at zero. Evaluating its bound at t=1 gives the conclusion.
steps.lean:
have hR' (t : ℝ) (ht : t ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 1) : HasDerivAt R (D t) t := by
    have hg : HasDerivAt (fun r => f (line r)) (fderiv ℝ f (line t) v) t :=
      ((hf t ht).differentiableAt (by norm_num)).hasFDerivAt.comp_hasDerivAt t (hline t)
    have hquad : HasDerivAt (fun r : ℝ => r ^ 2 / 2) t t := by
      have hp : HasDerivAt (fun r : ℝ => r ^ 2) (2 * t) t := by
        simpa [id] using (hasDerivAt_id t).fun_pow 2
      simpa only [show 2 * t / 2 = t by ring] using hp.div_const 2
    simpa only [R, D, id_eq, one_smul] using
      ((hg.sub_const (f x)).fun_sub ((hasDerivAt_id t).smul_const a)).fun_sub (hquad.smul_const b)
  have h := norm_image_sub_le_of_norm_deriv_le_segment_01'
    (fun t ht => (hR' t ht).hasDerivWithinAt) (fun t ht => hD t (Ico_subset_Icc_self ht))
  simpa [R, line, a, b, H, C, secondOrderRemainder] using h

units.title: A uniform Taylor residual estimate on a compact set
units.statement: For every ε>0, there is one radius δ>0 that controls the second-order residual for every starting point x in K and every increment with norm less than δ.
assumptions: Let E and F be real normed vector spaces. Derivatives are real Fréchet derivatives; D²f(x) is viewed as a continuous bilinear map.
E is locally compact, K⊆E is compact, and f is C² at every point of K. The set K may be empty.

steps.title: Choose a compact neighborhood inside the smooth locus
steps.text: The C² locus is open. Compactness of K and local compactness of E give a compact closed neighborhood of K contained in that locus.
steps.lean:
let U := {x : E | ContDiffAt ℝ 2 f x}
  have hU : IsOpen U := isOpen_iff_mem_nhds.2 fun x hx =>
    (show ContDiffAt ℝ 2 f x from hx).eventually (by norm_num)
  obtain ⟨r, hr, hUsub⟩ := hK.exists_cthickening_subset_open hU hf
  obtain ⟨s, hs, hS⟩ := hK.exists_isCompact_cthickening
  let ρ := min r s
  have hρ : 0 < ρ := lt_min hr hs
  have hT : IsCompact (cthickening ρ K) :=
    hS.of_isClosed_subset isClosed_cthickening (cthickening_mono (min_le_right r s) K)
  have hTsub : cthickening ρ K ⊆ U :=
    (cthickening_mono (min_le_left r s) K).trans hUsub

steps.title: Use uniform continuity of the Hessian
steps.text: The Hessian is continuous on this compact neighborhood, so a single distance threshold bounds its oscillation by ε.
steps.lean:
have hH : ContinuousOn (fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ f)) (cthickening ρ K) := by
    intro x hx
    have h : ContDiffAt ℝ 2 f x := hTsub hx
    exact ((h.fderiv_right (m := 1) (by norm_num)).continuousAt_fderiv one_ne_zero).continuousWithinAt
  have hu : UniformContinuousOn (fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ f)) (cthickening ρ K) :=
    hT.uniformContinuousOn_of_continuous hH
  obtain ⟨δ, hδ, hclose⟩ :=
    (Metric.uniformContinuousOn_iff (f := fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ f))).1 hu ε hε

steps.title: Keep every short segment in the neighborhood
steps.text: Take δ=min(ρ,δ₀). Every x+tv with x∈K, ‖v‖<δ and t∈[0,1] remains in the chosen neighborhood and within δ₀ of x. Apply the preceding segment estimate.
steps.lean:
refine ⟨min ρ δ, lt_min hρ hδ, fun x hx v hv => ?_⟩
  have hxT : x ∈ cthickening ρ K := self_subset_cthickening _ hx
  have hvρ : ‖v‖ < ρ := hv.trans_le (min_le_left _ _)
  have hvδ : ‖v‖ < δ := hv.trans_le (min_le_right _ _)
  have hdist (t : ℝ) (ht : t ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 1) : dist (x + t • v) x ≤ ‖v‖ := by
    rw [dist_eq_norm, add_sub_cancel_left, norm_smul, Real.norm_eq_abs, abs_of_nonneg ht.1]
    exact mul_le_of_le_one_left (norm_nonneg _) ht.2
  have hseg (t : ℝ) (ht : t ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 1) : x + t • v ∈ cthickening ρ K :=
    mem_cthickening_of_dist_le _ x ρ K hx ((hdist t ht).trans hvρ.le)
  apply norm_secondOrderRemainder_le_of_hessian_variation (fun t ht => hTsub (hseg t ht))
  intro t ht
  have h := hclose x hxT (x + t • v) (hseg t ht) (by rw [dist_comm]; exact (hdist t ht).trans_lt hvδ)
  change ‖-fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ f) x + fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ f) (x + t • v)‖ < ε at h
  rw [add_comm, ← sub_eq_add_neg] at h
  exact h.le

units.title: The extrinsic sphere Laplacian expression
units.statement: For a finite coordinate set I, define the following ambient real-valued expression for every f:ℝᴵ→ℝ and w∈ℝᴵ. On the unit sphere and for a C² ambient test this is the usual extrinsic formula for the sphere Laplacian.
assumptions: I is finite with decidable equality, E is Euclidean space ℝᴵ, f:E→ℝ and w∈E. The subtraction |I|−1 is natural-number subtraction before conversion to ℝ.

steps.title: Remove radial second and first derivatives
steps.text: The definition subtracts the radial Hessian and the radial first-derivative correction from the ambient Laplacian.
steps.lean:
noncomputable def sphereLaplacian (f : E → ℝ) (w : E) : ℝ :=
  (Δ f) w - fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ f) w w w -
    ((Fintype.card I - 1 : ℕ) : ℝ) * fderiv ℝ f w w

units.boundary: The definition is total off the sphere and without a smoothness assumption. It is an ambient expression; this declaration does not independently identify an intrinsic Laplace–Beltrami operator.

units.title: The exact mean-square error for predictable Brownian weights
units.statement: Let aᵢ be square-integrable real weights measurable at the left endpoints of a nondecreasing finite deterministic time grid. For Brownian motion B relative to that filtration, the compensated weighted square-increment sum is square-integrable and satisfies the exact identity below.
units.formula: Z=\sum_i a_i\big((B_{t_{i+1}}-B_{t_i})^2-\Delta t_i\big),\qquad \mathbb E Z^2=2\sum_i\mathbb E[a_i^2](\Delta t_i)^2.
assumptions: B is a real Brownian motion with the given filtration and measure; its law implies the measure is a probability measure. There are n≥0 cells with 0≤t₀≤⋯≤tₙ.
For every cell i, aᵢ is strongly measurable with respect to the filtration at tᵢ and belongs to L². Repeated times are allowed.

steps.title: Factor the diagonal second moments
steps.text: The compensated square of one increment has mean zero and second moment 2(Δt)². It is independent of every left-endpoint measurable weight. This also proves L² integrability of each weighted term.
steps.lean:
let _ : IsProbabilityMeasure mu := hB.isProbabilityMeasure
  let Z : Fin n → Omega → ℝ := fun i => centeredSquaredIncrement B times i
  let W : Fin n → Omega → ℝ := fun i omega => weight i omega * Z i omega
  have hPre := hB.isBrownian.toIsPreBrownianReal
  have hZ (i : Fin n) : MemLp (Z i) 2 mu :=
    centered_cell_memLp_two hPre _ _
  have hZMeas (i : Fin n) : StronglyMeasurable[filtration (times i.succ)] (Z i) := by
    have hs := (hB.stronglyAdapted (times i.castSucc)).mono
      (filtration.mono (hmono (Fin.castSucc_le_succ i)))
    exact (((hB.stronglyAdapted (times i.succ)).sub hs).pow 2).sub stronglyMeasurable_const
  have hInd (i : Fin n) (X : Omega → ℝ)
      (hX : StronglyMeasurable[filtration (times i.castSucc)] X) : IndepFun X (Z i) mu := by
    have hi := hB.indepFun_increment_of_stronglyMeasurable (hmono (Fin.castSucc_le_succ i)) hX
    exact hi.comp (φ := id)
      (ψ := fun x : ℝ => x^2 - ((times i.succ - times i.castSucc : ℝ≥0) : ℝ))
      measurable_id (by fun_prop)
  have hIndSq (i : Fin n) : IndepFun (fun omega => (weight i omega)^2)
      (fun omega => (Z i omega)^2) mu :=
    (hInd i (weight i) (hAdapted i)).comp
      (φ := fun x : ℝ => x^2) (ψ := fun x : ℝ => x^2) (by fun_prop) (by fun_prop)
  have hW (i : Fin n) : MemLp (W i) 2 mu := by
    have hMeas : AEStronglyMeasurable (W i) mu :=
      (hWeight i).aestronglyMeasurable.mul (hZ i).aestronglyMeasurable
    apply (memLp_two_iff_integrable_sq hMeas).2
    simpa only [W, mul_pow, Pi.mul_def] using
      (hIndSq i).integrable_mul (hWeight i).integrable_sq (hZ i).integrable_sq

steps.title: Eliminate the off-diagonal terms
steps.text: For i<j, the earlier weighted increment and the j-th weight are measurable at tⱼ. The j-th centered increment is independent of their product and has mean zero.
steps.lean:
have hOrdered {i j : Fin n} (hij : i < j) :
      (∫ omega, W i omega * W j omega ∂mu) = 0 := by
    have hend : times i.succ ≤ times j.castSucc := hmono (Fin.le_iff_val_le_val.mpr (by
      have h : i.val < j.val := hij
      simpa using h))
    let past : Omega → ℝ := fun omega => W i omega * weight j omega
    have hpast : StronglyMeasurable[filtration (times j.castSucc)] past := by
      have hw := (hAdapted i).mono
        (filtration.mono ((hmono (Fin.castSucc_le_succ i)).trans hend))
      have hz := (hZMeas i).mono (filtration.mono hend)
      exact (hw.mul hz).mul (hAdapted j)
    have hprod := (hInd j past hpast).integral_fun_mul_eq_mul_integral
      (hpast.mono (filtration.le _)).aestronglyMeasurable (hZ j).aestronglyMeasurable
    have hmean : (∫ omega, Z j omega ∂mu) = 0 :=
      BrownianQuadraticVariation.integral_centered_increment_sq_eq_zero hB (hmono (Fin.castSucc_le_succ j))
    calc
      (∫ omega, W i omega * W j omega ∂mu) =
          ∫ omega, past omega * Z j omega ∂mu := by
        apply integral_congr_ae
        filter_upwards [] with omega
        simp only [past,W]
        ring
      _ = 0 := by rw [hprod, hmean, mul_zero]
  have hCross {i j : Fin n} (hij : i ≠ j) :
      (∫ omega, W i omega * W j omega ∂mu) = 0 := by
    rcases lt_or_gt_of_ne hij with h | h
    · exact hOrdered h
    · simpa only [mul_comm] using hOrdered h

steps.title: Expand the square and retain only the diagonal
steps.text: Each product is integrable by the L² bounds. Interchange finite sums and integrals, cancel the cross terms and substitute the diagonal moments.
steps.lean:
have hDiag (i : Fin n) : (∫ omega, (W i omega)^2 ∂mu) =
      (∫ omega, (weight i omega)^2 ∂mu) *
        (2 * (((times i.succ - times i.castSucc : ℝ≥0) : ℝ)^2)) := by
    simp only [W, mul_pow]
    rw [(hIndSq i).integral_fun_mul_eq_mul_integral
      ((hWeight i).aestronglyMeasurable.pow 2) ((hZ i).aestronglyMeasurable.pow 2)]
    rw [show (∫ omega, (Z i omega)^2 ∂mu) =
        2 * (((times i.succ - times i.castSucc : ℝ≥0) : ℝ)^2) from
      integral_centered_cell_sq hPre (hmono (Fin.castSucc_le_succ i))]
  have hPair (i j : Fin n) : Integrable (fun omega => W i omega * W j omega) mu :=
    (hW i).integrable_mul (hW j)
  intro error
  refine ⟨memLp_finsetSum Finset.univ (fun i _ => hW i), ?_⟩
  calc
    (∫ omega, (error omega)^2 ∂mu) =
        ∫ omega, ∑ i, ∑ j, W i omega * W j omega ∂mu := by
      simp only [error, W, Z, pow_two, Finset.sum_mul_sum]
    _ = ∑ i, ∑ j, ∫ omega, W i omega * W j omega ∂mu := by
      rw [integral_finsetSum]
      · apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
        intro i _
        rw [integral_finsetSum]
        intro j _
        exact hPair i j
      · intro i _
        exact integrable_finsetSum _ fun j _ => hPair i j
    _ = ∑ i, ∫ omega, (W i omega)^2 ∂mu := by
      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
      intro i _
      rw [Finset.sum_eq_single i]
      · simp only [pow_two]
      · intro j _ hji
        exact hCross hji.symm
      · simp
    _ = _ := Finset.sum_congr rfl fun i _ => hDiag i

units.boundary: Weights need no almost-sure uniform bound. They may be dependent across cells; the required condition is left-endpoint measurability and a finite second moment.

units.title: Dyadic predictable Brownian square errors vanish in mean square
units.statement: For the dyadic grids on [0,T], suppose all predictable weights have second moments bounded by one constant C, uniformly over levels and cells. Their compensated weighted square-increment sums tend to zero in mean square.
assumptions: B is a real Brownian motion with the given filtration and measure. The horizon T is any nonnegative real.
At every level n and cell i, the real weight is strongly measurable at time iT/2ⁿ and is in L². A real C satisfies E[aₙ,ᵢ²]≤C for every n,i.

steps.title: Apply the exact finite-grid identity
steps.text: Bound each diagonal weight moment by C and sum the equal cell lengths.
steps.lean:
have hUpper (level : ℕ) :
      (∫ omega, (∑ i, weight level i omega * centeredSquaredIncrement B
          (regularGridTimes (dyadicMesh T level) (2 ^ level)) i omega)^2 ∂mu) ≤
        (2 * C) * ((T : ℝ) * (dyadicMesh T level : ℝ)) := by
    let times := regularGridTimes (dyadicMesh T level) (2 ^ level)
    rw [(predictable_weighted_quadraticVariationError_L2 hB
      (regularGridTimes_monotone (dyadicMesh T level) (2 ^ level))
      (weight level) (hAdapted level) (hWeight level)).2]
    calc
      _ ≤ ∑ i : Fin (2 ^ level), C *
          (2 * (((times i.succ - times i.castSucc : ℝ≥0) : ℝ)^2)) :=
        Finset.sum_le_sum fun i _ => mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right (hC level i) (by positivity)
      _ = ∑ i : Fin (2 ^ level), (2 * C) *
          (((times i.succ - times i.castSucc : ℝ≥0) : ℝ)^2) :=
        Finset.sum_congr rfl fun i _ => by ring
      _ = _ := by
        rw [← Finset.mul_sum, show (∑ i : Fin (2 ^ level),
          (((times i.succ - times i.castSucc : ℝ≥0) : ℝ)^2)) =
            (T : ℝ) * (dyadicMesh T level : ℝ) from sum_dyadic_cellLengths_sq T level]

steps.title: Let the mesh tend to zero
steps.text: The upper bound tends to zero and the integrand is nonnegative, so the squeeze theorem gives the limit.
steps.lean:
have hLimit := ((FiniteTimeGrid.dyadicMesh_tendsto_zero T).const_mul (T : ℝ)).const_mul (2 * C)
  refine tendsto_const_nhds.squeeze ?_ (fun level => integral_nonneg fun _ => sq_nonneg _) hUpper
  simpa using hLimit

units.boundary: This is mean-square convergence of a centered error, not an almost-sure convergence assertion. It includes T=0.

units.title: Choose a representative with values in a specified set
units.statement: Define r:E→K by keeping each point already in K and replacing every point outside K by the specified fallback k₀.
assumptions: E is a type, K⊆E, and k₀ is a specified member of K. The result does not assume compactness.

steps.title: Use membership to choose the subtype value
steps.text: The first branch retains x with its membership proof; the second uses the given element of K.
steps.lean:
noncomputable def restrictState (fallback : K) (x : E) : K := by
  classical
  exact
  if hx : x ∈ K then ⟨x, hx⟩ else fallback

units.title: The chosen representative is measurable
units.statement: If E is a measurable space and K is measurable, the map r:E→K is measurable for the induced subtype measurable structure.

steps.title: Express the underlying map as a measurable piecewise map
steps.text: The identity and the constant k₀ are measurable. Their piecewise combination on K is measurable, and the same map lifts to the subtype.
steps.lean:
theorem measurable_restrictState [MeasurableSpace E]
    (hK : MeasurableSet K) (fallback : K) : Measurable (restrictState fallback) := by
  classical
  apply Measurable.subtype_mk

    funext x

  change Measurable (fun x => (restrictState fallback x : E))
  rw [heq]
  exact measurable_id.piecewise hK measurable_const

units.title: Vanishing Taylor residuals on arbitrary fine grids
units.statement: On any compact pseudometric time space, take finite grids whose neighboring time distances vanish uniformly. If the sums of squared state increments converge in measure to a real-valued random variable Q, then the sums of second-order Taylor residuals converge in measure to zero.
assumptions: The sample space Ω carries a finite measure μ. E is a locally compact real normed space with its Borel measurable structure. K⊆E is compact.
f:E→ℝ is C² at every point of K. Each time evaluation of the K-valued process X is measurable. Its paths are continuous on the specified compact time domain for μ-almost every sample.

The time space is compact and pseudometric. Each grid has Nₙ+1 points, and for every δ>0, eventually all neighboring time distances are less than δ. Q:Ω→ℝ is a finite real-valued function. No ordering of the time space is required.

steps.title: Establish measurability of the residual sums
steps.text: The restrictions of f, Df and D²f to K are continuous. Hence the residual as a function of two K-valued endpoints is continuous, and the finite random sums are measurable.
steps.lean:
have : CompactSpace K := isCompact_iff_compactSpace.mp hK
  let Δ (n : ℕ) (i : Fin (N n)) (ω : Ω) :=
    (X (grid n i.succ) ω : E) - (X (grid n i.castSucc) ω : E)
  let A (n : ℕ) (ω : Ω) := ∑ i : Fin (N n), ‖Δ n i ω‖ ^ 2
  let R (n : ℕ) (ω : Ω) := ∑ i : Fin (N n),
    secondOrderRemainder f (X (grid n i.castSucc) ω : E) (Δ n i ω)
  change TendstoInMeasure μ R atTop (fun _ => 0)
  have hA : TendstoInMeasure μ A atTop Q := hQV
  have hfK : Continuous (fun x : K => f (x : E)) := continuous_iff_continuousAt.2 fun x =>
    (hf x x.property).continuousAt.comp continuous_subtype_val.continuousAt
  have hdK : Continuous (fun x : K => fderiv ℝ f (x : E)) :=
    continuous_iff_continuousAt.2 fun x =>
      ((hf x x.property).continuousAt_fderiv (by norm_num)).comp continuous_subtype_val.continuousAt
  have hHK : Continuous (fun x : K => fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ f) (x : E)) :=
    continuous_iff_continuousAt.2 fun x =>
      (((hf x x.property).fderiv_right (m := 1) (by norm_num)).continuousAt_fderiv one_ne_zero).comp
        continuous_subtype_val.continuousAt
  have hdif : Continuous (fun z : K × K => (z.2 : E) - (z.1 : E)) :=
    (continuous_subtype_val.comp continuous_snd).sub (continuous_subtype_val.comp continuous_fst)
  have hR : Continuous (fun z : K × K =>
      secondOrderRemainder f (z.1 : E) ((z.2 : E) - (z.1 : E))) := by
    have h := (((hfK.comp continuous_snd).sub (hfK.comp continuous_fst)).sub
      ((hdK.comp continuous_fst).clm_apply hdif)).sub
        ((continuous_const (y := (1 / 2 : ℝ))).smul
          (((hHK.comp continuous_fst).clm_apply hdif).clm_apply hdif))
    apply h.congr
    intro z
    simp [secondOrderRemainder, Function.comp_def, add_sub_cancel]
  have hRm (n : ℕ) : AEStronglyMeasurable (R n) μ := by
    have h (i : Fin (N n)) : AEStronglyMeasurable
        (fun ω => secondOrderRemainder f (X (grid n i.castSucc) ω : E) (Δ n i ω)) μ :=
      (hR.measurable.comp ((hX (grid n i.castSucc)).prodMk (hX (grid n i.succ)))).aestronglyMeasurable
    apply (Finset.aestronglyMeasurable_sum Finset.univ (fun i _ => h i)).congr
    exact Eventually.of_forall fun ω => by simp only [R, Finset.sum_apply]

steps.title: Extract a pathwise convergent energy subsequence
steps.text: From any subsequence, convergence in measure provides a further subsequence on which the square-increment sum converges almost everywhere. On each such continuous path it is eventually bounded by C=|Q|+1.
steps.lean:
apply (exists_seq_tendstoInMeasure_atTop_iff hRm).2
  intro ns hns
  obtain ⟨ks, hks, hPathEnergy⟩ := (hA.comp hns.tendsto_atTop).exists_seq_tendsto_ae
  refine ⟨ks, hks, ?_⟩
  filter_upwards [hpaths, hPathEnergy] with ω hpath hEnergy
  let C := |Q ω| + 1
  have hC : 0 < C := by dsimp [C]; positivity
  have hQC : Q ω < C := by dsimp [C]; linarith [le_abs_self (Q ω)]
  have hBound : ∀ᶠ n in atTop, A (ns (ks n)) ω ≤ C :=
    ((tendsto_order.1 hEnergy).2 C hQC).mono fun _ hn => hn.le
  rw [Metric.tendsto_nhds]
  intro ε hε
  let a := ε / (2 * C)
  have ha : 0 < a := div_pos hε (mul_pos (by norm_num) hC)

steps.title: Combine small increments with the uniform Taylor estimate
steps.text: Uniform continuity of each path turns the time-mesh condition into small state increments. Apply the compact uniform residual estimate with tolerance ε/(2C). The residual sum is then bounded by ε/2. The subsequence characterization yields convergence in measure.
steps.lean:
obtain ⟨r, hr, hRbound⟩ := exists_uniform_secondOrderRemainder_le_on_compact hK hf ha
  obtain ⟨δ, hδ, hclose⟩ := Metric.uniformContinuous_iff.1
    (CompactSpace.uniformContinuous_of_continuous hpath) r hr
  have hmesh' := (hns.comp hks).tendsto_atTop.eventually (hmesh δ hδ)
  filter_upwards [hBound, hmesh'] with n hnBound hnMesh
  let m := ns (ks n)
  have hstep (i : Fin (N m)) : ‖Δ m i ω‖ < r := by
    have h := hclose (hnMesh i)
    change dist (X (grid m i.succ) ω : E) (X (grid m i.castSucc) ω : E) < r at h
    simpa only [dist_eq_norm, Δ] using h
  change dist (R m ω) (0 : ℝ) < ε
  rw [dist_zero_right]
  calc
    ‖R m ω‖ ≤ ∑ i : Fin (N m),
        ‖secondOrderRemainder f (X (grid m i.castSucc) ω : E) (Δ m i ω)‖ :=
      norm_sum_le _ _
    _ ≤ a * A m ω := by
      change _ ≤ a * ∑ i : Fin (N m), ‖Δ m i ω‖ ^ 2
      rw [Finset.mul_sum]
      exact Finset.sum_le_sum fun i _ =>
        hRbound (X (grid m i.castSucc) ω : E) (X (grid m i.castSucc) ω).property _ (hstep i)
    _ ≤ a * C := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hnBound ha.le
    _ < ε := by
      have h : a * C = ε / 2 := by dsimp [a]; field_simp [hC.ne']
      rw [h]
      exact half_lt_self hε

units.boundary: Convergence of square-increment sums is an explicit input to this reusable lemma; the downstream Itô theorem derives it for its actual process. No rate or almost-sure limit for the full sequence is asserted.

units.title: Vanishing Taylor residuals on a dyadic time grid
units.statement: For a compact-state process on [0,T], the sums of second-order Taylor residuals over the dyadic grids converge in measure to zero whenever the sums of squared increments converge in measure to a real-valued Q.
assumptions: The sample space Ω carries a finite measure μ. E is a locally compact real normed space with its Borel measurable structure. K⊆E is compact.
f:E→ℝ is C² at every point of K. Each time evaluation of the K-valued process X is measurable. Its paths are continuous on the specified compact time domain for μ-almost every sample.
T>0, X is defined at all nonnegative times and has almost-sure continuous paths on [0,T]. The dyadic sums of squared increments converge in measure to Q:Ω→ℝ.

steps.title: Restrict time to the compact interval
steps.text: Every dyadic time lies in [0,T]. Restrict X to this interval, retaining measurable time slices and almost-sure path continuity.
steps.lean:
let times (n : ℕ) := regularGridTimes (dyadicMesh T n) (2 ^ n)
  let S := Icc (0 : ℝ≥0) T
  have : CompactSpace S := isCompact_iff_compactSpace.mp isCompact_Icc
  have htime (n : ℕ) (i : Fin (2 ^ n + 1)) : times n i ≤ T :=
    ((regularGridTimes_strictMono (dyadicMesh_pos hT n) _).monotone (Fin.le_last i)).trans_eq
      (regularDyadic_last_time T n)
  let grid (n : ℕ) (i : Fin (2 ^ n + 1)) : S := ⟨times n i, bot_le, htime n i⟩
  let Y (t : S) := X (t : ℝ≥0)
  have hY (t : S) : Measurable (Y t) := hX t
  have hYpaths : ∀ᵐ ω ∂μ, Continuous (fun t : S => Y t ω) :=
    hpaths.mono fun _ hω => hω.domRestrict

steps.title: Verify the mesh hypothesis and apply the grid theorem
steps.text: Consecutive grid points are exactly T/2ⁿ apart, so their distances tend to zero. All hypotheses of the arbitrary-grid residual theorem now hold.
steps.lean:
have hmesh (δ : ℝ) (hδ : 0 < δ) : ∀ᶠ n in atTop, ∀ i : Fin (2 ^ n),
      dist (grid n i.succ) (grid n i.castSucc) < δ := by
    filter_upwards [eventually_dyadicMesh_lt T hδ] with n hn i
    change dist ((times n i.succ : ℝ≥0) : ℝ) ((times n i.castSucc : ℝ≥0) : ℝ) < δ
    have h := dyadic_activeCell_right (T := T) i
    change times n i.succ = times n i.castSucc + dyadicMesh T n at h
    rw [h, NNReal.coe_add, Real.dist_eq, add_sub_cancel_left, abs_of_nonneg (NNReal.coe_nonneg _)]
    exact hn
  exact tendstoInMeasure_sum_secondOrderRemainder_of_quadraticVariation hK f hf Y hY
    hYpaths (fun n => 2 ^ n) grid hmesh hQV

units.boundary: This theorem transfers an assumed square-increment limit to a Taylor-residual limit; it does not itself prove quadratic variation for a stochastic integral.

units.title: Coordinate quadratic variation controls the vector Taylor residual
units.statement: In a finite-dimensional Euclidean state space, it suffices that the square-increment sum of each coordinate converge in measure to its own real-valued Qⱼ. The vector Taylor residual sum then converges in measure to zero.
assumptions: I is a finite coordinate set, E=ℝᴵ with its Euclidean norm, Ω carries a finite measure μ, and K⊆E is compact.
f:E→ℝ is C² at every point of K. The K-valued process X has measurable evaluations at every nonnegative time and almost-sure continuous paths on [0,T], where T>0.
For each j∈I the dyadic square-increment sum of coordinate j converges in measure to Qⱼ:Ω→ℝ.

steps.title: Sum the coordinate limits
steps.text: Coordinate increments are measurable. A finite simultaneous subsequence argument allows their convergence-in-measure limits to be summed.
steps.lean:
let times (n : ℕ) := regularGridTimes (dyadicMesh T n) (2 ^ n)
  let coord (j : I) (t : ℝ≥0) (ω : Ω) := (X t ω : EuclideanSpace ℝ I) j
  let V (j : I) (n : ℕ) (ω : Ω) := ∑ i : Fin (2 ^ n),
    (coord j (times n i.succ) ω - coord j (times n i.castSucc) ω) ^ 2
  have hcoord (j : I) (t : ℝ≥0) : Measurable (coord j t) :=
    ((EuclideanSpace.proj j).continuous.comp continuous_subtype_val).measurable.comp (hX t)
  have hV (j : I) (n : ℕ) : AEStronglyMeasurable (V j n) μ := by
    have hcell (i : Fin (2 ^ n)) : AEStronglyMeasurable
        (fun ω => (coord j (times n i.succ) ω - coord j (times n i.castSucc) ω) ^ 2) μ :=
      (((hcoord j _).sub (hcoord j _)).pow_const 2).aestronglyMeasurable
    apply (Finset.aestronglyMeasurable_sum Finset.univ (fun i _ => hcell i)).congr
    exact Eventually.of_forall fun ω => by simp only [V, Finset.sum_apply]
  have h := AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.StochasticProcesses.FiniteSumConvergenceInMeasure.tendstoInMeasure_fintype_sum hV (G := Q) hQV

steps.title: Recognize the Euclidean square norm
steps.text: Interchange the two finite sums and use the Euclidean norm identity. This supplies the square-increment hypothesis of the dyadic residual theorem.
steps.lean:
refine tendstoInMeasure_dyadic_sum_secondOrderRemainder hK f hf hT X hX hpaths
    (Q := fun ω => ∑ j, Q j ω) ?_
  apply h.congr_left
  intro n
  filter_upwards [] with ω
